stories.title: 14-year-old steals ₹85 lakh family jewellery for momos:UP's Deoria teen empties wardrobe; shopkeepers exchange gold for feeding him
stories.summary: A bizarre case has emerged from Deoria, Uttar Pradesh, where a 14-year-old boy reportedly stole jewelry worth Rs 85 lakh over three months to feed his obsession with momos. Each day, he took items from the family almirah and handed them to local shopkeepers, who in return gave him momos. The stolen items included gold necklaces, rings, bangles, earrings, and silver anklets, which were given to three shopkeepers. Discovery leaves family shocked The case came to light on Sunday, when the boy’s aunt opened the family almirah to collect some jewelry and found it empty. Shocked, the family questioned the boy, who confessed to giving the items to the shopkeepers in exchange for momos. Following this, the family filed a police complaint against the minor and the three accused shopkeepers. On Monday evening, police registered a case and arrested one of the accused, who is currently being interrogated. The case falls under the Rampur Karkhana police jurisdiction. How the theft happened The victim’s father, Vimlesh Mishra, a temple priest from Bhagwanpur Tiwari village, said his son studies locally. The boy developed a habit of eating momos, which was exploited by three young men running a momo stall at Dumri Chauraha on Deoria–Kasya road. The accused allegedly lured the boy with free momos, persuading him to hand over jewelry from the family almirah daily. List of stolen jewellery The missing items included: The total estimated value of the stolen items is approximately ₹85 lakh. Accused claims jewellery returned One of the accused, Rakesh, claimed that all the jewellery had been returned. He said, “The family is claiming four bangles, but we took only two. We recorded a video of the items and stored them at one location, which was later handed over to the police.” Police action According to Station House Officer Devendra Singh, a case has been registered against the minor and the three shopkeepers—Deepak Kumar, Rakesh, and Pintu. Rakesh has been arrested and is being questioned, while police are actively searching for the other two accused.

stories.title: Rain hits 10 districts in UP, hailstorms in 4 regions:Yogi asks officials to assess damage; 6 fog-related crashes, 15 vehicles collide
stories.summary: The weather in Uttar Pradesh has taken a sudden turn for the worse. In Lucknow and Kanpur, darkness descended during the daytime as drizzle was accompanied by strong, storm-like winds. Hoardings and tin sheds along roads collapsed, and several areas experienced waterlogging. In the early hours of Tuesday, heavy rainfall was recorded in 10 districts, including Auraiya and Jalaun. In Unnao, Chitrakoot, Hardoi, and Etawah, hail fell for about half an hour, covering roads with a white layer of ice. Standing crops in fields were damaged, and residents stayed indoors. Those venturing outside for essential work were seen relying on umbrellas and raincoats. See weather pictures- Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed officials to assess the damage caused by the unseasonal rains. Meanwhile, dense fog has settled over 20 districts, including Aligarh, Mainpuri, and Bulandshahr, reducing visibility in some areas to near zero. Road, rail, and air traffic have been severely affected. Over 25 trains are running late at several railway stations, including Lucknow, while flights at airports are departing with delays. In six districts, including Unnao, 15 vehicles collided due to slippery conditions. In Pilibhit, a truck ran over a farmer. On the Agra Expressway, a bus carrying passengers collided with a truck, leaving several people injured. According to the Meteorological Department, the late-night interaction between a western disturbance and an anticyclone has led to the formation of cloud clusters, resulting in rainfall. Agricultural expert Siddharth Singh stated that the strong winds, rain, and hail have caused damage to wheat and sugarcane crops, while mustard and vegetable crops have also started to rot. Senior scientist from Lucknow, Atul Kumar Singh, said: "The heavy snowfall in Uttarakhand and Nepal is directly affecting the Terai and plains districts of Uttar Pradesh. Due to the impact of a new western disturbance, the drizzle that began in western UP has now spread to Bundelkhand, the Vindhya region, and the Prayagraj division. This weather pattern is expected to continue until February 4. After that, the fog will clear, and temperatures will drop slightly."

stories.title: Trader hoards jewellery worth ₹33 crore in Sambhal:16 kg gold, 8 quintals silver, and diamonds seized; fails to account during 21-hour GST raid
stories.summary: The GST department conducted a major operation in Chandausi on Thursday, seizing undeclared jewellery worth Rs 33 crore from a trader who had allegedly stockpiled goods without bills amid rising gold and silver prices. The Moradabad GST team recovered 16 kg of gold, eight quintals of silver, and diamonds weighing around 34 carats. When the trader failed to produce business records, the team seized the entire stock. After a nearly 21-hour-long raid, the department imposed a penalty of Rs 1.20 crore and confiscated the jewellery. The action triggered protests by local jewellers, who shut shops and staged a sit-in demonstration on Thursday. Education Minister Gulab Devi’s daughter, Dr. Sugandha Singh, a block chief, reached the protest site to meet the traders. BJP city president Ankur Agarwal and former Union Minister of State for the Central Sanitation Commission, Manju Diler, also arrived and held talks with the traders. Following their assurance, the traders called off their protest. Three photos related to the raid Full incident details Montu Jewellers, located in Bada Bazar, Chandausi, is owned by Himanshu Agarwal. Ashok Kumar Singh, Additional Commissioner Grade-1, GST Moradabad Zone, said the department had been monitoring the jeweller’s activities and transactions for about a month. Acting on precise inputs, a 10-member GST team, including three women officers, raided the shop around 1 PM on Wednesday. Local police were also called. The operation continued uninterrupted for 21 hours and was carried out entirely under camera surveillance. During the investigation, the jeweller could account for only 439 grams of gold and 120 kg of silver jewellery in stock. However, officials recovered 16,638 grams of gold, 875 kg of silver jewellery and diamonds weighing 34.43 carats, none of which were recorded in the stock register. The market value of the seized gold, silver and diamond jewellery is estimated at around Rs 33 crore. The merchandise was seized for further investigation. During the operation, employees were not allowed to leave, and no outsider was permitted to enter or exit the premises. Rs 1.20 crore penalty imposed After the probe, a penalty of Rs 1.20 crore was imposed on the jeweller and deposited online. The GST team also seized loose business documents and mobile phone data from the showroom and the jeweller’s residence for further examination. Traders closed market in protest During the raid, traders in Bada Bazaar protested by wearing black bands, closing their shops and sitting on a dharna, raising slogans against GST officials. On Thursday morning, traders again kept the market shut and continued their sit-in protest outside their shops. Trader Rajesh Jindal said inflation had brought jewellery business to a standstill and traders were already under severe stress. ‘This is the fifth or sixth raid in Chandausi. We should not be exploited and must be given proper facilities,’ he said.

stories.title: Wife travelling for husband’s funeral narrowly escapes train accident:Woman trapped between train and platform; RPF jawan rescues her within 3 seconds
stories.summary: An elderly woman narrowly escaped death while boarding a moving train at Kanpur Central Railway Station late Wednesday night. She slipped, and her hand got trapped between the train and the platform, putting her in danger of being pulled under the wheels. The incident occurred around 2 am and was captured on the station’s CCTV cameras. An RPF jawan reacted within seconds and pulled the woman to safety, preventing a major tragedy. The entire rescue operation happened in just three seconds. The elderly woman said- My husband has passed away. I was going to Patna with family to attend his funeral. We had reservation in Magadh Express from Kanpur. The accident was about to happen due to hurry. After the video surfaced, the RPF jawan is being praised. After the incident, the family missed the Magadh Express. They went to Patna by another train. Woman Anwar Jahan lives with her family in Meston Road, Kanpur. Her husband, Iqbal Qureshi, had gone to Patna a few days ago. He passed away there on Wednesday evening. Upon receiving the news, the family was plunged into mourning. Anwar Jahan was going to Patna with her two sons to attend her husband Iqbal Qureshi's funeral. At 2 AM, the Magadh Express departed from Kanpur Central Railway Station platform number 5 for Patna. During this time, Anwar Jahan tried to board the train. While doing so, her foot slipped from the footboard. She fell face-first. Her hand got stuck between the train and the platform. During this time, RPF constable Vinod Yadav, who was on duty, spotted her. Acting quickly, Vinod pulled the woman out immediately. This saved her life. Family departed on another train After the incident, Railway Police Force officers spoke with Anwar Jahan and her sons. They were stopped at the station itself. There was no other train at night. The next train, Brahmaputra Mail, was at 8 AM on Thursday. The family stayed at the station until 8 AM. When the Brahmaputra Mail arrived, the family departed on it. The woman's son, Aamir, said - We were going to Patna to attend Abbu's funeral. My mother's maternal home is there. Abbu (Iqbal Qureshi) had gone to Patna for work. He passed away there. My mother was saved with the help of the police. We have already lost Abbu's support.

stories.title: Send me jail or shoot me, dares suspended PCS officer:Says, 'Not afraid now, if upper caste ministers feel ashamed, then come out from mental slavery’
stories.summary: Suspended PCS officer Alankar Agnihotri said he was no longer afraid of the government, whether it chose to send him to jail or shoot him. “Even if I am jailed, freedom will eventually come after 40 years,” he said. He added that if upper-caste ministers still have any sense of shame, they should break free from what he described as “mental slavery”. He warned that if upper castes do not raise their voice now, the country will not forgive them. Agnihotri further claimed that the introduction of the UGC had amounted to an attack on the soul of the nation. “At present, there is only an illusion of government in the country, and even that is in the minority,” he said. He asserted that if Lok Sabha elections were held today, the BJP would fail to win a single seat. “At the Centre, it is no longer the Bharatiya Janata Party but a Foreign Janata Party,” he remarked. They do not have public support: Suspended PCS Speaking in Shahjahanpur, the suspended City Magistrate alleged that leaders secure election tickets in the name of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and then win by polarising voters on Hindu-Muslim lines. “They do not have real public support of their own,” he said, while adding that leaders like Raja Bhaiya and Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh do enjoy grassroots backing. Drawing a historical parallel, Agnihotri said that just as the East India Company ruled during British times, a “West India Company” was now in control. He alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was acting as the CEO of this entity, with Home Minister Amit Shah as its managing director. He further claimed that political parties were being pressured through agencies such as the ED, CBI and Income Tax Department. 5 major points made by Alankar Agnihotri UGC law criminalises upper-caste students Suspended PCS officer Alankar Agnihotri claimed that protests began across the country after he resigned in protest against the UGC law. He alleged that the policy treats general category students as “self-declared criminals” and institutionalises caste-based discrimination. According to him, the law will lead to increased mental and physical exploitation of general category students, warning that such internal conflict will continue to deepen over time. Clashes in universities will not stop Agnihotri said that clashes have been reported over the past three days at universities in Prayagraj, Varanasi, Ghaziabad and Noida. He warned that such incidents would only increase in the coming days. Accusing the Centre of acting with a divisive mindset, he said the policy was driven by conspiracy. “I do not see this as a BJP government. This is a foreign people’s party,” he remarked. Contracts have become a new route for money laundering Referring to recent public disputes, Agnihotri said that even senior leaders, including the Water Power Minister and Brij Bhushan Rajput, were accusing each other. He alleged that despite claims of 70 per cent work completion, nearly 30 per cent of funds were being siphoned off. “All contracts have now become a new method of money laundering and looting,” he said, adding that even Kalraj Mishra has declared the UGC law unconstitutional. Entire democracy has failed On the question of not accepting the resignation, he said - When one part of the system goes, many questions arise. The question arises that the entire democracy has failed. Then that officer had to resign. Today not a single MP, MLA is standing with us. I haven't come to fight with my own people, but questions need to be asked. Will your conscience awaken after completely destroying the country? Aren't you ashamed? You are public representatives, the voice of the people. An alternative is being rapidly prepared to raise the issues of Brahmin society. Good news will come soon. The general category is suffering, including the OBC class. All people will be invited to the alternative being sought. Will launch Sanatan Swabhiman Yatra from February 7 We are going to take out Sanatan Swabhiman Pad Yatra on February 7. The yatra will start from Hathras at 9 AM for PM residence Delhi. The yatra will reach Delhi on February 12. I appeal to my companions to join the yatra to demand rollback of SC/ST Act, caste reservation, UGC black law and action against IAS Santosh Verma.

stories.title: Chinese manjha kills only son, mother breaks down hugging him:In Lucknow, wife seeing his dead body says, 'Look how smart he still looks'
stories.summary: The funeral of Shoaib, who lost his life due to Chinese manja in Lucknow, was held on Thursday. After seeing the body of her only son, his elderly mother was left inconsolable. His wife repeatedly fainted while crying. When she briefly regained consciousness, the grief-stricken wife could only say, ‘Look at him, he looks so smart, as if he is sleeping. Someone please wake him up.’ Shoaib lived in Sheet Vihar Colony of Dubagga. He died on February 4 after his neck was slashed by Chinese manja. After the post-mortem on Thursday morning, his body was brought home, where a large number of relatives and neighbours had gathered. Shoaib bought house 5 months ago Shoaib is survived by his two daughters. The elder daughter, aged six, kept crying on seeing her father’s body. The younger daughter, just two years old, appeared confused, staring at her father wrapped in a white shroud amid the sudden crowd of mourners. Neighbours said Shoaib had bought a house five months ago and was living there with his family after renovating it. He dreamed of giving his daughters a good education and wanted them to become an officer and a doctor. See photos Wife kept saying, 'he is sleeping, someone wake him up' Shoaib’s body was placed in the outer room on the ground floor of the two-storey house. His wife and mother sat beside him, crying inconsolably. Overwhelmed by grief, the wife kept telling the women around her, ‘He’s just sleeping… someone please wake him up.’ Her repeated words left even those trying to console her in tears. She kept looking at her husband’s body and saying how peaceful and smart he looked, as if he were asleep. Meanwhile, several people gathered around to support Shoaib’s mother, who was struggling to cope with the loss. Father passed away 8 years ago According to brother-in-law Officer Khan, Shoaib's father passed away 8 years ago. There is a 75-year-old elderly mother at home. He has a wife and two children. One daughter is 2 years old. She still plays in the lap. Shoaib was responsible for everyone. He used to make plans regarding this. He often said that he would educate both daughters well... make them good officers, doctors. He was building a house to secure their future. The plan was to rent it out. Call for ban on Chinese kite string after Shoaib’s death Calling for a complete ban on Chinese kite string, Shoaib’s elder brother-in-law, Rehan, said no other woman should be forced to become a widow because of it. He said Shoaib was like a younger brother to him, and his wife, whom he described as being like his own younger sister, lost her husband due to the deadly kite string. Rehan said Shoaib was riding his bike when a Chinese kite string was found hanging on the Haiderganj overbridge. The string was not visible and slit Shoaib’s neck instantly, causing severe bleeding. He collapsed on the spot and writhed in pain. “Who knows how many more sisters will be widowed because of this,” Rehan said, demanding an immediate and complete ban on Chinese kite string. He added that Shoaib was the only son of his family and was loved by everyone in the neighbourhood. He urged the authorities to take strict action and ensure those selling the dangerous string are punished without delay. Crowd of MR colleagues gathered at home Upon hearing the news of Shoaib's death, the staff who worked with him arrived at his house in large numbers. Rahman, who came from Delhi, said that he had been working with Shoaib for a long time. Shoaib was a very helpful person. He used to help everyone. Meanwhile, friend Abhishek said that we have been working together for 2 years. Had never seen such a kind-hearted person. Death by Chinese kite string will now be considered murder in UP CM Yogi got angry at officers over deaths caused by Chinese kite string. He asked officers how the string is still being sold in markets despite the ban. He ordered immediate stop to this. He sternly said, ‘Now deaths from Chinese kite string will be considered murder. Police chiefs were directed to conduct district-wise raids.’

stories.title: Woman shot dead by brother over financial dispute in Agra:Younger sister says, 'He is a thug, I would shoot him if I could'
stories.summary: A brother killed his sister by shooting her in the head. He made an excuse of fixing the electricity to get the door open late at night. As soon as the door opened, he fired with a pistol. The woman died on the spot after being shot. After the murder, the accused fled with his two friends. This incident happened late Wednesday night in Arjun Nagar of the Shahganj police station area. The accused has been identified as Hari Singh. According to police, there had been a long-running dispute between the brother and sister over money matters. Harisingh, a resident of Tajganj, works as an electrician. About four years ago, he went to jail in a case. It is being told that before going to jail, he had given some money and jewelry to his elder sister Anita. After getting out of jail, Harisingh asked his sister for jewelry and money. The sister said that a lot of money was spent on his bail. She used the money kept with her and sold the jewelry to get him bailed out. The brother got angry with sister's response. There was a lot of fighting between them. Since then, there have been daily fights between them over jewelry and money. According to neighbors and relatives, there were several disputes between the brother and sister, and he made life-threatening attacks on his sister. Door opened on pretext of fixing light Deceased Anita Sahu's husband, Shyam, said - On Wednesday night around 8 PM, Hari Singh and his two friends came to my house. They knocked on the door, saying - Your light is broken. Please open the door. Nephew Dev opened the door. After opening the door, one put a gun on my sister's head and another on me. The third shot my wife. The bullet went through my wife's head. My brother-in-law kept accusing his sister of keeping his jewelry. After shooting, all three fled. Hearing the gunshot, nearby people came running. Police arrived on information and took possession of the body, and sent it for post-mortem. Little sister said - If I could, I would shoot him Deceased Anita Kushwaha's sister Rajshree said - My brother Hari has a criminal mind. The family has nothing to do with him. We have ended our relationship with him. He has even attacked his mother. If I could, I would shoot him. Younger sister Manju said - The one who killed my sister is a thug and dacoit. Sister had gotten him out of jail. The jewelry was sold for his bail expenses. But, he used to say that the jewelry wasn't sold, so you have kept it. That's why he maintained enmity. DCP City Ali Abbas said - There was an ongoing dispute between sister and brother regarding financial transactions. Because of this, the brother killed his sister by shooting her. Police are searching for the accused.

stories.title: If we cannot live Korean culture, death is better, papa:Ghaziabad sisters’ suicide note reveals 16 choices personal struggles
stories.summary: You want to take Korean culture away from us. It was our life. The talks of marriage created deep tension in our hearts. Our preference and love was Korean culture. How can we marry an Indian man? No, no, no… if it comes to that, death feels better to us. These lines were written in the suicide note left behind by three sisters who died by suicide in Ghaziabad. In the note, the sisters also listed 16 personal preferences and wrote that it should now be clear that Korean culture was their life. They stated that they were willing to give up their lives for it. According to the police, the three sisters considered themselves Korean rather than Indian and had even adopted Korean names. On the night of February 3, at around 2 am, they jumped from the ninth floor of their residential building, ending their lives. Police recovered diary reveals 18-page suicide note Police recovered a diary from the room, which contained an 18-page suicide note written by the sisters before their deaths. The contents of the diary were later shared by the police with Dainik Bhaskar. The diary reveals details about the sisters’ lives and how deeply Korean culture had become part of their daily routine, including what they described as “Korean love games”. The diary pages offer insight into their mindset and emotional state in the days leading up to the incident. ‘See how deeply we loved Korean culture — now you have seen everything’ In the diary, the sisters wrote repeatedly: “We love Korean, love, love, love… sorry.” They urged readers to read the entire diary, saying everything written in it was true. The note also contained an apology addressed to their father. They wrote that attempts to make them give up Korean culture caused them deep pain, stating that Korean culture was their life. The sisters questioned how anyone could try to separate them from what they described as their identity, saying their family did not understand the depth of their attachment. In the diary, the sisters said it should now be clear that Korean culture and K-pop were central to their lives. They claimed their attachment to Korean culture and K-pop was stronger than their bond with family members. The note further mentioned that apart from Korean culture, there were 16 other things they loved more than their own lives, all of which were listed in the diary. 'Papa, you should have said that we were right, but you didn’t' In the diary, the sisters wrote that they loved Korean culture more than anything else. They described Korean culture and K-pop as their first loves and said they wanted to fully embrace them, but felt they were never given the opportunity to do so. They wrote that when their interest in K-pop and Korean culture became known at home, they believed it was their future. However, they felt there was no discussion or assurance about the future of all three sisters. The note says they expected a simple acknowledgment — “Okay, beta” — but when that did not come, it caused them deep emotional pain. They wrote that this moment led them to take a final decision and view the situation as an enemy in their lives. The sisters also questioned their place in the family, writing: ‘Should we live in this world just to be a burden to you? No’ They said they had lost hope in themselves and believed death was a better option. The note ends with an apology addressed to their father. Know full matter On the night of February 3, three minor sisters — Nishika (16), Prachi (14) and Pakhi (12) — died by suicide after jumping from the balcony of a ninth-floor apartment in Ghaziabad. According to the police, at around 2 am on Tuesday, the sisters locked themselves inside their room, placed a stool near the balcony and jumped one after the other. Father had scolded the girls and taken away their mobile phones Initially, the father told the police that his daughters had died while completing tasks related to a Korean game. However, after nearly 10 hours of investigation, the police found that the father had scolded the girls and taken away their mobile phones shortly before the incident. Investigators believe this led the sisters to take the extreme step. The girls’ father, Chetan, works in share trading. The police also revealed that the sisters had stopped attending school during the Covid period. The incident took place at Flat No. 907 in Bharat City’s B-1 Tower.

stories.title: Kanpur zoo turns digital on its 52nd anniversary:Enables remote animal viewing, live streaming and virtual safaris for all visitors natinowide
stories.summary: Kanpur Zoo has completed 52 years. On this occasion, the zoo administration is moving towards a digital transformation. Counted among the most popular zoos in north India, the Kanpur Zoological Park is now ready to adopt a fully digital avatar. Soon, visitors will not have to stand in long queues or wait under the scorching sun to see animals, as the zoo will be just a click away. People will be able to sit comfortably on their sofas at home and watch the king of the jungle, the lion, roar. Bears and langurs can also be seen playing live. In the coming days, Kanpur Zoo will become a blend of technology and nature, where the distance between humans and wildlife will be reduced through digital platforms. This initiative will not only boost tourism but will also place Kanpur Zoo among the country’s select smart zoos. Wildlife live streaming to be available on the website In an exclusive interaction with Dainik Bhaskar, Kanpur Zoo Director Dr Kanhaiya Patel shared details of this major transformation. The zoo department is preparing to fully shift to online mode. As part of this plan, the official website of the zoo is being upgraded with modern, high-tech features. After the update, people will be able to watch live activities of fierce and rare animals such as lions, cheetahs, bears and rhinoceroses from their homes. This will be especially beneficial for those who cannot visit the zoo due to time constraints or health issues. Movements inside the enclosures will be live-streamed directly on mobile phones and laptops. An option for those who want to avoid crowds During festivals and holidays, heavy crowds are often seen outside the ticket counters at Kanpur Zoo. Many visitors get exhausted after standing in queues for hours. To address this issue, Dr Patel said the ticket booking process is being made completely online. Visitors will be able to book tickets from home at their convenience and gain direct entry. To promote digital payments, the zoo administration has already introduced QR code-based payments, improving transparency and saving visitors’ time. Updates on every new animal arrival The new website will not just be a source of entertainment but also a centre of information. Whenever a new animal arrives at the zoo or a new member is born, the update will be immediately shared on the website. Visitors will be able to know which new animal has arrived and its special characteristics. For wildlife enthusiasts who want detailed information, a digital library will be available featuring the history and habits of each animal. This will give children and nature lovers a new opportunity to connect with wildlife. Kanpur Zoo’s transformation to be completed in two months The administration aims to make the entire system transparent and user-friendly within the next two months. According to Director Dr Kanhaiya Patel, this transparent system will not only benefit visitors but will also help improve wildlife monitoring. Zoo celebrates 52nd birthday with children A day earlier, Kanpur Zoo (Kanpur Prani Udyan) completed 52 years. The zoo was first opened to the public on February 4, 1974. Since then, it has been not only a home for wildlife but also an important part of childhood memories for generations of Kanpur residents. Children enjoy the celebration, Noor Alam becomes ‘guest of honour’ To make the 52nd anniversary special, the zoo administration organised a unique initiative on Wednesday. Fifty-two children, equal to the zoo’s age, were given free entry. The first name on the list was nine-year-old Noor Alam, whose excitement reflected the festive atmosphere. The highlight of the celebration was the cake-cutting ceremony. The cake was cut in the presence of Zoo Director Dr Kanhaiya Patel and Divya (Divisional Director). Forest department officials, including Regional Forest Officer Naved Ikram, Firoz Khan, and wildlife doctors Dr Mohammad Nasir and Nitesh Katiyar, were present and appeared enthusiastic. All of them pledged to further improve this green heritage. Kanpur Zoo is not just a place to see animals but a small forest located in the heart of the city. The atmosphere on the day was festive, with colourful balloons, children’s laughter and animals in their natural rhythm, making the celebration truly memorable.

stories.title: 3 sisters suffer brain haemorrhage after jumping from 9th floor:Postmortem confirms cause of death; family performs last rites in Delhi at midnight
stories.summary: The postmortem report of three sisters who died after jumping from a building in Ghaziabad has confirmed brain haemorrhage as the cause of death. Doctors said the girls suffered severe head injuries after falling from the ninth floor, around 85 feet high, which led to internal bleeding in the brain. The postmortem examination continued till around 8:30 pm on Wednesday in Ghaziabad. A team of three doctors conducted the procedure for nearly two-and-a-half hours. After the postmortem, police handed over the bodies to the family. The family later took the bodies to Delhi, where the last rites were performed at Nigambodh Ghat around midnight. Police have also recovered a note from the scene. According to officials, it contains a message apologising to the father and refers to distress caused by strict discipline at home. The contents are being examined as part of the investigation. DCP Nimish Patil said- So far, the family has not filed any complaint in the case. Police conducted post-mortem of the bodies based on information received on Dial 112. Investigation revealed it to be suicide. However, it is still not clear which girl jumped first. Father says he was at fault The girls’ father, Chetan, said he considers himself responsible for the incident and admitted negligence in paying attention to his daughters. He said the girls were influenced by Korean personalities and appealed to the government to ban Korean videos, serials and games, claiming such content has a negative impact on children. He said no other family should suffer what his has endured. Now know the complete case- Police are investigating 5 questions in the suicide case- Question 1. The balcony from where the girls jumped did not have enough space to stand outside the railing, while a resident from the opposite flat claimed one girl was seen sitting on the railing. Question 2. The height of the ninth floor from where the three jumped is about 85 feet. Of the three girls' bodies, one was found about 1 foot away from the wall, the second sister's body was 8 feet away, and the third girl's body was found 9 feet away. A body falling so close to the wall from such a height raises suspicion. Question 3. If all three girls jumped together while sitting, then their bodies should have fallen in the same direction. Question 4. According to neighbors, Chetan's both wives are sisters. There was a family dispute before the incident. The wives were using abusive language? They were pointing towards the husband. Question 5. On condition of anonymity, a police officer said - both wives did not come in front of the Police Commissioner, locked the door from inside, the husband was seen extending his hand to touch an officer's feet, then kept crying loudly.

stories.title: Youth marries minor girl forcibly and rapes her:Victim held captive for 3 days, raped, assaulted; tells family about ordeal after escape
stories.summary: The case came to light from the Saadatganj police station area, involving abduction, forced marriage, and sexual assault of a minor girl. The accused, identified as Mohammad Yusuf, allegedly lured the girl, took her with him, and forced her into a Hindu marriage ritual at a temple. He then kept her as his wife and continued to sexually assault her during this period. Three days ago, the girl somehow escaped from the accused’s custody and reached home. On Wednesday, her mother filed a report against Yusuf at Saadatganj police station, following which the police took him into custody. Identification at Hathi Park According to the family, the girl had discontinued her studies after her father’s death. About two months ago, she had gone to Hathi Park with her mother, where she met Yusuf. He took her mobile number and started communicating with her over phone calls. In December, the accused called the girl under the pretext of meeting her and lured her away. On December 13, he forcibly married her in a temple. When the family protested, he threatened to kill them. Threats to the family Following the family’s objections, Yusuf continued to threaten them with death. He then took the girl to Lakdmundi, where he committed further crimes and assaulted her when she resisted. Three days ago, while she was traveling to the market on a bike with him, some men in a car intercepted Yusuf. The girl took the opportunity to return home. Inspector Santosh Arya of Saadatganj police station said that Yusuf had earlier been taken by the STF in connection with another case and was released after questioning. A case has been registered against him under various sections, including rape and the POCSO Act

stories.title: When will UP celebrate Holi... on March 3 or 4?:Bhadra lunar eclipse cast doubt on celebration date; astrologers advise against playing colours
stories.summary: The festival of Holi this year coincides with an unusual alignment of Bhadra Kaal and a total lunar eclipse, prompting astrologers and religious scholars to advise changes in the traditional schedule of celebrations. According to astrologers, Holika Dahan will be performed on March 2, while Holi (Dhulendi) will not be observed on March 3 due to the presence of a lunar eclipse and the associated Sutak period. As per prevailing religious conventions, Holi celebrations are expected to shift to March 4. Limited window for Holika Dahan Pandit Narendra Upadhyay, an astrologer based in Gorakhpur, said that on March 2, Purnima tithi begins at 5:18 p.m. and continues until the following afternoon. However, Bhadra Kaal will remain in effect from 5:18 p.m. on March 2 until 4:56 a.m. on March 3, covering most of the night traditionally reserved for Holika Dahan. Scriptural texts discourage the performance of auspicious rituals during Bhadra, except during its tail period, which is considered permissible. This year, the tail-end of Bhadra falls between 12:50 a.m. and 2:02 a.m., providing an auspicious window of one hour and twelve minutes for Holika Dahan. Those unable to perform the ritual during this period may do so after Bhadra ends and before sunrise on March 3. However, scholars note that this is not considered ideal under traditional norms. Lunar eclipse on March 3 A total lunar eclipse will occur on the evening of March 3, 2026. According to Prof. Vinay Pandey, an astrologer at Banaras Hindu University, the Sutak period will begin approximately nine hours before the eclipse, around 6:30 a.m. During Sutak, religious practices generally restrict auspicious activities, public celebrations, and temple rituals. Since Holi involves social gatherings and community participation, it is not traditionally observed during this period. The eclipse will be visible after sunset and will conclude around 6:48 p.m. Although the astronomical phase of the eclipse begins earlier in the afternoon, religious observance considers only the period when the moon is visible. Impact on Holi celebrations Given the restrictions associated with Sutak, religious scholars have advised against celebrating Holi on March 3. As a result, Holi is expected to be observed on March 4, a day after the eclipse concludes. Extended celebrations in Braj region While Holi is generally a two-day festival across much of India, celebrations in the Braj region, including Mathura and Vrindavan, extend over several weeks. Festivities there traditionally begin with Basant Panchami and include various local forms of Holi observed in different towns and villages. In 2025, Holi was celebrated on March 14, with Holika Dahan on March 13. Although a lunar eclipse occurred on Holi that year, it was not visible in India and did not affect celebrations.

stories.title: UP govt to treat Chinese manjha deaths as murder:Yogi pulls up officers, asks how banned thread is selling; 8 deaths reported in 1 year in Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: CM Yogi Adityanath has expressed strong anger over deaths caused by Chinese manjha. He questioned officials on how the string is still being sold in markets despite the ban and ordered an immediate stop. In a stern tone, he said deaths caused by Chinese manjha will now be treated as murder. Police chiefs were directed to conduct district-wise raids. Despite the ban, Chinese manjha continues to be sold openly in Uttar Pradesh. In the past one year, eight people have lost their lives. On Wednesday, an MR in Lucknow had his throat slit, leading to a painful death. What did Yogi say? Yogi said that if anyone dies due to Chinese manjha, a murder case will be registered and strict action will be taken against those responsible. An FIR will be lodged and the accused will be sent to jail. UP Police will run an intensive statewide drive to seize Chinese manjha. The CM made it clear that Chinese manjha is banned. Its sale and use will not be tolerated at any cost. Yogi directed police chiefs to identify this illegal network and carry out immediate raids, taking the strictest possible action against the culprits. Recent deaths caused due to Chinese manjha: 1. MR’s throat slit while riding bike in Lucknow On February 4, an MR died in Lucknow after his neck was slit by Chinese manjha. He was riding a bike when the Chinese manjha got entangled around his throat. He fell along with the bike, bleeding heavily, and kept writhing in pain for nearly 10 minutes. Passersby rushed him to the trauma centre, where he died during treatment. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Shoaib (33). The incident took place around 2 pm at the Haiderganj overbridge under the Khala Bazaar police station area. 2. Doctor’s neck slit, dies writhing on road On January 14, a doctor died in Jaunpur after his neck was slit by Chinese manjha. He was returning home on a bike when the Chinese manjha got entangled around his neck and kept cutting into it. The string was so sharp that it cut up to his throat bone. The incident took place around 12.30 pm on Wednesday at Prasad Chowk under the Line Bazaar police station area. The deceased was identified as Dr Sameer Hashmi (28), a resident of Kerakat. Eight deaths caused by Chinese manjha in one year

stories.title: Deoria man stranded in Saudi Arabia for 2 years:Son approaches PMO, MEA and CM’s rally; no relief so far
stories.summary: “My father has been held hostage in Saudi Arabia for the past two years. He is unable to return to India. I have been running from the Prime Minister’s Office to the Home Ministry, Foreign Ministry and the Indian Embassy, but no one has helped,” says Aman Paswan from Deoria. Aman says he even went to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s public meeting as a last hope. “Officials did not let me meet the Chief Minister. I was sent back in 10 seconds. They said the matter would be forwarded to the Ministry of External Affairs,” he said. Aman shared his ordeal with Bhaskar. Father went to Saudi Arabia as driver Aman’s father, Heera Prasad, went to Saudi Arabia to work as a loader truck driver. About two years ago, a minor road accident took place during work. The truck was parked on the roadside when another vehicle hit it lightly. Despite minor damage, local police took Heera Prasad into custody and sent him to jail. He spent 22 days in jail. Trapped due to language barrier Aman said his father does not understand Arabic. After his jail term, people there made him put his thumb impression on a paper written in Arabic. He was told it was a formality for release. Later, the same document was used to impose a fine of 20,000 Riyals. On this basis, he was also barred from returning to India. Since then, his employer has allegedly kept him confined. Aman claims his father is being held hostage by the employer. Embassy did not provide help Aman said the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia has not taken effective steps. “My father keeps calling and asks me to somehow bring him back. The embassy knows the full matter, yet no legal or humanitarian help has been provided,” he said. Visited Delhi three times Aman said he went to Delhi three times seeking help. He first approached the Prime Minister’s Office. From there, he was sent to the Ministry of External Affairs. Later, he was directed to offices near Patiala House. “Everywhere I was told to send emails. After some time, the file status is shown as closed,” he said. Not allowed to meet Chief Minister Aman said he reached Lucknow to attend the Chief Minister’s public meeting with his complaint. Officials initially heard him and asked him to wait. Later, he was given only a few seconds. “They said the matter would be sent to the Ministry of External Affairs and moved on,” he said. ‘Only paperwork, no action’ Aman alleged that all departments are limited to paperwork. “Letters and emails are exchanged, but no officer is taking responsibility. Our family is completely broken,” he said. ‘I may go to Saudi Arabia myself’ Aman said he has two brothers and one sister. He is the youngest. His elder brother works in Gujarat. With his father stuck abroad, the entire family responsibility is on him. “My mother’s health is deteriorating. There is constant stress at home. I see no other option now. I may have to go to Saudi Arabia myself to bring my father back,” Aman said.

stories.title: Female constable commits suicide days before brother-in-law's wedding:Leaves 7-month-old daughter in distress, reason unclear, family shocked
stories.summary: In Hardoi, a female constable committed suicide by hanging. Her body was found hanging in her in-laws’ house. The reasons behind the suicide are not yet known. The constable was posted at Indiranagar police station in Lucknow. She had been on leave for the past five days. Her brother-in-law’s wedding was scheduled for 10 February, and she was at her in-laws’ house to attend the event. The house was bustling with wedding preparations and celebrations when her body was discovered hanging in her room at night. The constable had a love marriage 12 years ago. After several attempts, she had become a mother seven months ago. Police have sent the body for postmortem and begun investigating the case. No suicide note has been recovered so far. The incident occurred in Alu Thok Mohalla under Nagar Kotwali, just one kilometre from the district headquarters. Now, let’s understand the case in detail… Originally from Bareilly, Preeti Singh (34) was a 2021-batch constable. She had a love marriage with Saurabh Srivastava, a resident of Alu Thok Mohalla, Hardoi, 12 years ago. Preeti Singh was posted at Indiranagar police station in Lucknow. She used to live with her husband and daughter at her in-laws’ house in Hardoi and commuted daily to Lucknow. Preeti had been on leave for the past five days. Her brother-in-law Pankaj’s wedding was scheduled for 10 February, and the house was preparing for the celebrations. She completed household chores related to the wedding on Wednesday evening before retiring to her room. Although the wedding preparations were ongoing, Preeti stayed in her room for a long time. Around 9 PM, Pankaj knocked on the door, but it was locked from the inside. Despite repeated calls, there was no response from Preeti. When Pankaj peered through the window, he saw her body hanging from the ceiling fan. Family members broke the door and found her lifeless. On receiving information, CO City Ankit Mishra, along with police personnel and the field unit, arrived at the scene. Police removed the body, prepared the inspection report, and sent it for postmortem. No suicide note was recovered from the scene. Husband distraught, carried inside by police At the time of the incident, Preeti’s husband Saurabh was talking to relatives outside. Upon hearing the news of her death, he collapsed in shock. The police carried him on their shoulders inside the house. Family opposed the love marriage Neighbours stated that 12 years ago, Preeti and Saurabh had married against their family’s wishes. The families had rejected the couple. Since then, Saurabh and Preeti lived in Saurabh’s uncle’s house in Hardoi. Wedding preparations for Pankaj had gradually brought them back into the family’s routines. The police questioned the family but could not ascertain the reason for the suicide. Brother-in-law Pankaj stated that there were no disputes with anyone, and the couple had no conflicts. Police are continuing to question the family regarding the reasons behind the suicide. 7-month-old daughter lost mother's shadow Preeti and Saurabh had their first child just 7 months ago. After much prayer, they had a daughter. Husband Saurabh said - How will I now take care of such a small daughter alone? CO City Ankit Mishra said- The female constable was posted at Indira Nagar police station in Lucknow. The reasons for suicide are not yet clear. Investigation is being conducted from every angle. The situation will become clearer after the post-mortem report arrives.

stories.title: UP shivers in freezing winds, dense fog in 15 districts:Cold to intensify; snowfall, icy winds to push temperatures down to 3°C
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, the weather continues to fluctuate. On Thursday, dense fog returned across the state. Lucknow, Prayagraj and 21 other districts were shrouded in thick fog during the morning, reducing visibility to almost zero. The fog felt like light rain, leaving roads wet. Freezing winds have created near-cold wave conditions. People were seen bundled in warm clothes on the streets, while hands of those riding bikes went numb. Locals tried to keep warm by lighting small fires at several places. Due to the fog, more than 25 trains were running late at Kanpur and other railway stations. The Meteorological Department said that westerly winds in several parts of the state have increased the chill during mornings and evenings. Snowfall is expected in the hilly states from tomorrow, and some areas may also receive rain. These changes will impact the plains, including UP. The speed of freezing winds across the state is expected to rise, which may further lower temperatures. Earlier, on Wednesday, dense fog covered 21 districts including Kanpur and Jhansi. Light drizzle persisted in Prayagraj throughout the day, and clouds remained over most cities. In the past 24 hours, Barabanki recorded the lowest temperature at 6.5°C. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- Except for some parts of Purvanchal, most areas of the state recorded a drop in minimum night temperatures. Maximum temperatures have increased due to sunshine during the day. Cold will increase due to snowfall in the mountains. Minimum temperatures may drop by 2-3C in the next 48 hours. Maximum rainfall in Sambhal Over the past four days of February, Sambhal recorded the most rainfall at 73.9 mm, followed by Meerut at 51.8 mm and Baghpat at 41.3 mm. The changed weather after rain has further intensified the cold. These areas have orange alert for dense fog Kushinagar, Maharajganj, Siddharthnagar, Balrampur, Shravasti, Bahraich, Lakhimpur Kheri, Saharanpur, Bijnor, Moradabad, Rampur, Bareilly, Pilibhit and surrounding areas. Fog will also persist here Banda, Chitrakoot, Kaushambi, Prayagraj, Fatehpur, Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, Chandauli, Varanasi, Bhadohi, Deoria, Gorakhpur, Sant Kabir Nagar, Basti, Gonda, Sitapur, Kanpur Dehat, Kanpur Nagar, Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Baghpat, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Hapur, Agra, Firozabad, Etawah, Auraiya, Amroha, Shahjahanpur, Sambhal, Badaun, Jalaun, Hamirpur, Mahoba, Jhansi, Lalitpur and surrounding areas.

stories.summary: A major commotion broke out on Wednesday morning at Maharana Pratap Engineering College in Kanpur. Students were beaten with sticks and belts by teachers for arriving late. Ten students were injured in the incident, including four girls. One female student suffered a deep cut on her hand. Seeing the blood, other students became furious and created a ruckus. Students blocked the college gate and raised slogans such as “We Want Justice.” Some even caused damage inside the campus. The injured students were admitted to the college’s own hospital for treatment. As the situation escalated, police and PAC personnel were called to the scene. Authorities managed to pacify the students and end their protest. Following a complaint by a student’s father, an FIR has been lodged against three teachers. stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav goes aggressive on UP SIR:Samajwadi Party adopts Mamata like strategy; plans to take on from police to Supreme Court
stories.summary: The ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh has triggered a sharp political confrontation. The Samajwadi Party (SP) has accused the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of collusion, alleging a “planned and organised” effort to delete voters’ names—especially those of Muslims—through fraudulent use of Form 7 (objection to inclusion). SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has taken an unusually aggressive line, comparing his stance to that of Mamata Banerjee and warning of legal escalation, including approaching the Supreme Court. But what is the ground reality? What exactly is SP alleging? SP’s core charges revolve around large-scale misuse of Form 7: Fake, pre-printed forms allegedly filled on computers, carrying forged signatures, incorrect EPIC details, and invalid mobile numbers. Bulk submissions: claims that a single person submitted dozens—sometimes around 100—Form 7s. Specific instances cited: Sarojini Nagar, Lucknow: over 100 forms reportedly bearing the same signature (“Dasharath”). Sultanpur: forms submitted with “Nandlal’s” signatures despite him being illiterate and using thumb impressions. Pressure on officials: SP leaders allege BJP workers pressured Booth Level Officers (BLOs) to accept such forms. Akhilesh Yadav has demanded criminal action, arguing the alleged pattern should be treated as organised crime. Claim of targeted deletions SP leaders contend that Muslim voters are disproportionately affected. Party figures say that in booths with higher Muslim populations, forged Form 7s were filed to trigger deletions. The allegation extends to an organised chain—from party functionaries to mandal-level leaders—tasked with delivering forms to BLOs. Former SP candidate Jayaram Pandey has formally complained about irregularities in Sant Kabir Nagar’s Mehdawal seat, stating that signatories later denied having signed the forms. The district administration says an inquiry is underway and action will follow the findings. Is deleting a voter’s name really that easy? Election administrators and former officials say no. Atiq Ahmad, a former Additional Chief Electoral Officer, explains that Form 7 alone does not delete a name. The process requires: Verification of evidence supporting the objection. Notice to the concerned voter whose deletion is sought. Scrutiny by the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO)—typically an SDM—before any final decision. One Form 7 per person, not bulk submissions by a single individual. He also points to precedents that make officials cautious: What is the Election Commission saying? BJP’s stance The BJP rejects the allegations outright. Party spokespersons argue that: SIR is conducted by the ECI, not by political parties. SP is pre-emptively crying foul, citing its recent electoral setbacks. Claims of conspiracy are framed as anticipating defeat, not evidence-based. Senior journalists and election watchers see a high-stakes political battle layered over a rule-bound administrative process. Akhilesh Yadav’s escalation—press conferences, mobilisation of party workers, and hints of Supreme Court action—signals that SP views SIR as existential. Administratively, however, past precedents and the ECI’s stated safeguards suggest deletions are reversible if wrongdoing is proven, and officials face consequences for arbitrary action. If SP’s evidence of forged forms and coercion holds up, the law provides remedies—FIRs, suspensions, and restoration of names. If not, the ECI’s checks make mass, silent deletions unlikely. The coming weeks—especially inquiry findings—will determine whether this row becomes a legal reckoning or remains a political flashpoint.

stories.title: Ghaziabad sisters’ suicide case:Diary reveals obsession with Korean content; learned language on YouTube, adopted Korean names
stories.summary: In Ghaziabad, three sisters jumped from the ninth floor to commit suicide. Initial reports suggested that they embraced death while completing tasks in a Korean game. However, after just 10 hours of investigation, it was revealed that their father, Chetan, had scolded the children and confiscated their mobile phones. Following this, on the night of February 3, around 2 a.m., the sisters jumped from the balcony. Nishika was 16, Prachi 14, and Pakhi 12. A diary found in their room, along with statements from the family, revealed that the girls considered themselves Korean rather than Indian. They preferred Korean boys, had changed their names, and ran a YouTube channel creating Korean-themed content. With the help of YouTube, the sisters had also learned Korean and often spoke it at home. How the girls came to identify as Korean is explored in the ongoing investigation. During the COVID-19 pandemic, when schools were closed, the girls began watching Korean movies and web series. Nishika was the first to adopt Korean culture, followed by Prachi and Pakhi, who copied her habits. Family members told police that the girls listened to Korean music for hours daily, watched films, web series, and videos, and were so influenced that they began seeing themselves as Korean instead of Indian. They adopted Korean-style clothing, food habits, and mannerisms. Using videos and the internet, they learned the language and communicated with each other in Korean. Eventually, they even told their father that he was Indian while they were Korean. The sisters lived on the ninth floor of their society, where they jumped from the balcony. The three had created a YouTube channel together, posting Korean culture-based content. Nishika had gradually developed an interest in Korean reels on social media in 2022, which then influenced Prachi and Pakhi. Their father had confiscated their phones due to this. The channel had been deleted by the sisters a month before the incident. Nishika studied until class four, Prachi until class three, and Pakhi until class two. Their declining interest in education led them to fail, eventually stopping school entirely. Due to financial difficulties, Chetan did not insist on their studies, planning to re-enroll them when finances improved. Stopped talking to younger sister The sisters also involved their four-year-old younger sibling, trying to show her Korean videos and teach her the language. Their father noticed this and scolded the older sisters, instructing them to keep the younger daughter away. From that day, the three stopped interacting with her. On the night of February 3, the sisters were sleeping in a room with Chetan’s first wife. Around 1:30 a.m., they kissed her cheeks, said “I love you,” and left the room. They placed stools on the balcony and jumped one by one after locking the door from inside. The family had to break it open. Family disputes and prior issues Police investigation revealed that Chetan had suffered a ₹2 crore business loss, causing tension in the household. He had married Hina, the sister of his first wife, and had been living with his third and youngest wife for the past year. A conflict with his first wife in May 2025 had led her to leave, prompting Chetan to file a missing person report, later bringing her back from Delhi. This was the spot from which the sisters jumped. Police sealed the area, and forensic teams collected evidence. In this suicide case, police are seeking answers to 5 questions- Question 1. On the balcony from where the three sisters jumped to commit suicide, there was no space to stand on the railing or outside. However, the resident living in the apartment across said that a girl was sitting on the railing. Question 2. The height from where all three jumped was about 85 feet from the ninth floor. Where the bodies of the three girls fell, one body was found about 1 foot away from the wall, the second sister's body 8 feet away, and the third child's body 9 feet away. A body falling so close to the wall from such a height raises suspicion. Question 3. If all three girls jumped while sitting, then all three bodies should have fallen in the same direction. Question 4. Chetan's both wives are sisters. Why was the wife hurling abusive words at the end of the night? She was pointing towards the husband. Question 5. Both wives didn't come before the Police Commissioner, locked the door from inside, the husband was seen reaching to touch an officer's feet, then kept crying loudly. Scene and diary details The girls lived in a room where old family photos were found on the floor. Most were of their parents. Pencil-written quotes covered the walls of the balcony from which they jumped. One read, “My heart is broken. I am very lonely,” later crossed out. A diary page instructed, “Read this diary. Everything written here is true.” Jump from ninth floor The three sisters, aged approximately 12, 14, and 16, locked themselves in the room, placed stools, and jumped from the balcony one by one. According to their father, they were addicted to task-based Korean love games and spent all their time together, even bathing and using the toilet at the same time. Their addiction was so intense that they had stopped attending school. Media reports said their father had scolded them for playing games, leading them to take this step. Police found an 18-page suicide note in the room apologizing to their parents and expressing their love for the game. The incident occurred at India City B-1 Tower, Flat 907. Additional Police Commissioner Alok Priyadarshi said the girls played games on their mobiles. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the suicide. Evidence of Korean culture on phones Alok Priyadarshi confirmed that the girls’ mobiles contained evidence of Korean cultural influence. They had used different names, and the police are continuing the investigation based on all collected evidence.

stories.title: Prayagraj surrogate womb priced similar to an iPhone:Muslim woman brainwashes to donor, gets eggs removed through surgery at IVF centre
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, a case has emerged in which a 15-year-old girl’s eggs were sold. The “rent-a-womb” (surrogacy) price was an Apple iPhone and Rs 15,000. The mastermind behind the racket is a Muslim woman who brainwashed the girl, Komal (name changed), telling her, “After a small operation, you will get a new life.” The girl told the magistrate that the woman explained the freedoms of Islam and promised, “Once you earn good money, your marriage will be arranged.” According to police, there are indications that eggs may have been extracted from 20–25 underage girls in a year; this will become clear during the investigation. Authorities are now investigating the case from three angles: how many minors were exploited, whether a sex racket is involved, and whether the brainwashing was intended for religious conversion. For now, the girl has been placed in a shelter home. Her medical examination is scheduled for February 5. Victim went missing, later found admitted to IVF centre The case began in Nawabganj, Prayagraj. Shalini (name changed), a widow, lives with her three children. Her eldest daughter, Komal, 15, and her youngest son, Anuj, 5, were under her care. Shalini said that Komal had been in contact with a woman named Joya. She did not know where or how they met. Komal used to leave home in the morning and return only in the evening. When Shalini questioned her, Komal was evasive and rarely gave clear answers. On January 15, Komal suddenly went missing. Attempts to contact her failed, and her mobile phone was switched off. The family searched everywhere and filed a police complaint with her photograph. On January 21, they discovered that she had been admitted to an IVF centre in Civil Lines. Shalini learned that her daughter had undergone surgery and her eggs had been extracted for another woman’s child. Girl reveals periods stopped, operation done under promise of reward Shalini said that after returning home, Komal told her that she had been promised an Apple iPhone and Rs 15,000 for the operation, though only Rs 5,000 had been paid. Komal revealed that Joya supervised everything and was supposed to provide the iPhone. Other girls were also reportedly in contact with Joya. Before being admitted, Komal was given injections that stopped her periods. She was then called daily to the IVF centre, where injections were administered. On January 16, after being admitted, the operation was performed. Shalini reprimanded her daughter after bringing her home, and that night everyone went to sleep. However, the next day Komal went missing again. Following Shalini’s complaint, Fafamau police began searching for her. On February 3, she returned home. Police investigation, CWC involvement When police questioned Komal, she described Joya as someone helping her. Since Komal is only 15 years old, the case was referred to the Prayagraj Child Welfare Committee (CWC). Chairperson Akhilesh Mishra summoned the girl and her mother, recorded their statements, and placed Komal in a one-stop shelter home at Shahganj police station. On the chairperson’s orders, the Special Juvenile Police Unit recorded her statement on camera. Her medical examination has also been scheduled In the photo, Komal is seen with Joya, who is currently being traced by the police. CWC Chair Akhilesh Mishra said that information from Childline suggested the girl had been brainwashed. Therefore, she was placed in the shelter home. The girl’s statements clearly indicate that she was brainwashed and had her eggs extracted. Her statements also reveal that she was encouraged to adopt Islam. Authorities are investigating how many girls may have been trapped in the racket Complaint highlights brainwashing, religious conversion, and exploitation Shalini submitted a new complaint to the police. Joya, who lives in Kareli with her husband Mizan and mother Rinki, is accused of brainwashing girls to change their religion. She then takes them to IVF centres to extract their eggs. The gang reportedly also engages in sexual exploitation of these girls and rents out their wombs for surrogacy.

stories.title: Deadly crash in Unnao kills a family of 4:Truck strikes their bike and leaves them under its wheels; bodies recovered with difficulty
stories.summary: Four people, including a husband, wife, and their two children, died in a tragic road accident on the National Highway near Unnao late Wednesday night. Police said a speeding truck first hit the bike they were riding towards Lucknow and then ran over the family before fleeing the scene. The impact was severe, leaving the victims’ bodies badly crushed. Their remains were collected in polythene bags and sent for post-mortem. The bike was completely destroyed in the crash. The accident took place near Bhalla Farm, under the Soharamau police station area, and police are investigating the hit-and-run. After the accident, the truck driver fled the scene with the vehicle. Local residents immediately informed the police. Soharamau police station personnel arrived at the scene and inspected the accident site. The police removed the bodies lying on the highway and normalized traffic. The damaged bike was taken into custody. The accident occurred about 40 kilometers from the district headquarters. According to preliminary information, the family was from the Ajgain Kotwali area. The identities and names of the deceased have not yet been officially confirmed. Police are working to identify the deceased. Sohramau police station said - The incident is being investigated. Footage from nearby CCTV cameras is being scanned to search for the absconding truck driver.

stories.title: Major reshuffle in UP administration:SPs and SSPs of 11 districts transferred, 24 IPS officers reshuffled, Kaustubh takes over CM City command
stories.summary: 24 IPS officers have been transferred in UP. This includes SPs from 6 districts who were promoted to DIG. SPs and SSPs have been changed in a total of 11 districts. Dr. Kaustubh, who was an eye surgeon for seven years, has been made the new SSP of Gorakhpur. Additional Director General of Police of Lucknow Zone, Sujeet Pandey, has received a new responsibility after his promotion. He has been made the Director General of Police for Fire and Emergency Services. 1994 batch IPS Sujeet Pandey is counted among the sharp and efficient officers. Similarly, Praveen Kumar, who was promoted from IG to ADG, has been made ADG Zone Lucknow. Until now, he was the IG of Ayodhya Range. In place of Praveen Kumar, Mirzapur's SP Somen Verma has been sent to Ayodhya. He was recently promoted to IG. Jaunpur's SP Kaustubh has been sent to Gorakhpur. Gorakhpur's SP Raj Karan Nayyar was also promoted on January 1st. Nayyar has been made Additional CP in Ghaziabad. Additional Superintendent of Police Anukriti Sharma, who uncovered an insurance scam worth over 100 crore rupees in Sambhal, has been transferred to Gautam Buddh Nagar. She has been sent there as Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police. First, let's talk about the SPs and SSPs of the districts Sukirti Madhav: Sukirti Madhav Mishra, a resident of Malaypur village in Jamui district, Bihar, is a 2015 batch IPS officer. Sukirti Madhav was born in 1988. He was currently in Agra LIU. He recited the poem 'Main Khaki Hoon...' to PM Modi on September 4, 2020. Kunwar Anupam Singh: He is an IPS officer of the 2013 batch. He came into discussion in August 2023 when he was transferred from Kannauj to Amroha. Former MP Subrat Pathak had alleged that after the transfer, Anupam Singh, on a back date, made his area's PRO the Station House Officer (SHO) by taking money. Regarding this, he had also written a letter of complaint to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Later, the order was cancelled by IG Kanpur. Avinash Pandey: He is an IPS officer of the 2015 batch. During his posting in Pilibhit, the police had gunned down three Khalistani terrorists in an encounter. Later, he was removed from Pilibhit and posted in the Lucknow unit of the SSF (Special Security Force). Avinash Pandey has now returned once again with an important responsibility. He has been appointed as the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) of Meerut district. Aparna Rajat Kaushik: She is a 2015 batch IPS officer. Aparna has commanded Amethi, Kasganj and Auraiya districts. She served as Assistant Superintendent of Police in Ghaziabad and SPRA in Shahjahanpur. While serving as DCP in the capital Lucknow, she broke the backbone of mafias and criminals. Aparna Kaushik donned the uniform after leaving her job in Business Analysis. Now see the new postings of 13 IPS officers Alok Priyadarshi, Additional Commissioner of Police, Ghaziabad Commissionerate, has been sent as Additional Commissioner of Police, Varanasi Police Commissionerate. Raj Karan Nayyar has been sent as Additional Commissioner of Police, Ghaziabad, from Deputy Inspector General of Police, Senior Superintendent of Police, Gorakhpur. Sankalp Sharma, Deputy Inspector General of Police Mirzapur, has been given the responsibility of Joint Commissioner of Police in Kanpur Police Commissionerate Nagar. Vipin Tada, Deputy Inspector General of Police and Senior Superintendent of Police Meerut, has been made Joint Commissioner of Police in Kanpur Police Commissionerate.

stories.title: Former Bareilly City Magistrate meets Avimukteshwaranand after quitting post:Agnihotri announces Delhi march plan, calls SC-ST Act draconian, vows nationwide agitation
stories.summary: Bareilly's City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri, who resigned, reached Varanasi on Sunday. He met Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand at the monastery. During this time, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was observing a vow of silence. Due to this, their conversation took place through gestures. Alankar Agnihotri explained his future strategy and outline of social-legal struggle. Shankaracharya listened to his words. In conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Alankar said - Recently I resigned from my post in support of UGC and Shankaracharya. This step has been taken under ideological disagreement and commitment to constitutional values. The next fight regarding SC/ST issues will be fought in Delhi. I am reaching Delhi on February 6. Bhaskar discussed future strategy with him. Read the report... Question: Did you meet Shankaracharya after resignation? Answer: The UGC Regulation 2026 brought by the central government is a result of extremely hateful and vicious mentality. Through this, an attempt has been made to establish a dangerous tradition of dividing OBC and General category against each other. It is Bajrangbali's blessing that the public has seen what the government's intentions are. For the first time, there has been a direct attack on India's soul. As a result, even the government's core voters have separated. You must have seen shoes and slippers being thrown at cutouts, photos and banners. This has happened for the first time in history. Question: There are 2 types of governments in the country right now, how do you see it? Answer: Today there is actually no BJP government in the country. At the center, it's like an East India Company government. Two people are sitting there. One considers himself CEO as Prime Minister (Modi ji) and the other has become MD (Amit Shah ji). Their only objective is to take a portion of state governments' budgets, loot 20-30% through the contractor system, and shift that money to Gujarat companies. This entire model is running exactly like the East India Company. Question: After resigning, you were held for hours, what was going through your mind then? Answer: Look, when an officer resigns, seniors naturally consider it. Some efforts were made at that level. Many things were discussed at that time. But now that incident is in the past. There's no point in thinking too much about it. Question: What did you discuss with Shankaracharya ji today? Answer: Today Shankaracharya ji Maharaj was observing a vow of silence. So we couldn't have a conversation. We smiled seeing each other. We took his blessings. Question: Did you talk to Shankaracharya when you resigned? Answer: No, there was no conversation at that time. But I had seen some videos. In which the way the administration pulled the choti (sacred tuft of hair) was very painful to watch. Choti is a symbol of Sanatan Dharma. That's why I clearly wrote this point in my resignation that this is not just about one person, but a national and international matter. Question: You are talking about protest and opposition, what's the future strategy? Answer: We are not just talking about going to Delhi, but this issue will be strongly raised across the country. A press release will be issued. An ultimatum will be given to the government till February 6. If the SC-ST Act, which is the country's biggest black, draconian and blind law, is not repealed, there will be a nationwide movement. Question: Why are you calling this law a black law? Answer: Through this law, false cases are filed against OBC and general category people in 95% of cases. About 85% of the country's society including Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Bhumihar, Kayastha, Lodhi, Rajput, Gangwar, Patel, Gurjar, Jat, Sahu, Pal are affected by this. Even the mothers and sisters of the country are troubled by it. Only those who face this law can understand its pain. Question: Are you preparing to contest elections? Answer: No. Our aim is not to contest elections. Our only effort is nation building, taking the country in the right direction. As soon as the SC-ST Act is removed, you will see yourself how rapidly the country will progress. Question: An Ayodhya official had resigned and then withdrawn it, will you do the same? Answer: No, absolutely not. My resignation is final. It's firm. We will stand firm on the front we have taken. Resigned on January 26, said - hurt by the insult to Shankaracharya Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri had resigned from his post on Republic Day. He cited the new UGC law and the beating of Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand's disciples as the reason. However, his resignation was not accepted. The administration has suspended him and ordered an investigation. On January 26th evening around 7:30, they arrived at City Magistrate DM Avinash Singh's residence to meet him. Upon coming out, the City Magistrate said- I was held hostage at the DM residence for 45 minutes. DM received a call from Lucknow. They said abusively that Pandit has gone mad. Keep him hostage all night. I had already informed the media. I was released on SSP's orders. I have fled to save my life. The City Magistrate vacated his government residence. While leaving, he said - he is staying with his acquaintances in Bareilly today. They will sit together and decide the future strategy. Had submitted resignation with a 5-page letter Alankar Agnihotri wrote a 5-page letter in his resignation. In which he said - 'During the Prayagraj Magh Mela, the disciples of Shankaracharya were grabbed by their hair.' He wrote- Such an incident shakes any ordinary Brahmin from within. It seems that the administration and current government are working against Brahmins and saints-sages. Their dignity is being played with. There is no one to speak for Brahmins. Alankar Agnihotri asked - Is there a preparation for Brahmin genocide. ADM along with three other officers had come to convince the City Magistrate. All four officers stayed at the City Magistrate's residence for about an hour. Then returned. Leaders of several Brahmin organizations along with SP-Congress workers reached to meet Alankar Agnihotri. Brahmin leaders also protested outside the residence. Alankar Agnihotri, who comes from the Brahmin class, became a PCS officer in 2019. He secured 15th rank. Alankar came into discussion after putting up a picture of Lord Hanuman in his office. At that time, the Bhim Army had also created a ruckus at the collectorate. During this, there was also an altercation with the officer.
