stories.title: Toll plaza dispute escalates in Sonbhadra:Female advocate and 3 others thrashed by toll workers, video sparks outrage; two arrested
stories.summary: In Sonbhadra, a female lawyer and her three companions were brutally beaten by toll plaza workers, leaving all four seriously injured, with one woman in critical condition. A video of the assault has surfaced showing toll workers kicking and punching the victims. During the incident, the woman lawyer, seen in a red saree, tried to intervene, kicked the toll booth door, and got into an altercation. It is alleged that a long queue of vehicles had formed at the toll plaza. When the lawyer questioned the delay, the toll workers became agitated, leading to an argument that soon turned violent. The incident has triggered widespread anger among lawyers. Police have registered a case and arrested two accused. The matter falls under the Robertsganj Kotwali area. 3 pictures Know the full story Advocate Aarti, a resident of Robertsganj, said she was travelling to Obra police station with Naveen Kumar Singh, Garima Singh and Avnish Dubey. On Sunday around 4 pm, a long queue of vehicles had formed in the barrier lane at Lodhi Toll Plaza. Naveen Singh stepped out of the car, went to the toll booth and asked about the reason for the traffic jam. She alleged that the toll worker inside the booth abused Naveen Singh and threatened to kill him. When Naveen did not return, Avnish Dubey went to check on him, during which two toll workers attacked Naveen Singh, leading to a scuffle. Avnish Dubey, who arrived to intervene, was also assaulted. It is alleged that four to five toll workers repeatedly threw both of them to the ground and beat them. During this, Naveen Singh sustained serious head injuries and started bleeding, while Avnish Dubey sustained serious injuries to his hand. Misbehavior with woman advocate during intervention When Aarti Pandey arrived to intervene, the toll workers also pushed her. As a result, she fell and was injured. She stated that the push exacerbated her anxiety problem. Aarti Pandey alleged that the toll workers were wearing 'kadas' (bracelets) on their hands and attacked with those. Police arrived after about an hour Police reached the spot about an hour after the incident. The injured were admitted to the emergency ward of the medical college. A complaint has been lodged against the toll staff at Robertsganj Kotwali by the victim's side. Injured Naveen Singh said he was travelling from Robertsganj to Obra and had to wait for a long time due to vehicles stuck at the toll plaza. When he asked the toll worker about the delay, the worker used abusive language and, along with others, attacked him. He also alleged that the police who reached the spot behaved rudely with him. Complaints regarding toll plazas coming from across the state Bar Association President Ashok Kumar Srivastava said advocate Aarti Pandey was going to her grandmother’s house in Obra when more than half a dozen toll workers attacked her at the toll plaza using wristbands and sticks. He said complaints about toll plazas are continuously emerging across the state and demanded the immediate removal of the Lodhi toll plaza, alleging it was wrongly established. He added that a general body meeting of lawyers will be convened to decide the future course of action, and further steps will be taken based on the majority decision. CO City Randhir Mishra said- At the Lodhi Toll Plaza in Robertsganj police station area, toll workers had a dispute with the family members of a female advocate. In this matter, a case has been registered on the complaint of the female advocate, and two accused have been arrested. Further action will be taken after scrutinizing CCTV footage.

stories.title: Varanasi Police slap girls, drag them by their hands:Uproar and clashes over entry at Lit Fest; fans arrive for Piyush Mishra
stories.summary: There was a huge uproar on Sunday, the third day of the Kashi Literature and Arts Festival (Banaras Lit Fest) in Varanasi. People got angry over entry at the Taj Hotel. Police arrived at the scene after receiving information about the commotion. Initially, police tried to reason with people using loudspeakers, but people did not listen. The crowd became uncontrollable for entry. Angry people started pushing and shoving at the gate. They tried to force their way in. Police officers pushed people to disperse them, but this created a stampede-like situation. Actually, the event organizers and sponsors had invited thousands of people. However, when the crowd grew, they closed the gates. This caused an uproar there. Meanwhile, seeing the commotion, Piyush Mishra has not yet arrived at the event. There is also chaos on the stage inside. Organizers closed entry gate as crowd increased On Sunday, there was Piyush Mishra's concert, for which a large number of people had gathered. When more people than capacity arrived, the entire road and both gates of Taj Hotel got jammed. When entry was stopped due to overcrowding, the crowd also started creating a ruckus. During the chaotic situation, some youths started jumping over the wall to get inside. However, they were prevented from going inside. Meanwhile, when a gate was opened to let a car out, the crowd became uncontrollable. After this, there was a clash between police personnel and the crowd at the spot. After this, a sub-inspector beat up and chased away several youths. Women and young girls were misbehaved with. They were grabbed by their hands and removed from there. Women were misbehaved with in the presence of ACP Nitin Taneja and Cant Inspector at the spot. Police slapped girls, pulled them by hand People who came with VVIP passes to listen to Piyush Mishra called the main organizers Deepak Madhok, Amit Sevaramani and Brijesh Singh. However, their phones were switched off. People appeared angry about this. Many girls, who were students of Deepak Madhok's school, had VVIP passes but they were also not allowed to enter. To control the chaotic situation, ACP Nitin Taneja got ropes installed at the spot. Around 10 people were injured during the commotion.

stories.title: IndiGo flight makes emergency landing in Varanasi after bomb threat:237 passengers panic; departure area of airport evacuated
stories.summary: An IndiGo flight made an emergency landing at Varanasi airport following a bomb threat, prompting the evacuation of the runway and departure area. ATS, STF, the Intelligence Bureau and other security agencies rushed to the spot, while eight ambulances were deployed and health teams put on alert. Passengers were deplaned, checked and questioned as a high alert was declared at the airport. Gomti Zone DCP Akash Patel and ACP Prateek Chauhan are present at the site along with their forces. 2 photos Varanasi ATC received threat call On Sunday evening, an Indigo flight (6E-6719) was coming to Varanasi from Hyderabad. There were a total of 237 passengers on board the aircraft. The flight had taken off from Hyderabad at 5:56 PM. The plane was in the sky when a crew member found a paper in the washroom, on which it was written that there was a bomb. This was immediately reported to Varanasi Air Traffic Control (ATC). ATC immediately began preparations for an emergency landing. Security agencies were also alerted. 8 ambulances deployed at runway approach Airport officials say- Information was received about a bomb on the flight, due to which an emergency landing occurred. All teams are now inspecting the aircraft.

stories.title: Arrow pierces Ravana's eye, SC-ST case filed against 'Ram':Firing attempt misses at Sonbhadra Ramlila; victim claims death threat after seeking assistance
stories.summary: An accident during a Ramlila performance in Uttar Pradesh’s Sonbhadra district has left an actor permanently blind in one eye, prompting the police to register a case nearly two months later on the basis of his complaint. The incident occurred on November 13, 2025, during a Ramlila staged in Khaira village under the Shahganj police station area. The mishap took place during the enactment of the battle scene between Ram and Ravana. Arrow misses crown, hits actor’s eye According to the police and the victim’s statement, Sunil Kumar, who was playing the role of Ravana, sustained a serious eye injury when an arrow fired from a bow struck his left eye instead of knocking off his crown, as scripted. The role of Ram was being played by Naitik Pandey. Sunil Kumar alleged that immediately after the arrow struck him, blood and fluid began flowing from his eye. He was later referred to Varanasi for treatment, where doctors confirmed that he had lost vision in the injured eye during the course of medical care. Allegations of assault and threats In his complaint, the victim alleged that after the incident, the Ramlila organisers and the artist playing Ram failed to adequately assist him with treatment expenses. He further claimed that when he sought financial help for his medical care, he was abused, beaten and threatened with death. Sunil Kumar has also filed a case under provisions of the SC/ST Act, stating that he was subjected to abuse linked to his social identity. Delay in FIR registration Explaining the delay in approaching the police, Sunil Kumar said doctors had advised him rest and restricted movement due to the severity of his injury and ongoing treatment. He submitted a formal complaint in the first week of December, but the FIR was registered only on January 28, citing administrative procedures. He said he came to know about the registration of the case only later. ‘Can no longer perform on stage’ The victim said he has now completely lost vision in one eye, while his eyesight in the other eye has also deteriorated. Doctors have advised him to avoid outdoor activities. “Because of my condition, I will no longer be able to participate in stage performances such as Ramlila,” he said. Artist playing Ram calls it an accident Naitik Pandey, who portrayed Ram, maintained that the incident was purely accidental. He said the arrow was released from above the stage as part of the scene and was not aimed at anyone directly. “This was the last day of the Ramlila. I was told by committee members that it was not my fault. I was not aware that an FIR had been filed. It was my first time performing here, and I did not know Sunil Kumar personally,” he said. Police version Circle Officer Rahul Pandey said an FIR was registered on January 28 on the basis of the victim’s complaint. “Preliminary investigation suggests that the arrow was released to dislodge the crown, and there was no prior dispute between the two artists. Initial medical assistance was arranged by the Ramlila committee. Further investigation is ongoing,” he said.

stories.title: Man abducted after accepting lift from Thar riders:Victim beaten, robbed of Rs 60,000, tied and dumped in potato field
stories.summary: A young man was kidnapped by people in a Thar vehicle in Lucknow. They made him sit in the car under the pretext of giving him a lift. After that, they tied his hands and feet inside and beat him severely. They robbed him of Rs 60,000 and his phone from his pocket. Then they threw him tied up in a potato field and fled. The incident took place in the Sairpur area. The young man was sitting in the field crying and calling out to people. As soon as people saw him, they immediately reached him. They untied his hands and feet. After this, they asked him about the whole matter. The young man said that he is a resident of Ghatampur in Kanpur. He drives an LPG gas vehicle here. He was waiting for his vehicle, got lift The victim Hriday Narayan is a resident of Ghatampur in Kanpur and drives a gas truck. On Saturday night, he was returning to Kanpur with his truck from the LPG plant located in Amausi. Around 9 PM near Hydel in Amausi, he was waiting for his vehicle when a Thar stopped near him. Four youths sitting in the Thar asked Hriday Narayan about going to Kanpur. They made him sit in the car on the pretext of giving him a lift, but after driving some distance, they turned the car towards Ring Road. After this, one youth took out a pistol, pointed it at him and started beating him. Blindfolded and beaten inside the car The goons blindfolded Hriday Narayan and tied his hands and feet. They kept beating him throughout the way and snatched 60 thousand rupees kept in his pocket. Later, they threw him in a potato field by the roadside in Sairpur area and fled. Police is currently investigating the case.

stories.title: Sant Ravidas Jayanti celebrated with massive turnout in Kashi:Devotees arrive on 10 chartered planes, offer dollar garland; 3-km-long queue, MP Chandra Shekhar Azad visits shrine
stories.summary: Today marks the birth anniversary of Sant Ravidas. On the occasion, his birthplace, Sir Govardhanpur in Varanasi (Kashi), has virtually turned into a city of Ravidas followers. Lakhs of devotees from across India and abroad have arrived to pay their respects. Since early morning, a queue stretching nearly three kilometres has formed outside the temple. Devotees are waiting for hours to have darshan of Sant Ravidas. In the afternoon, Nagina MP Chandra Shekhar Azad reached the temple and offered prayers. He was welcomed by the temple trustees on arrival. More than 1,000 NRIs have reached Kashi on 10 chartered aircraft. They offered a garland made of US dollars to Sant Ravidas. A 150-foot-high Ravidas flag has also been hoisted near the temple, visible from a long distance. The temple has been decorated with over 200 kilograms of gold. Three large community kitchens (langars) are operating within the temple complex for devotees. On 10-foot-wide griddles, around 1,000 rotis are being prepared every minute. Prasad is being distributed to thousands of people. More than 10,000 volunteers are working round the clock to manage the arrangements. A tent city has also been set up to accommodate devotees coming from outside. Facilities for stay and meals have been arranged for visitors from Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and several other States. Several prominent leaders have also participated in the programme in the past. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, former Chief Minister Mayawati, former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, and Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi have all paid their respects at the shrine. See 6 pictures...

stories.title: Husband jumps into Ganga to save drowning wife:Unable to swim, both start drowning before PAC flood team rescues couple within 30 seconds
stories.summary: During the Magh Purnima holy bath in Ghazipur, a woman went into deep water in the Ganga and began to drown. When her husband, standing on the ghat, saw her struggling, he immediately jumped into the river to save her. The husband, however, did not know how to swim and soon started drowning as well. The flood relief team deployed at the ghat noticed the couple in distress and immediately began rescue operations along with local divers. Some team members reached the spot with a boat, while others jumped directly into the river. After a strenuous effort, the husband and wife were pulled out of deep water within 30 seconds. Throughout the rescue, the couple held on to each other’s hands. After being rescued, the woman said, “These people saved my life. I thank them. Otherwise, my entire world would have ended.” Know the incident in detail… On the morning of Magh Purnima, Amar Ojha, a resident of Badi Bagh in Ghazipur, reached Dadri Ghat with his wife Sushma Ojha for a holy dip in the Ganga. Amar completed his bath first. After this, his wife entered the river. While bathing, Sushma moved about 10 metres ahead of the ghat into deeper water and began to drown. Amar noticed her and, without thinking about the fact that he could not swim, jumped into the river to save her. While trying to rescue his wife, Amar too began to drown. Panic at the ghat As the couple struggled in the river, panic spread among the people present at the ghat. People started shouting for help. The 13-member flood disaster relief team of the 34th Battalion PAC, deployed at the spot, immediately became alert and started rescue operations. Team members Lal Yadav and Sonu Kumar Verma jumped into the river. Local boatmen and divers also joined the rescue. Some team members reached the spot with a boat. Within just 30 seconds, both Amar and Sushma were pulled out of deep water. During the rescue, the couple continued holding each other’s hands until they were safely brought out. After coming out, Amar and Sushma hugged each other and broke down in tears. Sushma said, “The administration saved us. I am extremely thankful to them. I felt my world was about to end.” Team will be honored SP City Rakesh Kumar Mishra said the PAC flood unit team showed excellent courage and would be honoured for their effort. A letter would also be sent to the government. He added that the administration remains on high alert at Ganga ghats during religious bathing, which helped avert a major tragedy.

stories.title: 'Saints should not indulge in party politics':Rajbhar asks Shankaracharya to enter active politics; Avimukteshwaranand skips Prayagraj on Maghi Purnima, returns to Kashi
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Minister Omprakash Rajbhar on Saturday openly advised Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand to enter active politics if he wishes to make political statements. Speaking in Aligarh, Rajbhar said that if the seer wants to do politics, he should join a political party, carry its flag and work among the people, adding that indirect political activity does not suit spiritual leaders. Reacting to the controversy, singer Anup Jalota said saints should speak with restraint and think carefully before making statements from public platforms. Meanwhile, the Shankaracharya’s absence from Prayagraj during Maghi Purnima has drawn attention, as he is currently staying at his monastery in Kashi. The dispute dates back to January 18, when police stopped the Shankaracharya’s palanquin during Mauni Amavasya as he was heading for a ritual bath. Following a scuffle involving his disciples, he staged an 11-day sit-in at the Magh Mela site to press his demands. He left the mela on January 28 and returned to Kashi. Anup Jalota urges restraint Bhajan singer Anup Jalota said everyone should think carefully before speaking in public. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar in Varanasi, where he had come to attend a bhajan programme on the eve of Sant Ravidas’s birth anniversary, Jalota said that even if opinions differ, speech should remain polite. He added that the Yogi and Modi governments have created a positive environment and people should work together to reduce differences. Manoj Tiwari questions demand for proof BJP MP Manoj Tiwari said he doubts the intentions of anyone who asks Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to prove that he is a Hindu. Speaking in Varanasi, Tiwari said that Yogi Adityanath’s entire life has been devoted to serving Sanatan culture and Hindu society, and questioning his faith raises doubts about the questioner’s own identity. Dharampal Singh attacks Shankaracharya Animal Husbandry Minister Dharampal Singh made sharp remarks against Swami Avimukteshwaranand in Bareilly. He said Avimukteshwaranand was making false claims about cow slaughter in Uttar Pradesh. “After Yogi ji formed the government, slaughterhouses were shut down. The cow slaughter he talks about was linked to his own gurus. Attempts to spread confusion and unrest will not be tolerated,” he said. The minister also said the state government does not officially recognise Avimukteshwaranand as Shankaracharya, adding that Shankaracharya is not a constitutional or government-appointed post but a matter of religious traditions. “The government will not accept anyone who spreads confusion in society under the cover of religion,” he said. Invitation from Badrinath amid dispute Amid the controversy, Swami Avimukteshwaranand has been invited as Shankaracharya for an important ritual linked to the opening of Badrinath Dham. The invitation was sent on January 25, even as his dispute with the Prayagraj Magh Mela administration continues. The administration had earlier sought proof of his status as Shankaracharya, to which he responded. On Friday, he also asked CM Yogi Adityanath to provide proof of being Hindu within 40 days. President of the Shri Badrinath Dimri Religious Central Panchayat, Ashutosh Dimri, said Avimukteshwaranand has been invited to take part in the Gadu Ghada Yatra from Rishikesh to Badrinath Dham. What is the Gadu Ghada Yatra? The Gadu Ghada Yatra is a key ritual held before the opening of the doors of Badrinath Dham and marks the formal beginning of the Char Dham Yatra. stories.title: Youth commits suicide by self‑immolation in Ghaziabad:Cyber probe launched as disturbing search history surfaces on his phone
stories.summary: A young man in Ghaziabad poured petrol on himself and set himself on fire. He was admitted to Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi in critical condition, where he later died. Before attempting suicide, the man reportedly searched on his mobile for ways to die quickly—whether to hang himself or burn alive. The young man’s death shocked his family. On receiving the news, Modinagar police reached the spot and took details of the incident. Police also seized the young man’s mobile. Neighbors said the deceased was reportedly involved in a relationship with a girl. Some days later, he was also supposed to join a government job. The deceased has been identified as Madhur Yadav. Selected for Steno position in Rajasthan Madhur Yadav (25) was the elder son of Jitendra Yadav, who works in the Irrigation Department and resides in Mangal Vihar Colony, Modinagar. Madhur had recently been selected for the post of Steno in a Rajasthan court, though the joining date had not yet arrived. He had one younger brother studying in 12th grade. Set himself on fire two kilometres from home On Saturday night around 9 pm, Madhur left his house and reached a spot near Niwari Road, about 2 km from his home. There, he poured petrol on himself and set himself ablaze in an area that was not crowded. A passerby, Abhishek, saw Madhur burning and immediately informed the police. Madhur was rushed to a private hospital in Modinagar, where his family also arrived. Doctors said he had suffered burns over 80% of his body and immediately referred him to a hospital in Delhi. Police asked Madhur about the incident while he was in a burnt state; he only mentioned the name “Abhishek” and was unable to provide further details. He was later admitted to a hospital in Delhi, where he died on Sunday morning. Searched on mobile how to die Police examined Madhur’s mobile and found that on 31 January, he had searched online how to die, how long it takes to die by hanging, and how to die by burning. Police have seized the mobile and are consulting cyber experts. Investigation also revealed that about a week earlier, Madhur had burnt his right hand deliberately. Neighbors said - he had an affair with a girl A neighbor, speaking on condition of anonymity, told police that Madhur had a relationship with a girl and may have taken this step because of the affair. The girl had also reportedly suggested marriage. ACP Modinagar Amit Saxena confirmed that the young man committed suicide. Evidence from his mobile shows that he had researched ways to die quickly, by hanging or burning. The police continue to examine his mobile to gather further details.

stories.summary: A tragic accident occurred in Ambedkar Nagar on Sunday morning when a speeding car rammed into a truck ahead, killing three people, including an uncle and his nephew. Five others sustained serious injuries. All the passengers were travelling from Delhi to Gorakhpur. The accident took place in the Bewana police station area at around 10:30 am. The collision was so severe that the Alto car was badly damaged. The left side of the bonnet was crushed up to the driver’s seat, trapping the occupants inside. After the crash, the truck driver fled the scene. Police arrived promptly and rescued the bodies trapped inside the car. The deceased were sent to the district hospital for post-mortem examination. The injured were admitted to the district hospital in Akbarpur, where their condition remains critical. The families of the victims have been informed and are on their way to the hospital. stories.title: Uttar Pradesh gets 2 high-speed rail corridors:Girls’ hostels planned in all 75 districts, Opposition calls it ‘dream-selling Budget’
stories.summary: With Assembly elections due in Uttar Pradesh next year, the Union Budget 2026 has unveiled a mix of infrastructure, health, urban development and women-centric measures for the State, while placing particular emphasis on Kashi. The announcements, however, have triggered a sharp political debate, with the ruling BJP hailing the Budget as growth-oriented and the Opposition calling it inadequate and election-driven. High-speed rail corridors through Uttar Pradesh A major announcement in the Budget is the sanctioning of two high-speed rail corridors passing through Uttar Pradesh, together covering nearly 1,500 km. The first corridor will connect Delhi and Varanasi, while the second will run from Varanasi to Siliguri in West Bengal. Trains on these corridors are proposed to operate at speeds of 300–350 kmph, compared with 120–150 kmph on conventional railway tracks. According to officials, the Delhi–Varanasi high-speed corridor is expected to be completed in phases over the next 10–15 years. The estimated route includes Delhi, Mathura, Agra, Etawah, Lucknow, Rae Bareli, Prayagraj, Bhadohi and Varanasi. Detailed alignments for both corridors are yet to be officially notified. The government said the corridors would significantly reduce travel time, ease pressure on road and air transport, and help lower pollution levels. Areas around high-speed rail stations are expected to see the development of new townships and basic infrastructure. Port and inland waterways push in Kashi The Budget has placed special emphasis on Kashi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s parliamentary constituency. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced that a port would be developed in Varanasi for the repair and maintenance of inland water vessels. In addition, an inland waterways ship repair ecosystem will be created in Varanasi and Patna. A coastal cargo promotion scheme has also been announced to encourage a modal shift from rail and road to waterways, with the aim of doubling the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping from 6% to 12% by 2047. Health sector: district hospitals and trauma care In a significant health-sector intervention, the Budget proposes a 50% increase in capacity at district hospitals across Uttar Pradesh. Emergency and trauma centres will be set up in districts where such facilities are currently unavailable, covering all 75 districts of the State. Officials said the measures are intended to strengthen secondary healthcare and reduce pressure on tertiary hospitals in major cities. Urban infrastructure and pilgrimage centres Urban infrastructure in cities with populations exceeding five lakh will be developed with an outlay of ₹12.2 lakh crore. About 25 cities in Uttar Pradesh fall under this category, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Ayodhya, Noida, Gorakhpur, Jhansi, Bareilly, Aligarh and Moradabad. Smaller pilgrimage and cultural centres will also be upgraded. The Budget announced focused development of Buddhist and cultural tourism sites such as Sarnath near Varanasi and Hastinapur near Meerut. In total, 15 cultural sites across the country will be taken up alongside eco-tourism projects. Railways, stations and semiconductor push Fifty railway stations in Uttar Pradesh will be redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat Station scheme. The Centre has also launched Semiconductor 2.0, under which a semiconductor park is coming up in Noida. Experts say the project could generate thousands of jobs and strengthen the electronics manufacturing ecosystem in the State. Women-centric measures and ‘Lakhpati Didi’ scheme Women’s self-help groups will be provided interest-free loans of up to ₹5 lakh, aimed at expanding the ‘Lakhpati Didi’ initiative. More than 18.56 lakh women in Uttar Pradesh have already become Lakhpati Didis. The State government has set a target of creating three crore such beneficiaries. In addition, a girls’ hostel will be constructed in each of the State’s 75 districts, a move officials say will support higher education access for women. Political reactions: praise and criticism Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath described the Budget as one of “hope and aspirations”, saying it would accelerate economic growth and create opportunities for youth across sectors. He highlighted the focus on AYUSH, healthcare, women’s hostels and reforms. Uttar Pradesh Finance Minister Suresh Kumar Khanna said increased capital expenditure would boost expressways, industrial corridors, logistics hubs, railways and urban infrastructure, opening new avenues for investment and employment. He added that ₹20,000 crore had been earmarked to reduce carbon emissions and improve air quality. Rajya Sabha MP and former Deputy Chief Minister Dinesh Sharma said the Budget laid the roadmap for making India a global leader in the “orange economy”, with the proposed Indian Institute of Creative Technology in Mumbai and content-creation labs in schools and colleges. The Opposition, however, was sharply critical. Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav called it a “dream-selling Budget” that ignored health, education and inflation. SP MP Dimple Yadav said the Budget had nothing substantial for women and youth. Congress Rajya Sabha MP Imran Pratapgarhi remarked that even the Finance Minister may not have fully understood the Budget. Former MLC Deepak Singh alleged that educated youth were being pushed into unemployment. Election context and expectations With Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh scheduled for March–April next year, economists and political observers noted that expectations of Bihar-like pre-election largesse were not fully met. Lucknow University economist Professor Arvind Mohan said the Budget’s electoral focus appeared to be on States going to polls this year, such as Tamil Nadu and those in the Northeast. He added that another Union Budget before the Uttar Pradesh elections could bring additional announcements, noting that public memory tends to be short-term. In the previous Budget, Uttar Pradesh had received ₹2.93 lakh crore, including ₹2.55 lakh crore as its share of central taxes and an additional ₹38,000 crore later. As the debate continues, the Budget’s long-term impact on connectivity, healthcare and urban development in Uttar Pradesh will depend on implementation timelines and future allocations.

stories.title: Son assaults elderly mother in Ghaziabad home:70-year-old woman slapped, punched and strangled; daughter alerts police, accused taken into custody
stories.summary: In Ghaziabad, a 44-year-old son brutally assaulted his 70-year-old elderly and ailing mother. He first entered the room and sat beside her, slapped her, then strangled her throat for about 30 seconds. After that, he started punching her. He also threw her medicines onto the floor. The daughter, sitting in the United States, watched the entire incident on a CCTV camera installed in her mother’s room. She sent the video to relatives and society members. On information from the society, the police reached the spot. The son was taken into custody and brought to Madhuban Bapudham police station. The incident is a few days old and took place in Sanjay Nagar Sector-23 under the Bapudham police station area. The CCTV footage surfaced on Saturday, showing the son beating his mother. The incident has triggered public anger. Now read the complete matter... The incident took place at house number 22 in Jagrati Vihar, Sanjay Nagar Sector-23. The house belongs to Bhagwan Devi (70). Bhagwan Devi’s husband, Vijaypal Singh, was a school principal. He passed away several years ago. Bhagwan Devi has one daughter and one son. The son, Nishant Raghav (44), lives in the same house. He has studied BCA. The daughter, Nisha Raghav, is a software engineer based in the United States. Son is married, has four children Nishant Raghav got married to Mamta about 17 years ago. They have four children — two sons and two daughters. Due to addiction habits and domestic disputes, a divorce case between Nishant and Mamta has been pending in court for the past around two and a half years. Mamta lives separately in Jagrati Vihar. Nishant returned about three months ago from a de-addiction centre in Noida. Cameras were installed in the house Because the daughter lives in the United States, she was unable to take care of her mother. There was also no one at home to look after Bhagwan Devi. Therefore, Nisha had CCTV cameras installed in the house to keep an eye on her mother. On January 30, Nisha saw the brutality inflicted on her mother from the US. She saw that her brother first came and sat beside their mother, then slapped her and tightly grabbed her throat with his hand. He kept strangling her like that for some time. When he released her, he started punching her. After this, he walked around the room for some time and then threw medicines and other items. The daughter immediately sent the video to her relatives and society members. As soon as the video surfaced, local residents became angry. They informed the Madhuban Bapudham police station. The police reached the spot and took Nishant into custody. Nisha has demanded strict action against her brother. ACP Suryabali Maurya said that in the viral video, a man is seen assaulting an elderly woman. He said the police took the accused into custody and initiated legal action. At present, giving priority to the safety of the elderly woman, the entire matter is being investigated seriously.

stories.title: Rajan Maharaj says, 'If you have the courage, shoot':Katchavachak gets angry on stage in Gorakhpur after his team receives shooting threat
stories.summary: A 9-day Shri Ram Katha by renowned kathavachak Rajan Ji Maharaj is currently underway in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh. However, the event witnessed serious unrest after a dispute broke out over people attempting to climb onto the stage. During the chaos, a member of Rajan Ji Maharaj’s team was allegedly threatened with being shot. Following the threat, Rajan Ji Maharaj decided to leave the Katha midway. He later stayed back only after organisers and local representatives persuaded him and assured his safety. A video related to the incident has now surfaced. Incident took place on 3rd day of Katha The incident occurred on January 29, the third day of the Shri Ram Katha, which began on January 27 at Champa Devi Park, Gorakhpur, and is scheduled to conclude on February 4. In the video, Rajan Ji Maharaj can be heard saying that there was chaos the previous day when some people tried to climb onto the stage. He stated that his team was misbehaved with, following which they decided to restrict access to the stage. Expressing distress, he said Gorakhpur was like his home and that in his 16-year-long spiritual journey, such an incident had happened for the first time. He added that members of his team were threatened with being shot and remarked that if anyone had the courage, they should go ahead. Dispute between organisers and team escalated According to information, a faction of the event organisers clashed with Rajan Ji Maharaj’s team on January 29 over certain issues. The disagreement escalated into a heated argument, during which a threat was allegedly issued to kill a member of the Katha team. As soon as the matter came to light, Rajan Ji Maharaj decided to return. The issue was taken seriously, and a public representative intervened, assuring him that such an incident would not recur. Only after receiving these assurances did Rajan Ji Maharaj and his team agree to continue the programme. Warning against money being taken in his name The following day, Rajan Ji Maharaj addressed the issue during his discourse. He said that such developments had surfaced for the first time in his 16-year journey. He urged devotees to listen to the Katha with love and respect, just as it was being delivered. He cautioned people, stating that he had received information that someone was charging ₹1,100 to arrange meetings with him. He warned such individuals to desist immediately. Rajan Ji Maharaj clarified that he does not meet anyone in exchange for money, either in India or abroad. He said the meeting time is fixed and that he meets devotees for one hour in the afternoon during every Katha. Organisers of the Shri Ram Katha The Shri Ram Katha is being organised by the Shri Ram Katha Organising Committee. The main organisers include Dr Kumud Tripathi, Madan Mohan Tripathi, MLA Pradeep Shukla, Ashok Shukla, Bholendra Dubey, and others. Locals have stated that a lack of coordination among organisers from the beginning may have led to the incident. They termed such an occurrence during a religious discourse in Gorakhpur as unfortunate. Who is Rajan Ji Maharaj ? Rajan Ji Maharaj was born on September 6, 1982, in Kolkata, West Bengal. His real name is Rajan Tiwari, and his family hails from Siwan, Bihar. He grew up in a religious Brahmin household, where his father, Shivji Tiwari, introduced him to Ramcharitmanas, spiritual stories, and saintly teachings. He studied Chemistry at Scottish Church College, Kolkata, and earned a BSc degree. He was deeply influenced by Swami Vivekananda and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. In 2004, after meeting Prem Bhushan Ji, he chose the path of spiritual discourse. He narrated his first Shri Ram Katha in Howrah in 2011. Since then, he has been delivering Kathas across India and abroad.

stories.title: Girl commits suicide after gang-rape in Meerut:5 boys brutalise 14-year-old, sister says, 'Police altered complaint, named only one accused'
stories.summary: The rape victim's sister broke down while making these allegations. After being raped on January 25, the girl consumed sulfas. My sister was only 14 years old. There were 5 boys who committed the atrocity, but police made only 1 boy accused. Why would we lie, we don't know anyone, have no enmity with anyone. Our complaint was also altered. We just want justice for our sister. On January 30, the girl died. The family created an uproar. The brother says- Sister was found in a bloody condition. She was in such shock that she could only speak broken words about herself. She was in pain, thinking about the dishonor in the village, she took her life. Such accused should get death penalty. The deceased girl is from OBC community. To prevent any political controversy, all roads leading to Mahmudpur Sikheda village in the Bahsuma area have been blocked. Police are only allowing village residents to pass through. Understand the complete sequence of events according to the family Accused lives just 1.5 Km away, called and served alcohol at night Mahmoodpur Sikheda village, located about 30 km from Meerut, is the site of a shocking alleged assault. In the early hours of January 25, around 3 AM, the girl went to the house of accused Anuj, situated approximately 1.5 km from her home. The two were reportedly known to each other prior to the incident. According to the complaint, Anuj allegedly made the girl consume alcohol before raping her. Other accused—Saurabh, Yamin, Aman, and an unidentified boy—are also said to have sexually assaulted her. Following the alleged attack, the girl was left in a severely injured and bloody state as the accused fled the scene. The girl was later taken to her home by Anuj’s mother in the morning, still in a critical condition. After recovering a bit, the girl narrates what happened to her. The girl's family members go to Anuj's house, but Anuj's mother says - I cannot keep your girl like this. After returning home, the girl consumed sulfas kept in the house. After her condition deteriorated, she was admitted to the medical college. After her condition worsened, she was put on ventilator on January 29. Brain not working, pressure for cremation at night Doctors stated that the girl’s brain had stopped functioning properly and her body had become numb. On January 30, at around 5 PM, the victim died while on a ventilator. At 8 PM, the police conducted her post-mortem and later brought her body back to the village that night. The police reportedly pressured the family to conduct the cremation immediately at night, but the family refused. Authorities sealed off the entire village. Barricades were set up with force deployment at all entry points, stopping entry and exit. The SP Rural, CO Mawana, and personnel from five police stations were deployed both inside and outside the village. On January 31, after much persuasion and commotion, the victim’s last rites were performed under police supervision at around 1 PM. Family members said - Cannot talk, police check mobile phones The girl’s family said they were unable to communicate with anyone as the internet was shut down across the entire village. They claimed villagers were not allowed to enter, and family members were prevented from meeting anyone. “Police are repeatedly checking our mobile phones. All entry points of the village are blocked, and barricades have been put up,” the family said. “We are only seeking justice for our child.” The family further alleged that on January 26, they filed a complaint at the police station, but no FIR was registered. On January 29, when the FIR was finally filed, they discovered that their original complaint had been altered. According to them, the police named only Anuj as the accused, even though their daughter was gang-raped. Names of Anuj’s accomplices were included in the original complaint, but police reportedly excluded them from the FIR. The case was filed only against Anuj and his mother, father, and brother. While Anuj has been arrested, the family claims that the police are protecting the other accused and facilitating their escape. Now the victim's sister's statement How do I tell my brothers that the bleeding won't stop? The victim’s elder sister recounted that Anuj’s mother brought her sister home in a distressed state around 4 AM, with the girl leaning on her shoulder for support. “As soon as Anuj’s mother let go, my sister fell. Blood was all over her clothes and on the floor. We were shocked and worried,” she said. The elder sister added that her sibling was unable to speak properly and appeared intoxicated, as if someone had given her alcohol. By morning, the girl managed to tell the family that Anuj and his friends had raped her. The family then went to confront Anuj’s household. According to the elder sister, members of Anuj’s family attacked them and verbally abused them. Frightened by the ordeal and the family’s attitude, the girl reportedly consumed pesticide at home, after which her condition deteriorated and she began screaming. The victim’s elder sister said she was too ashamed to even tell her brothers that her sister’s bleeding would not stop. She added that the family did not receive the blood-stained clothes that the doctors had removed at the hospital. According to the doctors, the injuries were consistent with gang rape, not the act of a single person. “She was so terrified of the boys that she could only name Anuj and could not identify any of the others,” the sister said. She further alleged that her sister had been friends with one of the accused for four years. “My sister was only 14 years old. Was she being exploited by him since she was 10? If there was love, was it just with one person, or were his friends involved as well?” she questioned. My flower-like daughter was crushed by monsters The victim’s mother said, “Those monsters crushed my flower-like daughter, and they are still roaming freely. No case has even been filed against them. The police caught only one accused and claimed justice was served. My daughter could not even breathe. The doctor said her uterus was ruptured—a condition that occurs when four to five people commit such a heinous act together.” Village turned into cantonment to prevent OBC politics Following the Kapsad incident in Sardhana, Meerut, on January 8, police reportedly took extensive precautions in the current case from the outset. Authorities made full preparations to prevent politicians from entering the village and turning the matter into a political issue, as had happened in Kapsad. A heavy police force was deployed in the village from the night of January 30. Personnel remained stationed both inside and outside, and entry to the village was blocked. Security forces continue to be deployed across the village, including around the victim’s house, with the SP personally monitoring the situation. Now read what the police have to say... SSP Dr. Vipin Tada said that a complaint of rape involving a minor girl was received at Bahsuma police station, naming Anuj as the accused. The complaint also included allegations of quarrels involving his parents. “Based on the complaint, a case was registered against Anuj, his parents, and brother. Anuj has been arrested, and action is being taken against other individuals involved,” the SSP said. He added that the other party alleges the victim died after consuming poison at her home and that undue pressure was being applied on them. “This aspect is also under investigation. The investigation is ongoing, and evidence from both sides is being examined. The girl’s cremation has been performed by the family. There is peace in the village, with full security deployed for the family’s protection. Statements from both parties are being recorded on video,” he said.

stories.title: Ayodhya gangrape accused Moid Khan acquitted, Raju gets 20-year sentence:Investigation lapses exposed as police ignored key evidence
stories.summary: The Bhadarsa gangrape case, which sparked a massive political storm and "bulldozer action" in Uttar Pradesh a year and a half ago, has reached a significant legal milestone. The Ayodhya POCSO court, presided over by Judge Nirupama Vikram, has honorably acquitted 72-year-old Samajwadi Party leader Moid Khan. Meanwhile, his 20-year-old servant, Raju Khan, has been sentenced to 20 years of imprisonment. Following the court’s verdict, the victim’s side has moved to the High Court. Moid Khan’s camp claims a similar outcome is likely there. Dainik Bhaskar’s team spoke to both parties, analyzed the court’s 32-page judgment, consulted lawyers, and examined gaps in the police investigation. Here’s a detailed look at the case. 14-year-old girl raped at Moid's bakery Bhadarsa village, located about 20 kilometers from Ayodhya district headquarters, is home to Moid Khan. His bakery, situated roughly 500 meters from his residence, lies at a similar distance from the house of the 14-year-old girl. On July 29, 2024, she filed an FIR against Moid Khan and his servant Raju Khan for gang rape. At that time, the girl was 2 months pregnant. She said that both the accused called her to the bakery and repeatedly raped her. At the time the FIR was registered, a by-election was scheduled in the Milkipur Assembly constituency, which brought the case into the spotlight. The very next day, the Purakalndar police station arrested Moid Khan and Raju Khan and sent them to jail. The following month, in August, Moid Khan's bakery and 2-story complex were demolished. The complex, which housed 52 shops belonged to Moid's brother Mahmood Khan. It was being overseen by Moid and his sons. Moid's name not in first statement Our team reviewed the 32-page court judgment and spoke with Moid Khan’s lawyer, Syed Khan. Quoting the judgment, Syed said that when the girl initially filed the complaint, her statement was recorded under Section 164 before the magistrate, in which she named Mohit instead of Moid. The magistrate read out the statement, and the girl did not raise any objections, confirming everything was correct. After this, a second statement was recorded. It was argued that at the time of the first statement, the girl was unwell, which is why she mentioned Mohit instead of Moid. In the second statement, she named Moid, after which the case proceeded. Syed further said that they raised the issue in court: if the girl had named Mohit, why did the police not investigate him or try to identify who he was? Upon investigation, it was revealed that Mohit is the brother-in-law of the girl’s elder sister. The team presented his family records and father’s name before the court, which acknowledged that the police had failed to investigate this matter. Additionally, when the police took the girl to the alleged crime scene, she pointed to a Chilbil tree about 100 meters away instead of the bakery. When asked to describe Moid, she claimed he was overweight, which did not match his actual appearance. Police did not retrieve CDR location, video not found The girl stated that she used to communicate with Raju Khan through her mother’s mobile phone and had gone to the bakery only at his request. She alleged that there, after being given something to eat, Moid and then Raju raped her. However, the police did not obtain call details of either party based on this statement, nor did they investigate their locations at the time of the incident. The girl also mentioned blackmail via a video, but despite seizing both phones, no such video was recovered. Saeed Khan said that in her statement, the girl had claimed she was covered in blood at the bakery and that her mother came looking for her and took her away. When questioned about this matter inside the court, the victim denied that any such incident occurred. Regarding the application she submitted at the police station, the girl said it was written at a local shop by dictation. When asked about the meaning of words like 'blackmail' in the application, she could not explain. She mentioned showing the shop but was unable to do so. When asked whether it was possible that BJP leaders had the application written, she said it could be possible. My father was framed because of BJP leader Zaheer Ahmad, Moid Khan’s elder son, spoke to our team about the case. He thanked the court for delivering a verdict based on truth, adding that though the family had rarely visited courts before, the past one and a half years involved multiple rounds of legal proceedings. Zaheer alleged that his father was falsely implicated at the behest of a local BJP leader. He said the girl’s first complaint did not mention Moid Khan’s name. Instead, local BJP leader Manju Nishad provided his father’s name after losing the Nagar Panchayat election from Bhadarsa, implicating Moid out of enmity. Zaheer added that false information was also given to CM Yogi. The victim’s mother had claimed that Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad was protecting Moid Khan and that the DNA report was altered. Zaheer questioned this, saying, “How can a DNA report be changed like this? If that were possible, a false FIR could also have been filed.” Zaheer further alleged that the administration demolished their bakery, claiming it was on pond land, despite a pending case. He said their family had an agreement with Janki Prasad and that their grandfather’s complex, built on registered land, was also demolished. “Can there be a deed for pond land?” he questioned. Our team visited the site of the demolished complex, which housed 52 shops. Landowners affected by the demolition have homes right next to the site. Another of Moid’s sons pointed out the back portion of the land, saying, “If this was a pond, how can the land behind belong to Praveen Nishad? We won’t comment further. What had to happen has happened. The stigma on our father has been removed.” Government lawyer says - Will go to High Court against the decision We spoke to Vinod Upadhyay, the victim’s lawyer appointed by the UP government. He said, “We do not want to comment on the court’s decision. We will challenge it in the High Court. I had prepared the entire file; all evidence was against Moid Khan. He was not someone who should have been released.” Regarding the video and crime scene disputes, Vinod explained that the video was made from Raju Khan’s phone, but the phone was not seized immediately. Around 15–20 days after Raju’s arrest, his family submitted a phone, making it impossible to verify if it belonged to him. Similarly, there were disputes regarding the crime scene; the incident with the girl reportedly occurred multiple times, with the first incident taking place in the bakery. Court verdict Ayodhya POCSO Court judge Nirupama Vikram ordered that Moid Khan be honorably acquitted. Raju Khan, however, was sentenced to 20 years in prison. Moid Khan will not be released immediately, as a case under the Gangster Act is also registered against him. Lawyers say he may soon be eligible for bail in that case.

stories.title: Hailstorm expected in 27 districts of UP tomorrow, alert issued:Hail blankets roads in western UP; winds blow at 50 km/h
stories.summary: The weather has deteriorated again in Uttar Pradesh. In western UP, intermittent rain has been continuing since late night in 15 districts, including Bareilly, Agra and Meerut. Hail also fell in Muzaffarnagar, Bijnor, Shamli and Amroha. Hailstones the size of peas covered the roads with a white layer. People were seen clearing the ice with spades. Hundreds of bighas of standing crops were flattened. Meanwhile, dense fog has enveloped Purvanchal. Around 25 districts, including Lucknow, Barabanki and Prayagraj, are in the grip of fog that feels like rain. Roads are deserted. People stepping out of vehicles say their hands are going numb. Many were seen warming themselves by bonfires along the roadside. Icy winds have brought back the cold. Due to the fog, road, rail and air services have once again been badly affected. More than 30 trains are running late at several railway stations, including Lucknow and Kanpur. At Lucknow airport, a flight arriving from Dammam kept circling for half an hour before returning. In RaeBareli and three other districts, eight vehicles collided. Two people, including a Home Guard, were killed, while 10 others, including a forest sub-inspector, were injured. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for 31 districts today. A cold-day warning has also been issued for 18 districts, including Maharajganj and Siddharth Nagar. The weather is expected to remain adverse for the next three days. See photos-

stories.title: MLA clashes with minister, roads remain broken:In Mahoba, 3- to 3.5-foot-deep potholes hold mud, taps are without water; troubling residents
stories.summary: In Mahoba district of Uttar Pradesh, BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput clashed with Cabinet Minister Swatantra Dev Singh on January 30. The MLA raised complaints about water not reaching 100 villages in the Charkhari assembly area and roads being damaged due to pipeline work. Dainik Bhaskar visited the area to check the situation. People said the Namami Gange scheme has made life harder for them. Roads in many villages, where the MLA and hundreds of village heads stopped the minister’s convoy, have potholes 3 feet deep. Water pipes are scattered on the roads, water is leaking in some places, and taps remain dry in others. People say that this scheme has worsened the condition of the village. Good CC roads were dug up to lay the lines. 3-4 feet deep pits were dug and left. Pipes were laid and left in front of every house. Neither a tap was installed, nor was a connection given inside the house. Somewhere water is flowing outside the house, somewhere water is not reaching at all. In our investigation, bad conditions were found in 8 villages of MLA Brijbhushan Rajput's constituency, including Dulara, Kusarma, Sabua, Ballany and Anaghora, Chandauli. Read the full report First, read the full story In Mahoba, on January 30, BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput and Cabinet Minister Swatantra Dev Singh clashed. Around 3:30 PM, the MLA, along with 100 village heads, blocked his path. 30 cars and 20 bikes were parked in front of the minister's convoy. The MLA expressed his displeasure to the minister over the lack of water supply in 100 villages of his constituency and the non-repair of roads dug for pipelines. He said, "People from 90 percent of the district's villages ask me. What should I answer?" During this, the MLA's supporters also clashed with the CO Sadar and the Kotwal. On this, Swatantra Dev Singh told the MLA that he was ready to visit 40 villages. "It is our job to provide water. Officers are with me. If roads are dug up somewhere and water is not available, I will suspend the officers," he said. After this, Swatantra Dev sat in his car. Inside the car too, there was an argument between the MLA and the Minister. People continued to chant slogans. After about half an hour of commotion, the MLA was taken to the DM's office in his car. A meeting was held there with the Pradhans for about half an hour. Assurance was given to repair all the dug-up roads within 20 days. Only then did the matter calm down. Now read reports from the villages People said - Har Ghar Nal Yojana has become a problem Dulra village is about 30 km from Mahoba district headquarters, in Charkhari assembly constituency. Its paved roads are dug up. Pipes for the Namami Gange scheme are laid outside homes, but taps have not been installed in them. In half the village, water was found flowing on the road. In the other half of the village, water has not even reached the pipes. Maan Singh, Lakhan Verma, Bhagwandin Ahirwar, and Babita from the village said that after laying the pipeline, the departmental officials disappeared from the site. They did not repair the roads. Walking in the village has also become difficult. The objective of the Har Ghar Jal Yojana (Water to Every Household Scheme) was to deliver water to every home, but in Dulara, this scheme remained confined to paper. Despite having pipelines, water is not coming from the taps. This forces women and the elderly to fetch water from distant places. Regarding MLA Brijbhushan Rajput's anger, the people here say that the officers did not listen to him. Due to this, he was forced to take such a step. The villagers demand that the roads be repaired as soon as possible. And there should be regular water supply under the Har Ghar Nal Se Jal Yojana (Tap Water to Every Household Scheme). 1500 people in Kusarma village facing problems Kusarma village is near Dulara. The roads dug up in this village under the Jal Jeevan Mission are also completely damaged. This village, with a population of about 1500, gets water only two or three days a week. Villagers are troubled by the bad roads. BJP leader said - How will a 3-year problem be solved in 20 days? Brijendra Kushwaha, BJP's sector convenor from Kusmara village, also spoke about the roads being damaged due to excavation by the Jal Jeevan Mission. He said, "We have been struggling with this problem for 3 years. The minister has asked to resolve it in 20 days. How this will happen, only the officers know." Besides this, Gram Pradhan representatives Gulab Singh, Hari Singh, Mangal Singh, and BJP booth president Ravindra Rajput said that after completing the work, the officers did not come back to inspect it. DM said - only 11 km of work remaining Mahoba DM Ghazal Bhardwaj said - In Charkhari assembly, 717 km of CC road was damaged during pipeline laying. Out of this, 706 km of CC construction has been completed. A site inspection of this has been conducted by an agency. The remaining 11 km of road, the construction agency has been directed for its construction. MLA said - Officers, walk with me and see the reality Charkhari MLA Brijbhushan Rajput said - The officers who are giving these figures, walk with me. If their figures are not found correct, they should decide what they will do. The Jal Shakti Minister has asked for 20 days. If the roads are not correct, we will take the matter to the high command. Then whatever the public and the head of our area say, we will do that. SDM-CO and the inspector were jostled BJP MLA's supporters had clashed with police officers deployed for the security of Minister Swatantra Dev Singh. The SDM and CO kept explaining to the people, but they were not allowing the minister's convoy to move forward. Then Swatantra Dev Singh took charge and explained to the policemen. Officers and supporters appeared to be clashing. Their only insistence was that they would present the entire problem before the minister. Seeing the dispute escalate, Minister Swatantra Dev Singh himself went to the DM's office with the MLA. The minister held a meeting with the MLA and village heads along with DM Ghazal Bhardwaj. The DM assured that all the dug-up roads would be repaired within 20 days. After which the village heads and the MLA agreed. Akhilesh had said - not just double engines, but coaches are also colliding On the clash between ministers and MLAs, Akhilesh Yadav had written on X - We had already said that not only the 'double engines' of BJP but also the coaches are colliding with each other. Whether it's BJP ministers or MLAs involved in making money and grabbing land, none of them are working for the public or for development. That's why, to avoid public anger, they are blaming each other. The SP chief had said - By the way, it should not be thought that this is a fight only between these two. In fact, this is just a sample, or rather, an example; the situation is the same in every assembly constituency. This time, BJP will not even find candidates to contest the elections.

stories.title: Saints wave tridents, Mauni Baba reaches Sangam lying down:Crowd so heavy on Magh Purnima that jawans form human chains; 1.2 cr take holy dip
stories.summary: The Magh Purnima holy bath is being held today at the Prayagraj Magh Mela. A huge rush has been witnessed at Sangam Nose since 4 am. So far, about 12 million devotees have taken a dip at the Sangam, far exceeding the administration’s estimate of 5.5 to 6 million pilgrims. Sadhus entered the Sangam waving tridents and damrus, raising chants of Har Har Mahadev. Mauni Baba reached the Sangam after covering nearly 1.5 km while lying down. To manage the swelling crowd, police personnel are regulating movement by forming human chains and repeatedly announcing that devotees should vacate the ghats immediately after bathing. All VIP movement has been completely suspended. See few pictures of the crowd at Sangam- Dense fog covered the area in the morning, forcing people to walk while holding each other’s hands due to poor visibility. This year, the Magh Mela is spread across nearly 8,000 hectares and is being monitored using AI-based technology. After Magh Purnima, only one more bathing day remains on Mahashivratri, scheduled for February 15. Every year, the Magh Mela begins on Paush Purnima and continues until Mahashivratri. Dense fog in the morning reduced visibility to the extent that people were seen walking while holding each other’s hands. This year, the Magh Mela is spread across an area of about 8,000 hectares and is being monitored using AI-based technology. After Magh Purnima, only one more major snan day remains on Mahashivratri, scheduled for February 15. The Magh Mela begins every year on Paush Purnima and continues until Mahashivratri. A total of 2,250 buses will operate from the Jhunsi bus terminal UP Roadways is operating 3,800 buses during the Magh Mela this year, of which 2,250 buses are being run from Jhunsi. Shuttle bus services are also being operated from different parts of the city. Due to bus operations being shifted to Jhunsi, traffic congestion in the Sangam area has eased significantly. As many as 435 buses are operating for Lucknow, Raebareli, Unnao, Basti, Ayodhya, Pratapgarh, Sultanpur and Faizabad.Around 50 buses are running for Mirzapur.Nearly 410 buses are operating for Kanpur, Kaushambi and Delhi.

stories.title: AIIMS for Western UP, IIT for Bundelkhand:People expect more from the upcoming budget; UP govt requests key projects from centre before elections
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh will go to assembly elections next year. Today, the Modi government will present the general budget. Before this, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman held a pre-budget meeting with all states’ Chief Ministers, Finance Ministers, and Additional Chief Secretaries. From Uttar Pradesh, Finance Minister Suresh Khanna and Additional Chief Secretary Deepak Kumar attended. Suresh Khanna asked for budget allocations for 33 sectors, including law and order, social justice, education, health, women, and farmers. After the meeting, all states sent their demands to the center. The UP government has asked for a bigger share of central taxes based on population. It also requested an AIIMS for better medical facilities in Western UP and the pending funds for the Namami Gange project. Due to rising urbanization, the state has also asked for a budget to improve basic facilities in cities. In the last budget before UP Assembly elections in 2022, the state received special packages, including metro projects for Varanasi and Noida, funds for Jewar International Airport, and financial help for Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, and the Ganga Expressway. Bihar received similar benefits at that time. This year, experts expect UP may get special attention in the budget again because of the upcoming elections. Read in Dainik Bhaskar's Sunday Big Story what gifts UP has asked for from the Union Budget as electoral gifts AIIMS demanded for Western UP Uttar Pradesh has the largest population in the country. Currently, there are only 2 AIIMS in the state. The first is in Raebareli in Central UP and the second in Gorakhpur in Purvanchal. This time, the Yogi government has demanded an AIIMS for Western UP as well. Currently, people here go to Delhi for treatment of serious illnesses. With an AIIMS in Western UP, the entire state will be covered. Health expert Mohammad Monish Siddiqui says- Speaking of the health sector, apart from AIIMS, UP can become a big hub for pharmaceutical and medical devices. The government is also talking about this. But, for this, facilities like those in Uttarakhand and Himachal will also have to be provided. There are high hopes from the central budget for this. If better facilities are provided for entrepreneurs, they can come forward in this sector. The coverage of up to 5 lakh for the poor under the Ayushman Bharat scheme should be further increased. National Mission for Clean Ganga Under the National Mission for Clean Ganga, a provision of 25,459 crore rupees was included in the last budget. Most of this amount was to be spent in UP. However, a large portion of the budget could not be received by UP. In such a situation, the government has requested the release of the outstanding amount, so that sufficient funds can be obtained for the ongoing schemes to keep the Ganga clean and stalled projects can be completed. Demanded money for infrastructure in urban areas The central government has closed the Smart City Scheme, while urbanization continues to grow. The UP government has demanded a special budget for building infrastructure in cities. This has also been raised before NITI Aayog. Demanded a larger share in central taxes Last time, in the budget, UP received 2.55 lakh crore rupees as a share in central taxes and later 38 thousand crore rupees. Thus, UP received a total of 2.93 lakh crore rupees. This time, the government has demanded a larger share in central taxes. It is estimated that UP will receive more than 3 lakh crore rupees. Arvind Mohan, Professor of Economics at Lucknow University, says- Due to it being an election year, UP will be seen receiving special attention in the budget. There are two ways this is possible. First- in terms of basic infrastructure, Second- Direct Benefit Scheme. The stalled funds for central scheme projects will also be released. Especially, the center's focus will be on schemes that directly affect common people. These demands were also made One Nyaya Panchayat - one inter college Under the PM-SHRI scheme, 655 crore has been requested for 797 government inter colleges and one Nyaya Panchayat - one inter college for access to all secondary education. Additionally, the establishment of Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district has been demanded. Women must be empowered in AI For a developed India, a special centrally sponsored scheme and financial provision have been demanded to empower women in AI and Data Analytics. Approval should be given for the use of railway land Many lands of Indian Railways are not in use. A demand has been made to provide states with a simple and practical permission system for the public interest use of such land. Additionally, 6 thousand crore has been requested for pure water in villages. Separate Housing Scheme for Valmiki Community Many families of the Valmiki community are unable to meet the standards of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana due to being homeless. A demand has been made to start a separate housing scheme for them. Additionally, a demand has been made to include houses with permanent walls and tin-shed roofs under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) in the category of eligible housing. Review of GST on Brick Kilns, Pan Masala, and Tobacco The brick kiln industry is an important base of the rural economy. Before GST, it generated approximately ?700 crore in annual revenue. This has decreased to ?250 crore after GST. A demand has been made to review this. Additionally, before GST, pan masala and tobacco products generated approximately ?1,000 crore in tax, which has now decreased to ?300 crore, even though consumption has not decreased. A demand has also been made to review this. Western UP districts should be connected to Lucknow Bench A large number of cases from Western UP go to the High Court. However, in the absence of a bench, citizens have to travel far. Therefore, there has been a demand to associate the western districts with the Lucknow Bench of the High Court. These demands can also be fulfilled by the Union Budget Income Tax: Earnings up to 13 lakh can be tax-free In the new income tax regime, the standard deduction can be increased from 75 thousand to 1 lakh rupees. This will make the income of salaried people up to 13 lakh rupees tax-free. Currently, income up to 12.75 lakh rupees is tax-free. Uttar Pradesh will benefit the most from this in terms of population. The money available to the middle class will increase. They could save a few thousand rupees every month. This amount will be useful for expenses, savings, or investment. Kisan Samman Nidhi: Annual amount may increase by 50% The amount of the PM-Kisan scheme can be increased from 6 thousand to 9 thousand rupees annually. There has been talk of increasing it for the past 3 years. Elections are due next year in UP. Currently, 1.89 lakh farmers are receiving this amount here. There has been no change in the scheme since its inception in 2019. In 2024, the Parliamentary Standing Committee had recommended doubling the amount to 12 thousand rupees annually. Similar demands have been raised by farmer organizations. The Bihar government is adding 3 thousand rupees from its side. Similarly, the Madhya Pradesh government is giving 6 thousand rupees, equal to the central government. In this budget, there are preparations to increase it to 9 thousand. This will benefit 1.89 crore farmer families in UP. With this extra amount, farmers will be able to meet their small farming needs. Ayushman Bharat: Benefit for all elders above 60 years of age The government may expand the scope of the Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) scheme. Currently, elderly people above 70 years are benefiting from this scheme, which may be reduced to 60 years. Additionally, the annual limit of 5 lakh for free treatment may be increased, so that the expenses of serious illnesses like cancer and heart surgery can be covered. In UP, there are 5.42 crore Ayushman cardholders. Among them, the number of people aged 60 to 70 years is approximately 1 crore. Out of these, 80 percent do not have any health insurance. For serious illnesses, they are forced to spend their savings. In such a situation, the government can provide them relief. With the increase in the 5 lakh limit, families will not have to take loans for major operations. Patients will also be able to get free treatment in large and specialist hospitals. Rail Infrastructure: New Amrit Bharat and Vande Bharat trains requested The government wants to eliminate the reservation waiting list by 2030 by running new trains. Elections are to be held in UP. The highest demand for trains is also from UP-Bihar. The highest migration is also from here. In view of the increasing pressure from religious tourism and passengers, the government has demanded 20 to 25 new Amrit Bharat and Vande Bharat sleeper trains for UP. Currently, there is a difference of about 20-25% between demand and seat availability during peak season. For this, along with increasing trains, track expansion will also be necessary. PM Surya Ghar Yojana, 80 thousand subsidy on 2 KW solar panel In the budget, the subsidy on solar systems up to 2 kilowatts (KW) may be announced to be increased from 30 thousand per kilowatt to 40 thousand. According to existing rules, installing a 2 KW solar system provides a total subsidy of 60 thousand rupees at the rate of 30 thousand per kilowatt. If the subsidy is increased by 10 thousand rupees per kilowatt in the budget, then a total subsidy of 80 thousand rupees will be received on a 2KW solar system. That means a saving of 20 thousand rupees. For systems between 2 to 3 KW, the subsidy is 18 thousand rupees per kilowatt. For systems above 3 KW, the subsidy is limited to 78 thousand rupees. So far, 3.57 lakh connections have been provided in UP under the PM Surya Ghar Yojana. This has made a solar capacity of 1227 megawatts available. Till now, 10.94 lakh applications have been received. With the increase in subsidy, families installing a 2 KW system will save an extra 20 thousand rupees. What did UP get in the Union Budget before the 2022 Assembly Elections It was the era of Covid. Despite this, the 2021-22 Union Budget provided funds for metro projects for Varanasi and Noida, for Jewar International Airport, and financial assistance for Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, and Ganga Expressway. Under the PM Atmanirbhar Swasth Bharat Yojana, funds were received for opening medical colleges, labs, and health infrastructure in every district of UP. It had received a 7.36 percent share from central taxes. AIIMS had started in Gorakhpur, and it also received a budget for that. This time there is no disaster like COVID. Political experts believe that just as Bihar received special schemes in the last budget, UP can also receive many gifts in this budget. What Bihar received from the Union Budget before the elections In 2025, Bihar received approximately1.43 lakh crore as its share in central taxes and 54,575 crore as grants. This amount constituted about 74% of the state's total revenue receipts. The budget also provided Bihar with an interest-free loan of approximately15,000 crore for long-term (50 years) infrastructure development. Key Announcements

stories.title: Mahoba row: Minister Swatantra Dev Singh denies hostage claim:Says, 'BJP MLA Brijbhushan should have met him formally'
stories.summary: UP Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh on Friday gave his statement on the Mahoba incident. He said that he is a minister and Brijbhushan Rajput is a BJP MLA. Had the MLA come to meet him at the DM office or the circuit house, the issue could have been discussed properly. On the allegation of being taken hostage, Singh said no such incident took place. He added that if the MLA has any work, he can approach him directly. On Thursday in Mahoba, the MLA allegedly blocked Swatantra Dev Singh’s convoy by parking around 50 vehicles in front of it. This led to an argument between the supporters of the minister and the MLA. The MLA claimed that the tap water scheme is in a poor state across the district, with roads left damaged after digging, broken pipelines, and water leaking from tanks. Minister replied to Akhilesh Yadav's taunt Swatantra Dev Singh had arrived on Saturday to attend the Jhansi Day celebrations. Responding to a taunt by Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav over the incident, the minister said he had come to work. He questioned why the issue was being repeatedly raised and asked whether those questioning him had received instructions from “above”. 37 villages receive tap water gift On Saturday afternoon, Minister Swatantra Dev Singh reached Paricha village in Babina assembly. Here he inaugurated the ‘Har Ghar Jal Yojana’ under the Jal Arpan campaign. Under this scheme, water supply through taps was initiated in a total of 37 villages including Paricha village. Minister says it is wrong to call it a hostage situation In Mahoba, Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh spoke to Dainik Bhaskar in Paricha regarding the allegation that he was surrounded on the road by Charkhari MLA Brijbhushan Rajput. He said that just as a village head had come to inform him about a leakage issue, the MLA also approached him with his concerns. Singh said he met them on the road itself and even visited the affected areas along with them. He made it clear that there was no question of him being taken hostage. See photos related to incident... Know the full matter… In Mahoba, BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput and Cabinet Minister Swatantra Dev Singh came face to face during a tense standoff. The minister was returning from a programme when, at around 3:30 pm on Friday, the MLA, accompanied by around 100 village heads, blocked his route. About 30 cars and 20 motorcycles were parked in front of the minister’s convoy, bringing it to a halt. The Charkhari MLA raised concerns over poor water supply in nearly 100 villages of his constituency and the damaged roads that were left unrepaired after pipelines were laid. He said that residents from almost 90 per cent of the district’s villages were questioning him, and he had no answers to give. The situation escalated, leading to a heated exchange between the MLA’s supporters and police officials, including the CO Sadar and the Kotwal. Responding to the MLA, Swatantra Dev Singh said he was ready to visit 40 villages on foot if needed. He said it was the government’s responsibility to provide water and that officers were accompanying him. He added that if roads had been dug up and water was still unavailable, the concerned officers would be suspended. Despite angry village heads attempting to stop him, the minister moved ahead and sat in his car. Slogans were raised as tensions remained high. An argument also took place between the MLA and the minister inside the vehicle before the convoy finally moved on.
