stories.title: 4 women caught in Prayagraj for egg extraction scam:Minor girl lured into IVF with iPhone using false marriage documents, accused under police custody
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, major action has been taken in a case involving the extraction and sale of eggs (ova) from minor girls. Police have taken five people into custody, including four women allegedly involved in the racket. The accused include a mother-daughter pair, an IVF agent, another woman, and a man. The accused allegedly trapped a minor girl by offering her an iPhone and ₹10,000, and then took her to an IVF centre, claiming she was married. There, the minor’s eggs were extracted. The girl’s mother had filed a complaint about the matter on 6 February. Following the complaint, the police took into custody the victim’s neighbour Rinki, her daughter Palak alias Zoya, Seema Bharti, Himanshu Bharti, and Kalpana Bharti. Earlier investigations also revealed the involvement of a Muslim woman in orchestrating the racket. Police are tracing her and examining the case from three angles: The case falls under the Phaphamau police station area. Let's first understand the entire matter... Now know how the arrest happened... DCP Ganga Nagar Kuldeep Gunawat said that after Shalini’s complaint, the police first arrested Rinki and Palak. During questioning, they revealed that they had taken the girl to Seema Bharti (wife of Dileep Bharti). Seema then had her son, Himanshu, create a fake Aadhaar card for the minor, making her appear adult and married. Using these fake documents, Seema handed the girl over to Kalpana Bharti, a registered IVF agent. Kalpana then prepared a fake consent affidavit. Using the fake Aadhaar card and consent affidavit, the IVF centre performed egg extraction on the minor. Based on this, the police took Rinki, Palak, Seema, Himanshu, Kalpana, and another accused into custody. Commission from 30 to 35 thousand rupees DCP Kuldeep Singh Gunawat said- Police investigation revealed that a commission of about 30 to 35 thousand rupees is given for one client. The scam was running because of the commission. More people's involvement may come to light in this. Police are also investigating the role of other agents of the IVF center as well as other people. FIR will be filed against everyone and they will be sent to jail. Investigation ongoing into how many girls trapped in racket Child Welfare Committee (CWC) Chairman Akhilesh Kumar Mishra said- Information about the girl was received through Child Line. stories.title: AIMIM starts preparing for UP 2027 elections:SP and Congress challenge Owaisi to translate numbers into public rallies and advocate for the oppressed
stories.summary: In the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Asaduddin Owaisi’s party AIMIM has started mobilising. The All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen claims to have added over 10 lakh members in UP in the past two months. According to the party, over 86 lakh members are now registered across the state. AIMIM is steadily increasing its presence in UP and claims it will perform better in the 2027 Assembly elections, similar to its results in Bihar and Maharashtra. Meanwhile, the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress have accused Owaisi of indulging in religion-based politics and benefiting the BJP. Read on for the full report… During a membership camp in Kanpur, AIMIM members were present. Congress leader speaks on AIMIM and Owaisi Former Congress city president Naushad Alam Mansoori said that AIMIM’s politics is religion-based and such an organisation can never manage the country. He alleged that the BJP government encourages such organisations, allowing them to grow. He added that if AIMIM truly has 87 lakh members, they should show courage and hold a rally in UP with at least 2 lakh people in attendance. He questioned that despite the atrocities in UP, Owaisi has only been seen giving speeches and has not been on the streets. SP’s comments on AIMIM and Owaisi SP leaders said AIMIM’s membership claims are a private matter. However, if there is any alternative to the BJP in UP, it is only the Samajwadi Party. They added that AIMIM is under a misconception that having so many members will automatically give them a major advantage. Yes, some of their corporators have won, but municipal elections are individual contests. SP leaders described Owaisi as a good speaker, saying that while he delivers good speeches in the house, he could secure better justice for the poor and oppressed by advocating for them in the Supreme Court. They also stated that celebrating just five corporator wins is not significant. If anyone has truly worked for Muslims in UP, it has been only Akhilesh Yadav and earlier Mulayam Singh Yadav. AIMIM leaders respond to SP-Congress Kanpur city vice-president Noor Alam said that Congress and SP accuse AIMIM of being the BJP’s ‘B-team’. He questioned why SP members secretly register for AIMIM membership while their own party is gradually becoming a “declining party.” He added that instead of making accusations, SP should focus on its own work. What AIMIM claims The party first entered UP in 2012. Party’s state general secretary (Central Zone) Azhar Alam said that the enthusiasm among party workers has increased following the party’s strong performance in Maharashtra municipal elections. He added that the party’s growing presence in Bihar has attracted large numbers of supporters nationwide. According to him, there are currently 87 lakh registered members in UP, with over 10 lakh added in the last 40 days of the membership campaign. In Kanpur, membership camps are held every two to three days. So far, 40,000 members have joined in the city. Along with camps, online membership drives are also being conducted. AIMIM claims that it is already strong in UP, holding five chairmen positions and 83 corporators. Both young and elderly citizens are joining the party in significant numbers.

A forensic team was immediately called, which collected important evidence from the site. According to the police, the identity of the deceased has not yet been confirmed. stories.title: Window too narrow for three sisters to jump together:Police spend five hours recreating scene in Ghaziabad triple suicide case
stories.summary: As police continue to probe the triple suicide incident in Ghaziabad, investigators have concluded that it was technically impossible for two or three children to jump together from the same window of the flat. The finding emerged after police spent nearly five hours inside Flat No. 907, recreating the crime scene to determine the sequence of events. The girls had allegedly jumped from a window of the ninth-floor apartment in Bharat City Society. During the reconstruction, police opened the window from which the sisters fell and placed a plastic stool to assess whether more than one child could stand there simultaneously. The experiment showed that only one child could jump at a time. It is to be noted that on the night of February 3, at 2 AM, three girls died after falling from the 9th floor of Tower B-1 of Bharat City Society. From 8 pages of a pocket diary found in the room, it was revealed that the girls were fond of Korean culture. Their mobile phones had been snatched away, which made them upset. What new facts emerged in the 4-day police investigation? Read this in the report… Father questioned after contradictions in marriage claims Following this discovery, police conducted a prolonged interrogation of Chetan Kumar, the father of the deceased girls. Investigators found inconsistencies in the narrative he provided regarding his marriages. Chetan had earlier claimed that he married his second wife due to childlessness. However, police found that several facts related to this claim do not align, prompting further verification. Authorities are now examining whether false information was deliberately provided during the investigation. Incident occurred at 2 AM on February 3 The incident took place around 2 am on February 3, when three sisters—Nishika (16), Prachi (14), and Pakhi (12)—fell from the ninth floor of Tower B-1 in Bharat City Society, resulting in their deaths. An eight-page pocket diary recovered from the room revealed that the girls were deeply influenced by Korean culture. The notes suggested they were distressed after their mobile phones were taken away. Several new facts have emerged during four days of police investigation. CCTV footage and family’s location under scrutiny CCTV cameras installed in the society captured visuals at 2:03 am, showing Chetan Kumar, his wives Sujata and Hina, and sister-in-law Tina going downstairs. Police are also reconstructing who slept in which room that night. In the three-bedroom flat, Chetan was sleeping with his two wives and sister-in-law, along with his son and youngest daughter, Debu. Investigators are questioning how the adults failed to notice the girls’ actions in the adjacent room. Confusion over family relationships According to Chetan’s statement, he married Sujata in 2006. He claimed the families were acquainted as both fathers worked as taxi drivers. After a few months, the couple moved from Delhi to Ghaziabad. Chetan told police that due to childlessness until 2009, he married Sujata’s sister Hina with Sujata’s consent. However, police found contradictions regarding the identity of Tina and the parentage of the youngest child, Debu. Initially, Chetan stated that Debu was Hina’s daughter. Later, it emerged that he had legally married Tina through a court marriage, and Debu is Tina’s child. Police are now verifying these claims. Financial troubles: Trading losses and debt Police also examined Chetan’s financial background. He is one of four brothers; two live in Shalimar City and one in Delhi. His parents are deceased. The family owns two plots measuring 700 and 70 square yards in Delhi’s Khajuri area. When questioned about alleged Rs 2 crore losses in share trading, Chetan claimed that his actual loss was Rs 10 lakh, with another Rs 10 lakh borrowed to meet household expenses. Korean contacts and seized mobile phones The suicide note revealed that the sisters communicated with Korean friends through their youngest sister. Police are yet to determine the nature of these contacts or the social media platforms used. Chetan admitted to selling the girls’ mobile phones. One phone was sold three months ago, while the other was sold ten days before the incident. Nishika and Prachi each had a phone. The only phone found in the room belonged to their mother, Sujata. Police found no Korean apps, games, or data on this device, nor any evidence of connection to Korean online platforms. In the suicide note, one page of a diary and some writings on the walls were repeatedly crossed out. See its pictures Phones being traced through IMEI numbers Police are now using IMEI numbers to trace the sold phones. Once recovered, the devices will be sent for forensic examination to retrieve deleted data and identify any digital interactions. Post-mortem findings: Severe internal injuries According to post-mortem reports, the sisters fell from a height of approximately 80 feet, resulting in multiple fractures and severe internal organ damage, including ruptured heart, liver, lungs, and kidneys. Doctors stated that survival chances after such a fall are extremely low. No old injuries or signs of assault were found on the bodies. Food intake analysis revealed that Nishika had eaten only 50 grams of food two hours before the fall, while Prachi and Pakhi had consumed 250–300 grams, indicating they had dinner that night. Cause of death: Hemorrhage Medical expert Dr. Sanjeev stated that the sisters died due to excessive bleeding (hemorrhage) caused by extensive bodily injuries. The post-mortems were conducted by doctors from Christian Medical College. Police statement DCP Trans-Hindon Nimish Patil said police are investigating all angles. “The crime scene was recreated inside the flat, and several important facts have emerged. Efforts are underway to recover the mobile phones sold by Chetan so that the complete digital trail can be examined,” he said.

stories.title: Akhilesh aide seizes YouTuber’s phone in Kannauj:SP chief asks if questions are ‘coming from BJP’, supporters raise slogans
stories.summary: At a public interaction in Kannauj, an aide to Akhilesh Yadav, Ashish Yadav, briefly seized a YouTuber’s mobile phone after noticing that the questions being posed were appearing as written prompts on the device. According to those present, Ashish Yadav examined the WhatsApp messages on the phone, photographed the questions and showed them to Mr. Yadav. Responding to this, the Samajwadi Party president made a sarcastic remark, asking whether the questions were “coming from the BJP,” before breaking into laughter. Mr. Yadav then asked journalists present to identify themselves by name, remarking that such information helped determine whether the questioners were adequately informed. The exchange prompted slogans from party supporters gathered at the venue. Later, Mr. Yadav inaugurated a local cricket tournament, participating briefly in both batting and bowling. Addressing broader political issues, he accused the Bharatiya Janata Party of diverting the attention of the younger generation through campaigns such as ‘Ghuskhoor Pandit’ and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. He said the government was doing so because it had failed to generate jobs or employment opportunities and was apprehensive of an increasingly discontented youth population. Akhilesh Yadav’s key remarks 1. On the OTT film controversy Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav said people needed to be cautious of the Bharatiya Janata Party, arguing that the same authorities that cleared a controversial film for release on OTT platforms were now allowing cases to be filed over it. He alleged that citizens were being deliberately “entangled”, noting that individuals could face trouble regardless of whether they supported or opposed the film. He further claimed that the funding for such OTT content was likely to have come from individuals linked to the BJP. 2. On U.S. tariffs and ‘Swadeshi’ Referring to reports of the United States reducing tariffs, Mr. Yadav remarked sarcastically that Indians would now “eat American food, wear American clothes and praise America”. He questioned the silence of BJP leaders who, he said, had earlier been vocal proponents of Swadeshi, asking where those voices had gone. 3. On youth, jobs and SIR Mr. Yadav alleged that the BJP was fearful of the younger generation as it had failed to provide adequate jobs and employment opportunities. He claimed that young voters were instead being drawn into the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. Citing an example from Lucknow, he alleged that Muslim votes had been deleted using forged signatures under Hindu names such as Dasharath and Nandlal Kashyap. According to him, an inquiry revealed that one of the named individuals did not know how to sign and used only a thumb impression. Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav attended a series of programmes in Kannauj on Friday, paying condolences to bereaved families and participating in a private function. Mr. Yadav first visited Tirwa, where he reached the residence of late Parmanand Tiwari and paid tribute by offering flowers to his portrait. He also met family members and expressed his condolences. He later paid homage to Pratham Pandey, the son of women’s wing leader Sangeet Pandey, who died recently. He subsequently visited the Abantibai Nagar locality, where he met the family of Jaikaran Yadav and offered condolences on the death of his son. Mr. Yadav also went to the residence of Samajwadi Party leader Anshul Yadav to pay tribute following the death of his father. During the course of the visit, Mr. Yadav expressed condolences to the families of Anand Katheria and Abeer Ali as well. The tour concluded at Hotel BK Grand, where Mr. Yadav attended the wedding ceremony of Vishal Dixit, son of perfume businessman Ram Dixit, and extended his blessings to the newly married couple.

stories.title: Over 12 ministers may be replaced in UP:Second cabinet expansion likely soon; BJP plans Gujarat model reshuffle ahead of key elections
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief minister Yogi Adityanath-led government is preparing for its second cabinet expansion, which is expected to take place soon. Keeping the 2027 Assembly polls and this year’s Panchayat elections in sight, the ruling Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) is reportedly considering a major reshuffle on the lines of the Gujarat model, potentially dropping more than half of the current ministers. According to party sources, over 12 ministers are likely to be replaced, while around 15 MLAs and party office-bearers could be inducted to create new social and political equations. What is the Saffron Party's strategy? Which new faces can get a place in the cabinet? What is the Gujarat model? Why is there a need to adopt it here? Read the special news… Current strength of the Yogi cabinet At present, the Yogi government includes 21 cabinet ministers, 14 ministers of state with independent charge, and 19 ministers of state, apart from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak—taking the total strength to 54 ministers. The maximum permissible size of the cabinet is 60, leaving room for six additional inductions. The first cabinet expansion of Yogi Government 2.0 took place on March 5, 2024, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, when Om Prakash Rajbhar (SBSP), Anil Kumar (RLD), Sunil Sharma and Dara Singh Chauhan were inducted. With Pankaj Chaudhary becoming the BJP’s Uttar Pradesh president in December 2025 and Nitin Nabin recently taking charge as national president, political circles believe the cabinet expansion is now imminent. Why is a cabinet overhaul being considered? 1. Making space for new faces and leadership According to party sources, a section of the central leadership favors a major cabinet reset, removing up to 50% of the existing ministers and replacing them with fresh faces from the party organization and legislature. The proposal suggests sending outgoing ministers into the field for at least a year to focus on election strategy and ground-level mobilization. The move is expected to correct social equations, energize governance, and address internal dissatisfaction among party workers and legislators. However, another faction within the party advises caution, arguing that major changes in an election year could be risky. They recommend minor reshuffles or portfolio changes instead, warning that dropped ministers may defect to rival parties like the Samajwadi Party. 2. Addressing public discontent Multiple complaints against ministers have reportedly reached both state and central leadership through MLAs, RSS functionaries and party workers. Feedback from RSS coordination meetings has also flagged dissatisfaction over the performance of several ministers. What is the Gujarat model and why Uttar Pradesh needs it Ahead of the 2022 Gujarat Assembly elections, Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel accepted the resignations of 16 ministers and formed a new cabinet after consultations with the central leadership. Out of 26 ministers, 19 were fresh faces. The strategy proved successful, as the BJP won 156 of 182 seats, its biggest-ever mandate in Gujarat. Political experts view this approach as a political reset, aimed at balancing caste, regional and social equations while neutralizing public anger against incumbent ministers. Analysts believe a similar strategy in Uttar Pradesh—inducting new faces while sidelining underperformers—could help the BJP regain momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. Political analyst and journalist Virendra Nath Bhatt said that ministers facing dissatisfaction among the public, party workers, government and RSS could be removed, while new inductions would send a clear message that performance matters. Samajwadi Party rebels may also find a place Some of the seven MLAs who rebelled against the Samajwadi Party and joined the BJP may be rewarded with ministerial berths. Names doing the rounds include Manoj Pandey (Unchahar) and Rakesh Pratap Singh (Gauriganj). An audio clip allegedly featuring Manoj Pandey’s son claiming his father would soon become a minister recently went viral. There is also speculation that Pooja Pal could be inducted to project a strong female face against the SP, though senior leaders downplay this possibility. When could the cabinet expansion happen? Political observers see two possible timelines: Senior journalist Yogesh Mishra, however, downplays the likelihood of a major reshuffle. He believes the cabinet expansion will occur between February and March, with only the five to six vacant positions being filled by a mix of old and new faces. According to him, the BJP is not in a position to risk a large-scale purge of ministers, as such a move could destabilize the leadership structure. However, a cabinet expansion is inevitable. Even without major changes, Jat and Brahmin representation likely Political analysts agree that even if sweeping changes are avoided, the cabinet is likely to include one Jat and one Brahmin minister. A Jat ministerial berth has remained vacant since former BJP state president Bhupendra Chaudhary resigned from the cabinet in 2022. Despite the BJP’s alliance with the RLD, there is currently no core-cadre Jat leader in the cabinet, making Bhupendra Chaudhary a frontrunner. Similarly, a Brahmin slot has remained vacant since Jitin Prasada joined the Union cabinet. Potential contenders include Shrikant Sharma, Shalabh Mani Tripathi, Govind Narayan Shukla, and Vijay Bahadur Pathak. Analysts note that Brahmin discontent was openly raised in a meeting of Brahmin MLAs in December, prompting intervention from the party leadership. To contain the fallout, the induction of a Brahmin MLA or MLC is considered almost certain. At present, the cabinet includes seven ministers, each from the Brahmin and Kshatriya communities.

stories.title: Ghaziabad triple suicide case:Girls’ aunt died the same way; grandfather blames son-in-law’s debt woes
stories.summary: The mystery surrounding the suicide case of three young sisters in Ghaziabad has deepened after their grandfather revealed that another girl from the same family had died earlier after falling from the same building. Dilip Kumar, the maternal grandfather of the three deceased girls—Nishika, Prachi and Pakhi—said that around six to seven years ago, one of his daughters had also died after falling from his son-in-law’s flat. At that time, the family had treated it as an accident. Under what circumstances did Dilip marry both his daughters to Chetan? What was Chetan's situation at that time? What did he do? We spoke in detail with his father-in-law, Dilip, on questions like how the situation deteriorated. Read on... “My son-in-Law Once Lived Well, Later Fell Into Debt” Speaking to reporters, Dilip Kumar said his son-in-law Chetan, was once financially stable. “Chetan had a lot of money. He owned a Fortuner car. He worked in vehicle financing and used to buy old houses, renovate them and sell them,” he said. According to him, Chetan lived in Shalimar Garden near Ekta Park in Delhi and later shifted to Ghaziabad. Over time, however, his financial condition deteriorated. “I don’t know what went wrong. He kept sinking into debt. Even the car was sold,” Dilip added. Three sisters died after jumping from ninth floor Chetan lived in Bharat City Society, Ghaziabad, with two of his wives—who are sisters—and their five children. On the night of February 3, the three girls died after falling from the ninth floor of the building. Post-mortem reports revealed that most of their body parts were badly damaged due to the fall. Initially, Chetan claimed the girls had taken their lives after playing a “Korean game,” but police investigations found no evidence supporting this theory. Soon after the incident, the family locked the flat and left. Another daughter died earlier after falling from balcony Dilip Kumar revealed that around six to seven years ago, his daughter, Anchal, aged 16–17, died after falling from the third floor of the same building where the family lived in Shalimar Garden. “She had gone there for my granddaughter Nishika’s birthday. Clothes were drying on the balcony. She slipped while removing them and fell,” he said. The family had then accepted it as an accident and did not pursue any legal action. Two sisters married to the same man Dilip Kumar said he married his eldest daughter Sujata to Chetan around 18 years ago. When Sujata could not conceive initially, the family later married their second daughter Heena to him as well. He said the children were once well cared for and attended school when the family was financially stable. However, as conditions worsened, the girls stopped going to school. “If the parents had made the girls sleep with them, this might not have happened,” he said, questioning why the children slept in a separate room. Sister-in-law falls to death from Chetan's flat About 6-7 years ago, when Chetan lived in Shalimar Garden, his sister-in-law Anchal had gone there. She died after falling from the third floor of the building. Dilip says, 'It was my granddaughter Nishika's birthday, and Anchal had gone there for that. Clothes were put out to dry on the balcony, Anchal was standing on the railing to take down the clothes, her foot slipped and she died on the spot.' Anchal was Dilip's sixth daughter, and was about 16-17 years old. At that time, the family considered it an accident and did not take any action. Limited contact with maternal family The grandfather said that over time, Chetan reduced contact between the girls and their maternal family. Festivals visits stopped, and communication became minimal. One of the sisters, Tanya, said off-camera that the girls slowly became withdrawn and stopped speaking to relatives. “Chetan was in heavy debt. He avoided people, wore masks outside and stopped talking to anyone,” she said. Police continue investigation Police officials are continuing to record statements and investigate unanswered questions. Chetan has not spoken to the media and is reportedly not allowing others to speak either. The case remains under investigation, with authorities trying to piece together the circumstances that led to the deaths of the three sisters.

stories.title: 6 killed on Yamuna Expressway in Mathura:Noida–Farrukhabad bus stops mid-route, container crushes passengers standing roadside
stories.summary: On the Yamuna Expressway in Mathura, six passengers were crushed to death by a speeding container after stepping out of a sleeper bus. One person was critically injured, while two others also sustained injuries. The accident occurred early Saturday morning at around 2:45 am. According to reports, the Agnihotri Travels sleeper bus (UP 75 BT 3907) had left Nangloi, Delhi, around midnight. The bus was packed with passengers and was heading via Noida to Farrukhabad and Rasoolabad in Kanpur Dehat. During the journey, some passengers requested the driver to stop so they could use the bathroom. Instead of stopping at a designated green zone, the driver halted the bus on the expressway itself. Several passengers got down and stood by the roadside. At that moment, a high-speed container (DL 1GE 4418) coming from behind first hit the bus and then ran over the passengers standing on the road. The container driver fled the scene immediately. After the crash, there was chaos at the site, and traffic was blocked for a considerable time. Passersby alerted the police, who rushed ambulances to take the injured to the nearest hospital. The bodies were sent for post-mortem examination. The accident took place near Milestone 88 in the Surir police station area. Victims identified Mohammad Arif, a resident of Etawah, said he was travelling to Katra on the bus. Some passengers asked to stop for the toilet, and the driver pulled over on the roadside. At that moment, the speeding container struck and crushed the passengers. Six people died on the spot, while three others were injured. Arif said his son-in-law Aslam, who worked as a tailor, was among the deceased. The deceased include Sonu, a resident of Sarwa Katra in Auraiya; Devesh from Alewal in Basti; Aslam from Ganesh Ka Purwa in Kannauj; and Santosh from Prem Nagar in Delhi. The identities of two other deceased passengers are yet to be confirmed. Amar Dubey, a resident of Bela in Auraiya, was critically injured and is receiving treatment at a hospital. Surir Station House Officer Ajay Kumar said traffic was disrupted temporarily after the accident, but movement was restored following relief and rescue operations. The police are investigating the case further. Recall of a major Expressway accident Earlier, on December 16 last year, dense fog caused a collision of eight buses and three cars on the Yamuna Expressway. The impact caused fire, killing 19 people including a BJP leader and injuring over 70 others. Police had recovered the bodies in polythene bags, and DNA tests were used to confirm their identities Surir Station House Officer Ajay Kumar said Traffic was disrupted for some time after the accident, but movement was normalized after relief and rescue operations. Police are conducting further investigation into the case. The news is being continuously updated...

stories.title: BJP MLA's nephew ends life in Lucknow:Body found hanging in flat; 'Not God, we will cause your downfall' instagram post emerges
stories.summary: The body of Shivam Tiwari, nephew of BJP MLA Vinay Kumar Dwivedi from Mehnoun assembly constituency of Gonda, was found in his flat in Lucknow. His body was hanging from a fan with the support of a bedsheet. Family members allege that Shivam's partners had committed fraud with him and embezzled money, due to which he had been troubled for many days. In this case, family members have filed a complaint against the accused partners at Sushant Golf City police station. About a week ago, on January 24, Shivam had also made a post on his Instagram account. Sharing a video of him working out at the gym, he wrote - "Not God, we will cause your downfall." The song playing in the background of the video was - "We are a different kind of people Bhakt ji. We don't leave everything to God's mercy. If you have wronged us, rest assured, not God but we will cause your downfall." Landlord broke down the door to enter Balrampur's Shivam Tiwari lived in a rented flat in Tower No. A2, Flat No. 407 at Rishta Manhattan in Sushant Golf City police station area. On the evening of February 1, the landlord arrived at the flat. Despite calling out for a long time, the door did not open. When the flat owner became suspicious, he called the security guard. Then while making a video, they broke down the flat's door, and upon going inside, found Shivam hanging from the fan with a noose. He immediately informed the police. When police arrived, family members were called. The body was brought down. Police said no suicide note was found at the scene. The body has been taken into custody and sent for post-mortem. Was troubled over money matters The deceased's family members said that Shivam worked in property business. For quite some time, his business associates were not paying him money. Shivam had asked them for money several times, but there was no response from them. Due to this, Shivam was mentally very disturbed. Uncle is BJP MLA in Gonda Deceased Shivam Tiwari's uncle Vinay Kumar Dwivedi is a BJP MLA from Mehnoun assembly constituency of Gonda district. In the 2022 assembly elections, he won for the second consecutive time by defeating the SP candidate. Other members of Shivam's family have also contested MLC elections. Shivam's family includes father Rajesh Tiwari, mother, younger brother Prakhar and Abhishek. Family members have demanded filing of FIR against the accused partners.

stories.title: UP cabinet ministers clash publicly in Varanasi:OP Prakash criticises Anil Rajbhar's father; says, 'politics should not drag mothers into disputes'
stories.summary: 'If there is a shop selling votes anywhere in the country, let them tell us where. If anyone has the courage, let them speak up. Those who are pointing fingers today used to steal iron in the past. Has anyone done what Om Prakash Rajbhar has done in 23 years? When we started calling our father as father, only then did people's attention turn towards Suheldev Maharaj.'- Om Prakash Rajbhar 'OP Rajbhar used to drive an auto in Sindhora, Varanasi. Don't know when he came to our village to buy iron rods. You are calling all shopkeepers thieves. This is wrong. We remember that you never came to buy anything from our brother's shop. Why he is saying such things, only he knows.' - Anil Rajbhar These are statements from two cabinet ministers of UP government, who are currently at loggerheads with each other. Both ministers are in Varanasi on Monday. As soon as OP Rajbhar made his statement, Anil Rajbhar countered him after about 6 hours. First about OP Rajbhar's statement Called Anil Rajbhar and his father iron thieves OP Rajbhar became furious when questioned about Cabinet Minister Anil Rajbhar's statement. Without naming names, he called Anil Rajbhar and his father iron thieves. He said that you don't know their history. When his father was in politics, during this time he opened an iron rod selling shop. Any shopkeeper may claim to be honest, but he is not honest. If he becomes honest, how will he earn? If someone takes one quintal of iron rods and gives one quintal back, what will be left for him? OP Rajbhar said - We challenge that if a mother has fed milk, then tell us where votes are sold? We will also find out where the shop for buying and selling votes is? Let us also see that shop. If needed, we will sell our vote. Is a vote something in a sack or bag that can be handed over? Now read what Anil Rajbhar said Cabinet Minister Anil Rajbhar, who arrived in Varanasi on Monday evening, responded to OP Rajbhar's statements. Regarding the statement about drinking mother's milk, Anil Rajbhar said - Mother should not be dragged into politics. A mother is a mother. Whether she's yours or mine. It's not appropriate to challenge mother's milk. Our party's directive is to move forward with coalition partners. I hadn't named any party or leader. However, 10 to 15 people are sent drunk to disrupt our programs. We had those people removed. Now read what OP Rajbhar said On Shankaracharya - Country runs by Constitution, not by statements Om Prakash Rajbhar spoke openly about Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand's statements. Said - the country runs by the Constitution. The Constitution cannot be changed by anyone's statements. On Shankaracharya's 40-day statement, he asked if he is the owner of 145 crore people? When the matter of giving state mother status to cow mother comes to the cabinet, it will be considered then. He called the Bareilly City Magistrate's resignation and meeting with Shankaracharya a drama and politics. Said that we are Rajbhars and speak boldly with pride. Said - UGC has not been withdrawn Om Prakash Rajbhar said - UGC has not been withdrawn, rather it has been stayed. Those who are protesting should tell that there were 17 people from general category in the UGC committee. Didn't they notice any shortcomings? Coding the Education Minister's statement, Rajbhar said that whatever shortcomings are there, they will be improved. Regarding UGC's new guidelines and laws, Rajbhar said - if anyone finds something wrong with this, the Supreme Court's doors are open. There is discrimination against OBC, SC and ST classes in the education system. We will fight for this. Rajbhar also taunted SP Taking a jibe at SP's PDA slogan, Rajbhar said that PDA means "Family Development Authority". Regarding the budget, he said that it has been made keeping in mind the interests of 145 crore citizens. The budget has been made for a developed India.

stories.title: Union Budget allocates ₹20,000 crore for UP Railways:Northern Railway DRM Sunil Kumar Verma says, 'Delhi–Kashi high-speed rail corridor approved'
stories.summary: Regarding the Union Budget, Northern Railway DRM Sunil Kumar Verma said that major approval has been granted for constructing a high-speed rail network in Uttar Pradesh. Under this decision, high-speed rail corridors connecting Varanasi with Delhi and Siliguri will be developed. Completion of these projects will not only save passengers’ time but also make travel between major religious, cultural, and economic centres of the state and the country much easier. Delhi to Kashi in just 4 hours DRM Sunil Kumar Verma stated that under the proposed high-speed rail project, the journey from Varanasi to Delhi will be completed in just four hours. At present, this journey takes around eight to ten hours. With the operation of high-speed trains, long-distance travel will become faster, safer, and more comfortable for passengers. Delhi–Varanasi corridor to span 865 kms The Railways will prepare a project of approximately 865 kilometres for the Delhi–Varanasi High-Speed Rail Corridor. This corridor will be based on state-of-the-art technology, including high-speed operations, advanced signalling systems, and strict safety standards to ensure reliable and secure travel. 2 major high-speed corridors linked to UP Out of the total newly announced high-speed rail corridors, two will be directly connected to Uttar Pradesh. The combined length of these two corridors is expected to be around 1,500 kilometres. Once completed, travel from Delhi to Kashi and towards eastern India will become significantly faster and smoother than before. Trains to operate at 300–350 kmph Trains running on the high-speed rail corridors will operate at speeds ranging from 300 to 350 kilometres per hour. This will save valuable time for passengers and bring a transformative change to long-distance rail travel across regions. The introduction of high-speed rail is also expected to reduce the growing pressure on roads and air traffic. A large number of passengers are likely to prefer fast and affordable rail services, which will help ease traffic congestion and reduce pressure on airfares. UP receives highest allocation of ₹20,000 crore Uttar Pradesh has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of this initiative. A budget allocation of approximately ₹20,000 crore has been made for the high-speed rail network in the state. This investment is expected to provide fresh momentum to infrastructure development, employment generation, and overall economic activity in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: Boyfriend kills girlfriend, alters look by shaving head:Man brings woman from Mumbai, kills her brutally in Gorakhpur; wife supported him
stories.summary: Priya Shetty (35), a Mumbai resident, was murdered on January 30 and her body was dumped in Gorakhpur, police said. Her face was badly damaged with a brick and the body was stripped to prevent identification. Police arrested Priya’s boyfriend Vijay Kumar Sahni on February 2. Investigators said he strangled her, with his wife Sandhya also involved. Vijay shaved his head, beard and moustache to avoid CCTV identification, while his wife disposed of the clothes in a river. Despite this, police traced him through CCTV footage. He used his father-in-law Rambilas Sahni’s scooter during the crime, making him an accused as well. All three have been sent to jail. Senior police officers said a nude woman’s body was found under Barghatta bridge in Pipganj on January 30. Police launched an investigation using CCTV footage and surveillance to identify both the victim and the suspects. CCTV footage from the night showed three people riding a scooter, which raised suspicion. Tracing the vehicle led police to Vijay Sahni, who told investigators he works in the insurance sector and earns around ₹1.5 lakh a month. Police said Vijay had first met the victim, Priya Shetty, in 2012 during work-related interactions. Distance grew after having a son in live-in relationship Vijay told police that he and Priya grew close after a few meetings and began living together in a live-in relationship. He said they later married in a temple and had a son, who is now 13. After the child’s birth, relations soured and Vijay separated from Priya, also filing for divorce in a Mumbai court, which could not be completed as Priya changed her address. Vijay said he returned to Gorakhpur and married Sandhya in 2014. After moving back to Mumbai, Priya contacted him again through Instagram. He resumed meeting her and stayed away for long periods, during which his wife filed missing person complaints. Vijay said Priya later pressured him to take her home and threatened to create a scene, following which his family advised him to bring her to Gorakhpur to talk. Came to Gorakhpur from Mumbai on January 26 Vijay told police that on January 26 he reached Gorakhpur with his wife Sandhya and Priya Shetty and stayed in a hotel for two days, visiting local places. He said the three consumed alcohol frequently, and Priya often threatened to defame the family while drunk. He said that on the evening of January 29, they travelled by auto to Pipiganj after drinking. After an argument with the auto driver over fare, Vijay arranged a scooter belonging to his father-in-law. He claimed that while travelling towards Sahjanwa, the trio drank again, during which Priya created a scene and later collapsed in an intoxicated state, after which he and Sandhya put her on the scooter. Vijay said - I was driving the scooter. Priya was sitting in the middle and Sandhya was holding her from behind. Then we came across the Barghatta bridge on the way. We stopped the vehicle there and all three of us drank alcohol again. There too Priya started creating a scene. Then Sandhya said that she should be killed. At this, I quickly strangled Priya. Being intoxicated, she couldn't even scream. Vijay said that after killing her, along with his wife, he took her body 20 feet down from the bridge. There, to hide her identity, first crushed her face. After this, removed her clothes and made her nude. Then Sandhya and I went home and slept. The next morning, I went to the barber and got my hair and beard removed so that I couldn't be recognized. My wife had also thrown her clothes in the river. Police got help from auto driver SP Gyanendra Prasad said - The auto driver also played an important role in solving this case. After identification in CCTV, he was interrogated. He told that there was one young man and two women. This made it easier to identify the accused. Priya's son is in Mumbai. Her acquaintances have identified her. Now her post-mortem will be conducted. Morning walkers saw the dead body A nude body of a 35-year-old woman was found on the morning of January 30 (Friday) in the Pipiganj area of Gorakhpur. Police and forensic team arrived after receiving information. Evidence was collected from the scene. It was suspected that someone killed her and dumped the body here. The head was crushed to hide the identity. Additionally, injury marks were found at several other places on the body. People who went for morning walks under the Barghatta bridge in Pipiganj saw the woman's body. The woman's body did not have a single piece of clothing on it. The dog squad went to Bairghatta village climbing up the bridge from where the body was found. After about 200 meters, the dog returned. Signs of dragging were also found at some distance from the crime scene.

stories.title: Lok Sabha Speaker turned off Akhilesh's mic:'China issue is very sensitive; Rahul Gandhi should be allowed to speak' says Yadav
stories.summary: In the Lok Sabha, Speaker Om Birla turned off SP President Akhilesh Yadav's microphone. Akhilesh had stood up in support of Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi. He said - The China issue is very sensitive. If it's a matter related to national security, then Rahul Gandhi should be allowed to speak. Speaker Om Birla interrupted him on this. Akhilesh again rose from his seat. He said - I remember that Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, George Fernandes and Netaji (Mulayam Singh Yadav) always emphasized that we need to remain cautious of China. If we don't remain cautious of China, China has already occupied our lands. Akhilesh said - Open discussion in Parliament on important issues like national security and international relations is a fundamental requirement of democracy. It is necessary to hear the opposition's perspective so that correct facts and viewpoints can be presented before the country. Meanwhile, Akhilesh Yadav's microphone was turned off. However, the voices of other leaders sitting in the house could be heard. Rahul says - Chinese tanks were coming to Doklam, uproar in Lok Sabha Actually, Rahul Gandhi gave a speech in Lok Sabha on Monday during the motion of thanks on the President's address. He said Chinese tanks had reached India's border in Doklam. I am saying this with reference to a magazine article which quotes former Army Chief MM Naravane's book (memoir). Rahul said- Listen carefully to what I am reading, it will reveal who is patriotic and who is not. 4 Chinese tanks were coming onto Indian territory in Doklam. They were just 100 meters away. After this, first Defense Minister Rajnath Singh interrupted, then Speaker Om Birla insisted on placing the book in the house. Rajnath said - Let them (Rahul) tell if this book has been published or not. Don't mislead the house. The uproar over Rahul's speech continued for 46 minutes in the Lok Sabha. Speaker Om Birla interrupted him every time he spoke and cited the rules. Rajnath, Shah, Rijiju, and Nishikant Dubey were also seen opposing him. Naravane's autobiography 'Four Stars of Destiny' not published The book based on which Rahul Gandhi is claiming Chinese tanks entered Doklam in Parliament was written by former Army Chief General MM Naravane. This book titled 'Four Stars of Destiny' has not been published yet. It's hardcover is available on online shopping sites from April 2024. The book reviews the Indian Army's 2020 clashes with China along with the Agniveer scheme. Naravane, who served as Army Chief from 2019 to 2022, had told in an interview with Indian Express that he had given his book to Penguin Publisher Group for printing. Now this is a matter between the publishing group and the government. The book has been sent to the Ministry of Defense for approval. More than a year has passed but permission to publish it has not been granted. Imran Pratapgarhi asked - Why was that match played in Dubai after Operation Sindoor?

stories.title: Avimukteshwaranand says Ayodhya GST officer took embarrassing U-turn:Questions raised as beef shipped abroad as buffalo meat
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati on Wednesday mocked Ayodhya GST Deputy Commissioner Prashant Singh for withdrawing his resignation. Laughingly, he said that after the Bareilly City Magistrate’s resignation, another “forced resignation” had now been taken back. He remarked that the officer had “licked back what he spat out” and claimed they had already predicted that the resignation would be withdrawn within four days — which is exactly what happened. GST Deputy Commissioner Prashant Kumar Singh had resigned on January 27 in support of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath but made a U-turn just four days later and withdrew his resignation. The officer later said that there was no pressure on him and that he was continuing to work normally. Avimukteshwaranand also hit back at Uttar Pradesh Animal Husbandry Minister Dharampal Singh over his remarks. He objected to the minister using the word “aaka”, saying it is an Arabic term and reflects a lack of understanding. He said that Shankaracharya is the highest spiritual position, above any administrative hierarchy. “A minister has a Chief Minister above him, and the Chief Minister has the Governor and Union ministers above him,” he said. The Shankaracharya added that the use of such language showed a “Mughal-like mindset”. This came two days after Dharampal Singh accused Avimukteshwaranand of spreading falsehoods about cow slaughter in Uttar Pradesh, claiming that the incidents cited were linked to the Shankaracharya’s own “superiors”. 'Ministers are misleading the public by making allegations against me' Shankaracharya got angry over the statements of ministers Om Prakash Rajbhar and Dharampal Singh Saini. Said- The government is claiming that only buffalo, goat and pork is exported from UP, not beef. However, pork is not exported from UP at all. Then on what basis is this claim being made. We want it to be clarified first how true is the talk of pork exports. If this is false, then there is no point in further discussion. Allegation of beef export under the guise of buffalo meat Shankaracharya alleged that cow meat is being continuously sent abroad under the name of buffalo meat. Referring to incidents in Noida and Bhopal, he said - initially the meat was claimed to be buffaloes, but in lab tests it turned out to be cow meat. When buffalo meat repeatedly turns out to be cow meat in investigations, how can government claims be trusted? Raised questions on number of slaughterhouses Shankaracharya also questioned the Yogi government's claim about shutting down illegal slaughterhouses. On this issue, he said - At the time when the Chief Minister took charge, there were about 40 processed meat exporting slaughterhouses in the state, which have now increased to more than 70 in 9 years. He asked - During whose tenure did this increase happen? If illegal slaughterhouses were closed, how did their numbers increase? Shankaracharya said - No sadhu, sanyasi or monastery head can be a meat seller. He alleged that the CM is taking salary from the treasury that receives income from meat exports. The Chief Minister's monthly salary of about four lakh rupees comes from the same treasury where money from meat sales is deposited. In 106 months, about four crore rupees have been taken as salary. Is this not an insult to saffron clothes and the sanyasi tradition? 'Questioning validity of Shankaracharya position shows ignorance' Responding to ministers calling the Shankaracharya position unconstitutional, Shankaracharya said - When the Shankaracharya tradition was established, the constitution did not even exist, but there were kings and they had given this honor. When the king gave us this position, throne and respect, today's governments are the successors of that system. Therefore, questioning the validity of the Shankaracharya position shows ignorance. He said in clear words - The position of Shankaracharya is not a gift of any modern constitution, rather this position is thousands of years older than the constitution. You cannot say that our position came from your constitution. This position has been continuing since before your constitution was even born. He also said that it is not Shankaracharya's work to make someone win or lose elections. Our work is to give right education to Sanatan Dharma followers. To save society from great sins like the killing of mother cow. If someone wins or loses by their own actions, how is that our fault? Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand said that former Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri, who resigned, met him late at night. However, as he was observing a vow of silence, no discussion took place. Agnihotri shared his views, the Shankaracharya listened and gave his blessings. The monks of the monastery honoured Agnihotri with a tilak and wished him success. Agnihotri spoke about protesting against the SC-ST Act, but the Shankaracharya could not ask questions due to his silence. Speaking on future plans, the Shankaracharya said he will write a letter to saints across the country. The letter will ask whether their Sanatan journey is on the right path or has gone astray. He said saints will be advised to stay away from meat traders and not trust anyone merely by saffron clothing, but to judge by conduct. He added that just as one checks the flow of milk or oil, people should look at actions, not appearances. What will happen to the Shivlings removed from Mahakumbh? On the question of removing the Shivling installed in Mahakumbh, Shankaracharya said - when the camp itself will not be there, why would the Shivling remain there. He informed that these Shivlings will now be installed in that temple where one and a quarter lakh Shivlings are to be consecrated. This temple is being built in Sapad Laksheshwar Dham (Saldha) on the banks of Shivganga river, Bemetara district of Chhattisgarh. The consecration of Shivlings will begin there on the occasion of Mahashivratri.

stories.title: Mute deaf children dance to bhajan:Premanand Maharaj watches with folded hands; kids ask, ‘How do we keep our courage?
stories.summary: Deaf and mute children from Kanpur met Premanand Maharaj in Vrindavan. They asked questions through their gestures. They danced to bhajans they had prepared themselves. During this time, Maharaj ji appeared immersed in the bhajan. He kept watching the children intently with folded hands. Actually, on Sunday evening, Manpreet Kaur, president of the Presidential Award-winning Divyang Development Society, arrived with the deaf and mute children. Manpreet said - These children cannot hear or speak. Some people call us crazy. They call us clever. What should we do so that our and the children's courage doesn't break? To this, Premanand Maharaj said that it is a matter of great fortune that you are nurturing such children. You deserve many thanks. Let selfish people say whatever they want. Your greatness lies in giving love and enthusiasm to such people, as you have accepted them leaving everyone else behind. 'Please bless us that our patience does not break' Manpreet Kaur said, ‘Maharaj ji, some people call us crazy, some call us clever. We are working in our own way. All the people who are associated with us are working in their own way. We just need your blessings that our patience should not break. May our courage remain intact.’ 'Your greatness lies in giving affection to such children' Premanand Maharaj said, 'It is a matter of great fortune that you are nurturing such children with motherly affection. You are also encouraging such children, otherwise such children become discouraged from life. You are worthy of much gratitude. Keep doing what you're doing. What do people know about all this? Everyone is selfish. You are walking the path of spiritual welfare. This is pure spiritual welfare. Because bringing enthusiasm in their minds, giving love to such ones, showing affection to them, this is your greatness. How to connect these children with spirituality? Manpreet Kaur asked - Maharaj ji, we are teaching these children. We are trying for their social upliftment. How do we connect these children with spirituality? Please give us that guidance. 'The heart will begin to purify through name chanting' Premanand Maharaj said - If they start chanting the name in any way, start remembering the Lord, meaning if it happens under your guidance. Radha, Radha, Radha... then their hearts will begin to become pure. They will begin to become sinless. Their auspiciousness will begin. Children sang - Are Man Le Chal Vrindavan... During this time, the children requested to present a bhajan in front of Maharaj ji. After getting Premanand Maharaj's consent, the children performed the bhajan. Adorned with flower garlands and kumkum like Radha-Krishna, the children sang - O mind, let's go to Vrindavan... O mind, let's go to Vrindavan Take me to the banks of Yamuna... Take me to Radha's feet O mind, let's go to Vrindavan... Bansivat... Shringar Vat and Keshi Ghat Want to talk to Radha, worship the dust... O mind, let's go to Vrindavan O mind, let's go to Yamuna's banks... Take me to Radha's feet. Watched children's dance attentively with folded hands Premanand ji was very happy seeing the children's performance. He listened to the bhajan attentively with folded hands. He said - it was a very beautiful presentation. Premanand Maharaj praised Manpreet Kaur for this kind of service and education of children. He blessed the organization's president and the children. Now the story of Sant Premanand Maharaj Left home at age 13 Premanand Maharaj was born in Akhri village of Narwal tehsil in Kanpur district of UP. His father is Shambhu Narayan Pandey and mother is Rama Devi. He has 3 brothers, Premanand is the middle one. In childhood, Premanand ji's name was Aniruddh Kumar Pandey. He was spiritual since childhood. He studied till class 8. In childhood, Aniruddh wanted to build a platform for a Shiva temple with his group of friends. He also started its construction, but some people stopped it. He became disappointed by this. His heart was so broken that he decided to leave home. He reached Kashi via Kanpur. When he turned 13, he decided to become a Brahmachari. Initially, Premanand Maharaj was named 'Aryan Brahmachari'. He spent about 15 months in Kashi. He received initiation from Guru Gauri Sharan Ji Maharaj. Then he came to Mathura. Premanand Maharaj transformed from a monk to a Radhavallabhi saint After reaching Vrindavan, Premanand Maharaj would visit Banke Bihari Ji daily. Then he started attending Raasleela and Radhavallabh programs. He would stand there for hours. One day a saint read a verse from Sri Radharassudhani, but Maharaj could not understand it. Then one day while circumambulating Vrindavan, he heard a sakhi singing a verse. Hearing it, Maharaj stopped in his tracks. The verse resonated so deeply that breaking his sannyasa dharma, he went to that sakhi. Asked her the meaning of the verse. The sakhi said - to understand its meaning, one must become a Radhavallabhi. This is how Maharaj became a Radhavallabhi.

stories.title: Teacher aspirants clash with Lucknow police, scuffles erupt:Forcibly crammed into buses and banners torn after reaching Keshav Maurya’s residence
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a clash broke out between candidates of 69,000 teacher recruitment and the police during a protest. When their path was blocked, protesters got agitated. This led to pushing, shoving, and arguments. Police forcibly lifted the protesters and made them board buses. The demonstrators were crammed into buses and taken to Eco Garden. It is alleged that during this, the police also tore their banners. Protesters had arrived at the site around 11 am on Monday morning. One protester had a banner with slogans such as “I am unfortunate, backward, Dalit” and “Supreme Court is casteist.” Slogans were also written on the hands and bodies of the candidates. ‘Yogi rule is casteist, Supreme Court is casteist’ Candidates said: “I am unfortunate, backward, Dalit. The Supreme Court is casteist. Backward-Dalit reservations are being opposed, casteist Yogi rule prevails.” Using graphics, they explained that the Supreme Court gave a decision for 15% of upper-castes in a single day, while backward-Dalit candidates, who make up 85%, have been waiting 10 months with no decision. No progress has been made for reservation-category candidates in the 69,000 teacher recruitment. Protesters said that while a UGC decision was delivered in one day, the teacher recruitment matter has been stuck for 10 months. ‘We will come every day; let’s see how long police can stop us’ Amarendra, participating in the protest, said: “We will come every day and surround one by one every MLA, leader, and minister. Let’s see how long the police can stop us. We will fight this battle as long as we breathe. Om Prakash Rajbhar and Swami Prasad Maurya claim to be the biggest leaders of backward communities. If they were true leaders, why are children from backward castes being beaten?” “We have come to protest. Police are scared. They are cramming everyone into vehicles. These leaders and ministers are making police beat us and wield lathis. If our leaders had stood firmly, jobs would have been given by now. It is unfortunate that even in ongoing Supreme Court hearings, the government’s lawyer has not appeared.” News is being continuously updated...

stories.title: BSP leader’s Rottweiler attacks child in Hamirpur:Boy bitten on chest and arm, rushed to hospital; police probe, inquiry on dog's licence status
stories.summary: A Rottweiler dog owned by a BSP leader launched a life-threatening attack on a minor child in Hamirpur. The child fell to the ground as the dog attacked him, biting his hand and chest at four places and causing serious injuries. Hearing the child’s screams, the BSP leader rushed to the spot. The child was somehow rescued and immediately admitted to hospital. The 11-year-old had gone to the leader’s house to play with other children. He was coming down the stairs after playing on the terrace when the dog suddenly attacked him. The incident took place on Sunday night in the Sumerpur police station area. Police said a complaint has been received from the family. Preliminary inquiry has revealed that BSP Nagar President Shivam Janardan owns two Rottweiler dogs, neither of which is licensed. Know the full matter Rajendra Kumar Gautam, a resident of Sumerpur town, works in a steel mill. On Sunday evening, his son Ansh went to play at the BSP leader’s house, located about 50 metres away. He played on the terrace with his friend Pathik for around two hours. While returning home, the Rottweiler suddenly pounced on him. Ansh said he did not even get a chance to react. The dog bit him multiple times on his hand and chest. Hearing his cries, the BSP leader and family members reached the spot and rescued the child, but by then he had suffered serious injuries. The injured child was rushed to the Sumerpur Community Health Centre for treatment. Father said - Police did not take action even after complaint The victim’s father Rajendra Kumar said he submitted a written complaint against neighbour Shivam Janardan, but no action has been taken so far. Police said the matter is under investigation based on the complaint. Don't be careless if a dog bites Dr Rohit Bhati said dog bites should never be taken lightly. Rabies is a fatal viral disease that spreads through bites or scratches from dogs, cats or other animals. If anti-rabies injections are not given in time, the virus can spread rapidly and affect the brain, nervous system and heart, which can be fatal. Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of stray dogs According to 2019 data from the Union Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Uttar Pradesh had the highest number of stray dogs in the country — over 20.5 lakh. In Lucknow alone, surveys estimated between 75,000 and 95,000 stray dogs. Rules for Pet Dogs Rules for Stray Dogs (ABC Program)

stories.title: Human trafficking racket busted near Nepal border:Police rescue four girls being brought at night through dense jungle routes, two traffickers arrested
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Police have busted another gang involved in prostitution and human trafficking in Shravasti district. Four Nepali girls being brought into Uttar Pradesh through dense forest routes along the Nepal border were rescued by the police. Two traffickers were also arrested during the operation. Police said the girls were being brought from Nepal through forest routes late at night after being lured with false promises of work as dancers in orchestras. Acting on a tip-off, the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) and local police carried out a joint operation and rescued the girls, who were being transported on two motorcycles. According to police, the girls were extremely frightened. On seeing the police, they panicked and began crying loudly. Female constables present with the rescue team counselled the girls and helped calm them down. It may be noted that Dainik Bhaskar had carried a special investigation report two days earlier exposing the trafficking of underage Nepali girls in the India–Nepal border areas. During the investigation, traffickers and agents had gone on camera explaining how girls are taken from small villages in Nepal and routed through Uttar Pradesh to major Indian cities and even Gulf countries. Following the report’s publication, border police, the SSB and local police had intensified surveillance and operations. Rescue operation in detail On January 31, 2026, Sub-Inspector Deepak Giri of Sirsiya police station was attending a border coordination meeting with the SSB along the India–Nepal border. During the meeting, an informer provided critical information that two Indian youths were bringing four Nepali girls into India via forest routes on motorcycles. Given the seriousness of the information, NGOs and the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) were immediately alerted, and a swift action plan was drawn up. Police teams set up a strategic blockade on the forest route ahead of Bhachkahi village in the Gujjar Gauri border area. Shortly afterwards, two motorcycles carrying two youths and four visibly distressed Nepali girls were spotted. The police intercepted the vehicles and apprehended the youths on the spot, successfully rescuing the four girls from falling into the trafficking network. During questioning, the arrested accused were identified as Hariram Yadav, son of Raksharam, and Ramroop, son of Ram Lotan—both residents of Babhani Kukurbhukva village under Sirsiya police station in Shravasti district. Preliminary investigations revealed that the accused were operating a local human trafficking network along the Nepal border. Police recovered two motorcycles, one Aadhaar card and two mobile phones from their possession. A case has been registered under serious sections related to human trafficking, and both accused have been sent to judicial custody. Police said the role of other members linked to the network is also being investigated. Orchestra lure, plan to send girls to different locations Interrogation revealed that the accused had shown the girls dreams of earning money by dancing in orchestras. In reality, they were preparing to send them to different locations, where the risk of exploitation was evident. stories.title: Gorakhpur to get sewer connections for 3 lakh homes:2,650 km of lines to be laid across 8 zones, ₹2,500 crore project to transform city
stories.summary: Gorakhpur city is set to provide sewer connections to nearly three lakh homes over the next two to three years, transforming the city’s sanitation infrastructure through a ₹2,500 crore sewerage project. The Yogi government has taken several steps in recent years to address the city’s long-standing sewerage problems. Under this initiative, approximately 2,650 kilometres of sewer lines will be laid. Several projects under the plan have already been completed, while others are in progress. Additionally, another project worth ₹721.40 crore has been approved to further expand the sewer network. City divided into 8 zones for sewer development Since taking office, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has focused on improving Gorakhpur’s sewerage system, implementing solutions in multiple phases. The Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation area has been divided into eight zones to streamline the work. Currently, around 2,318 km of sewer lines have been laid or are under construction, with an expenditure of ₹1,858.34 crore. These works are connecting approximately 2.5 lakh homes to the sewer system. Thousands of homes benefiting through AMRUT scheme Under the AMRUT 2.0 (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation) program: For Zone C-2 Part 2, a project worth ₹561.34 crore is underway, which includes laying 188.47 km of sewer lines and establishing a 30 MLD STP. Once completed by March 2026, this phase will connect 43,963 homes. As of now, about 165 km of sewer lines in this zone have already been laid. Additional projects strengthening sewer infrastructure The Godhoiya Nala project, under AMRUT, involves constructing a 38 MLD STP at a cost of ₹495.24 crore. Meanwhile, the Katniya-Mahewa Nala Interception and Diversion project, costing ₹53.03 crore, includes a 10 MLD STP. The National Lake Conservation Program has also contributed to improving Gorakhpur’s sewerage system. Under this program, ₹196.57 crore projects in Zone A-1 and Zone A-2 have already established 15 MLD and 30 MLD STPs respectively. New project approved to benefit 43,604 homes In a state cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the government approved a ₹721.40 crore project for Gorakhpur Sewerage Scheme Zone A-3. This project will provide sewer connections to 43,604 homes across 17 wards, laying 342.19 km of sewer lines. Once completed, Gorakhpur’s sewer network will extend over 2,500 km, significantly improving sanitation, sewage management, and urban hygiene in the city.

stories.title: Govt teacher forces students to offer Namaz in school:Pressurised students to accept Islam, scolded for reciting national anthem; suspended
stories.summary: A case has come to light from a government school in Mathura where a teacher allegedly forced students to offer Namaz. The teacher is also accused of brainwashing children, compelling them to embrace Islam. He reportedly portrayed Islam as superior to other religions and made disrespectful remarks about Hindu deities. Following a complaint by a BJP leader, the Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) suspended the teacher and formed a two-member committee to investigate. Preliminary inquiry found the teacher’s actions to be true. According to the BJP leader, the children’s parents informed him of the matter. He filed a complaint with the BSA on January 30, and action was taken two days later. The incident occurred at Naujheel Primary School under Manta police station. Motivating children to adopt Islam Durgesh Pradhan, BJP Bazna Mandal president, said the school has both Hindu and Muslim students, with Hindus being the majority. The teacher, identified as Jan Mohammad, reportedly brainwashed children, forcing them to offer Namaz. “He demeaned Hinduism, insulted Hindu gods and goddesses, and invited outsiders from the Tablighi Jamaat to the school to teach Islam,” Pradhan said. “Children were scolded for singing the national anthem and told that Islam is superior to other religions and that they must follow its teachings.” Parents had complained to BJP leader Pradhan added that children, distressed by the teacher’s behaviour, informed their parents, who then brought it to his attention. The parents requested the BSA to investigate and take action against the accused teacher. BSA says - Initial investigation confirms allegations against teacher Ratan Kirti of BSA said that a complaint was received regarding the teacher forcing students to offer Namaz. The Block Education Officer (BEO) submitted a report, which found the teacher prima facie guilty. “Jan Mohammad has been suspended and attached to Nagla Humayun Primary School in Manta. BEOs of Chhata and Manta have been ordered to investigate further. Action will be taken based on their report,” Kirti said.

stories.title: Lucknow residents share views on Union Budget 2026:Experts say it is filled with expectations; professionals argue there is no significant relief
stories.summary: In the 2026 general budget, the central government announced several new schemes. The focus is on making India a medical hub and improving youth skills. Experts say the budget will strengthen the infrastructure sector. However, some people feel it did not meet expectations, as there were hopes for major concessions. There is also no change in the income tax slab. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to selected experts in Lucknow to understand the key points of the budget. Dr. Sanjay Singh, Vice-Chancellor of Dr. Shakuntala Misra National Rehabilitation University, said the budget includes support for caregivers of elderly people. He called this a milestone, as today’s young population will eventually become senior citizens, and this step will help them in the future. He added that the budget includes other long-term benefits. While it may not be called a populist budget, experts agree it will have a significant impact. Dr Singh also highlighted the budget’s focus on science and technology. India’s growing achievements in space technology, he said, show the country’s potential to become a global leader in the coming years. The budget also announces several measures for persons with disabilities, aiming to bring them into the mainstream and allow them to contribute more to the country’s progress. A significant step towards an empowered and prosperous India Acharya Narayan Das of Shri Bharat Milap Ashram, situated in Mayakund, Rishikesh, and a native of Lucknow, says that: The Union Budget of 2026 on India's economic horizon is not merely a simple financial statement, but a strong pillar that will give concrete shape to the vision of 'Developed India'. The soul of this budget lies in the coordination of economic discipline and modern national aspirations. On one hand, the government has controlled the fiscal deficit within the modest limit of 4.3%, while on the other hand, the huge capital allocated for basic infrastructure will accelerate the country's progress. Special emphasis on emerging and strategic sectors like semiconductors and bio-pharma clearly indicates that India is now not just a market for consumption, but is moving towards becoming a global hub for innovation, research, and manufacturing. This budget is free from the allure of momentary populist promises and focuses on long-term and sustainable results. A robust banking system, accessible and inclusive technology, along with these, are important steps towards a self-reliant, capable, and prosperous India. Disappointment due to no discussion on new pay scale Satyashankar Mishra, provincial president of the Government Teachers' Association, says that there has been great disappointment regarding Budget 2026. It was hoped that this time the government would definitely pay attention to teachers and the education system in the budget, but by showing a 7% increase, a rattle has been handed over (implying a trivial gesture). Along with increasing the budget, mismanagement was to be removed, which did not happen; money is merely being wasted, neither administrative management is correct nor financial management is correct. Ever since digitalization came, there has been a race among people to make everyone an engineer, everyone a doctor. No one talks about character education. Another problem has arisen in schools: with the aim of making education employment-oriented, they have paid a lot of attention to skill development in schools, but no attention is paid to the arrangement of teachers or their regular curriculum. Posts for important subjects are vacant, and even the teachers who are there have been given other tasks by the department. The condition of schools is very pathetic. First, their infrastructure should be improved, and teachers should be provided so that students can receive basic education. Teaching and learning inside schools should not be disturbed. These practices must be stopped. No one even discusses moral education; everyone wants to make them scientists. It would be better if cultural activities were promoted. Good students should be prepared so that a good society can be formed. The eighth pay commission has not even been discussed; all teaching staff are disappointed.

stories.title: UP PWD’s condemned vehicles 'ran' on paper:Rusted wheels, broken steering; officials siphoned millions in fake diesel claims
stories.summary: A 43-year-old UP PWD jeep, URE-3740, has been lying idle in the Lucknow PWD workshop for years. Its tires are rusted, seats torn, and the gearbox, steering, and dashboard are all broken. The interior is cluttered with old dustbins, posters, and spare tires. The department has officially declared it condemned. Yet, shockingly, officials continued to record it as “operational” on paper—claiming it covered over 5,000 km each month, enabling them to report ₹50,000 monthly in diesel expenses for a vehicle that doesn’t run. Investigations reveal this is not an isolated case—multiple condemned PWD vehicles are being misused in similar ways. What is this diesel expense scam involving condemned vehicles in the PWD? Which officers are responsible? To answer these questions, Dainik Bhaskar conducted a detailed investigation. To uncover and expose this malpractice, two types of case studies were conducted: Vehicles officially declared condemned but still recorded as running on paper. Vehicles not declared condemned yet lying unused for years, which are being “run” on paper to claim diesel expenses. Case Study- 1 The investigation team of Dainik Bhaskar documented that URE-3740 has been stationary in the PWD workshop for at least two years. Photos and videos confirmed the jeep is nothing more than scrap. The Chief Engineer, UK Singh, issued a letter on 26 August 2025, officially declaring the jeep condemned. He confirmed the order and stated a committee was formed to take action against those responsible, with the Senior Engineer RM Srivastava assigned to investigate. Despite this, a diesel bill from November 2025 showed 540 litres of diesel injected into the jeep over 16 days, amounting to Rs 49,816. Who benefited from the diesel scam? Responsibility for operating the jeep was assigned to Junior Engineer Technical (JET) Anil Verma. Verma claimed the jeep was parked from 1 January 2026, though he said it was operational until December 2025. He named drivers Sujit and Laddoo (Abhishek Bhardwaj) as having driven the jeep. Both drivers denied ever operating the jeep. Laddu refused to comment, while Sujeet stated he had no knowledge and threatened to file an FIR against the false allegations. Even the workshop employees confirmed the jeep had been parked for 2–3 years and never left the premises. The claims of December operations were therefore false. We called Laddu (Abhishek Bhardwaj). He said- I am a watchman, why would I drive a vehicle? He refused to say anything else besides this. Case study 2: Old ambassador misused Another case involved an old Ambassador car, UP32-BG-5326, lying in a scrapyard. Although not officially condemned, it too was falsely reported as operational to claim diesel expenses. A diesel bill from November 2025 showed ₹60,767 spent on this vehicle, signed off by Executive Engineer Ranjita Prasad. JET Anil Verma claimed the car was parked since December 2025, and its last actual use was by XEN Firdous Rahmani until October 2025. Both Rahmani and the driver, Saurabh Yadav, confirmed they had not used the car for months. How the scam operated At Alambagh Kohli Pump, diesel was supplied based on a PWD JE slip without verifying the vehicle number. The pump manager admitted: "We provided diesel as per the JE's signature. We did not check the vehicle number. For further details, you need to contact the pump owner." This shows a clear system-level lapse allowing officials to claim diesel for non-operational vehicles, funneling public funds into their pockets. Investigation findings Department Head says, ‘Action will be taken against offenders’ This investigation exposes a disturbing PWD practice: condemned vehicles are listed as running on paper to siphon diesel funds, highlighting corruption in government departments and lack of oversight.
