stories.title: AKT University launches new visual gaming content degree programme:Vice chancellor says AI growth creates high-paying creative career; opportunities for students across Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Azad Technical University (AKTU) in Lucknow, which is affiliated to 765 colleges across Uttar Pradesh, will soon start a new course on AVGC (Audio Visual Gaming Content). The 18 credit course will be offered under the Minor Degree Programme. AKTU Vice Chancellor Prof JP Pandey shared this information in an interview with Dainik Bhaskar after the Union Budget. He said the growth of artificial intelligence has created many new career opportunities in this field. He added that the AVGC sector offers some of the highest salaries for young people globally and is becoming very popular among students because of its creative and interesting nature. Because of this, the launch of the course is being seen as very important. Read the special excerpts from the conversation Question: What has the technical education sector received in this budget? Answer: I would say this is a very good budget. It is technology-oriented. Almost all sectors have been covered in it. It can be called a step taken towards the goal of a developed India. This budget has been brought keeping in mind today's global circumstances, an attempt has been made to respond to the tariffs imposed by America. Question: What is special in the budget for those pursuing a career in technology and future students in this field? Answer: The Semiconductor 2.0 Mission launched by the government in this budget is very important. To increase research in the field of semiconductors and VLSI, a 'technical manpower' will have to be prepared. Experts will have to be trained to bring a boom in the electronics manufacturing sector. In such a situation, technical universities and technical institutions like ours will have to increase work on VLSI, semiconductor devices, and focus more on research. For this, everyone will have to make a concerted effort. Second, skilled manpower for AI will also have to be prepared. AI is to be used in every sector. For this, all faculty and teachers will have to be given AI training. Students will have to be trained in AI. Question: More than 750 technical institutions are affiliated with AKTU, what is important for those colleges? Answer: Besides semiconductor machines, we are also working in the direction of satellite and space technology. We are also working on the Quantum Mission. The goal is to make students of any degree course experts in new and on-demand courses through minor degrees. If the government talks about promoting the MSME or manufacturing sector, then the resource persons for that will come from us. Question: What changes have occurred since the implementation of NEP and how do you see the journey ahead? Answer: The biggest focus is on skill upgradation. The National Skill Qualification Framework has also been linked with the Core Care Ecosystem. All these things mentioned in the budget are also part of NEP. These are all a multidisciplinary approach. With this objective, minor degree programs are being started. The focus is on the all-round development of students. The initiative to set up content creator labs in 1500 schools and 500 colleges has also been taken in this budget. This can also be termed as a big step. Question: Which new course is AKTU going to start after this budget? Answer: We are going to start a minor degree course program related to AVGC, which stands for Audio Visual Content Creation. This will also be important from the students' perspective. Students are interested in this field. This is a very interesting field with new experiences. Students are also doing many innovations in gaming content and technology. With the advent of AI, this also has a lot of potential from an industry perspective. Thus, students are going to get many options and many new opportunities. We will plan and share this 18-credit course.

stories.title: Hail and rain alert in 27 UP districts today:Thunderstorm expected; weather likely to continue for 3 days, Muzaffarnagar records lowest temp in state
stories.summary: The weather in Uttar Pradesh has changed suddenly. Rain accompanied by thunder, lightning and strong winds is continuing across western UP, adjoining Delhi-NCR, and Tarai regions bordering Uttarakhand. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a hailstorm warning for 27 districts today. In addition, 16 districts may experience gusty winds of 40–50 km per hour. Rainfall recorded in several Western UP districts Due to the impact of a western disturbance, rainfall that began in western UP continued intermittently throughout Sunday. In terms of temperature, Muzaffarnagar was the coldest place in the state, with the minimum temperature dropping to 6.4°C. Rainfall area to expand on Monday and Tuesday According to the Weather Department, the spread of rain will increase further on Monday and Tuesday. Central UP, the Awadh region, and parts of Bundelkhand are also likely to witness light to moderate rainfall with thunderstorms. Weather conditions are expected to remain similar for the next three days, till 4 February. What is causing the weather change? Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Singh explained the reason behind the ongoing weather activity. He said, Due to an active western disturbance over northern Pakistan, an induced cyclonic circulation has formed around southern Haryana. This system triggered rainfall in western UP. From late tonight to early morning, the rain may extend to central and adjoining eastern parts of the state. Additionally, the impact of two more western disturbances could keep the rainfall active till 4 February.

stories.title: MLA confronts minister, alleges officers are lying:Says roads are damaged and villages waterlogged; raises issue during proceedings in UP Assembly
stories.summary: BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput from Charkhari in Mahoba district of Uttar Pradesh is in the spotlight after he stopped state minister Swatantra Dev Singh on January 30. The MLA protested over the lack of drinking water in about 100 villages of his constituency and the poor condition of roads dug for pipeline work. He said people from nearly 90 percent of the district’s villages are questioning him, and he has no answers to give. Angry with his own government and officials, Brijbhushan Rajput told Dainik Bhaskar that the Namami Gange scheme, started to solve water problems in Bundelkhand, has still not been completed even after six years. He said village roads were dug in the name of the scheme and left unfinished, leading to waterlogging and serious problems for daily movement, while officers are showing figures that do not match the ground reality. Read the conversation with MLA Brijbhushan Rajput Question: Why was it necessary to block the minister's way on the road? Answer- We went to tell the minister that the 'Har Ghar Nal Yojana' (Tap Water to Every Home Scheme) running under Namami Gange in Bundelkhand is very important and multi-beneficial. The Prime Minister of the country gave this scheme understanding the pain of Bundelkhand. Because, even today, women here have to go miles away to fetch water. This major scheme to provide tap water to every house in every village of Bundelkhand has not been completed even after 6 years. Due to this scheme, the roads that were already built have been damaged. This has led to waterlogging in the villages. Villagers are facing great difficulty in commuting. Question: Are the MLAs not being heard? Answer: The work is not happening. We submitted letters. This issue was also raised in the assembly, but no concrete action was taken. When the minister came, we wanted to show him the ground reality. The officials are presenting false figures. 50 to 60 village heads also went with us. They wanted to tell the minister that the figures being presented from the stage are incorrect. The actual situation on the ground is completely different. Question: How many times have you complained to Minister Swatantra Dev Singh? Answer: Whenever the assembly session was in progress, I and other MLAs raised this issue in the house. However, no effective action has been taken so far. Question: Do the district officials not listen to you? Answer: I feel that the district officials have no interest in getting work done on this scheme. You can also go and see for yourself on the ground. The villagers are also showing the ground situation to the media and public representatives. There is no need to explain this separately. Question: Did you speak to the minister again after this incident? Answer: There was no conversation after this incident. He only said that the work would be done within 20 days. Now we have to see whether the work actually happens or not. Question: Did the Chief Minister, state president, or any senior leader speak to you? Answer: No, I did not try to speak to anyone. Question: How big is the Jal Jeevan Mission scam? Answer: I only want to say that there has been corruption in this scheme. This issue is directly related to the common people. Its truth should come before the government and the public. The MLA stands with the public. Read the full story On January 30, BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput clashed with Cabinet Minister Swatantra Dev Singh. The minister was returning from an event around 3:30 PM. That's when the MLA, along with 100 village heads, blocked his way. 30 cars and 20 bikes were parked in front of the minister's convoy. The Charkhari MLA had expressed displeasure to the minister over the lack of water supply in 100 villages of his constituency and the non-repair of roads dug for pipelines. MLA had told the minister - officers don't listen to us Seeing MLA Brijbhushan's displeasure, the minister made him sit in his car. Even then, the MLA kept hitting his hands together, telling the minister that all the village heads who have come to me have problems in their villages. There has been rampant negligence in the Har Ghar Nal Yojana (Tap Water to Every Home Scheme). You people don't see anything. The ground-level problem is very big. The MLA had also accused the scheme of corruption. He had said that officers don't listen to us. After the meeting with the minister, the MLA had said that the minister has given the officers 20 days to resolve the problems. Now, in 20 days, we will see how much the officers heed the minister's words. In the coming days, whoever needs to be stopped, we will stop them. Whatever fight I have to fight, I will not back down. Who is Brijbhushan Rajput? BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput from Charkhari (Mahoba) was born on May 28, 1982, in Orai (Jalaun). His father, Ganga Charan Rajput, has been a Lok Sabha MP 3 times (1989, 1996, 1998) and a Rajya Sabha MP (2009). Brijbhushan Rajput was married to Kanak Lodhi on May 9, 2005. They have two sons. Brijbhushan Rajput has inherited political conflict. His father, Ganga Charan Rajput, was known for controversies and defections in UP politics. Ganga Charan Rajput has been with Janata Dal, BJP, Congress, and BSP. He led many movements on electricity, water, and OBC issues in Bundelkhand. On May 18, 2004, after the UPA's victory, when there was talk of Sonia Gandhi becoming Prime Minister and she declined the post, a high-voltage drama unfolded outside the Congress office in Delhi. Ganga Charan Rajput climbed onto the roof of a car, brandished a pistol, and, pointing it at his own temple, threatened to shoot himself if Sonia Gandhi did not become PM. Today, a glimpse of that same political temperament is visible in his son, Brijbhushan Rajput. His message is clear: if work is not done, there will be trouble.

stories.title: Woman quits government job to build moringa enterprise:Lucknow’s Kamini builds 8,000-women network; cites Narendra Modi’s moringa paratha remark
stories.summary: While thousands of young Indians chase the security of government jobs, one woman chose to walk away from it — and built a model of entrepreneurship that today empowers more than a thousand women. Eight years ago, Dr Kamini Singh resigned from her prestigious government position to choose an uncertain but self-defined path. What followed was the creation of a unique “moringa army” — a network of nearly 1,000 women farmers — and a business that now records an annual turnover of ₹2.5 crore. Her success reached the national stage in October 2025, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi invited her for a meeting. During the interaction, the Prime Minister mentioned that he eats moringa (sahjan) parathas twice a week. The remark sparked widespread curiosity, leading to a surge in online searches about moringa’s nutritional benefits. This is the story of Dr Kamini Singh from Lucknow, who today manufactures more than 18 value-added products from moringa. Bhaskar spoke to Dr Kamini to understand why she left her government job, how she chose organic farming, and how moringa became the centre of her mission. Connecting women farmers through moringa Dr Kamini Singh brought together more than 1,000 women farmers through a Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) and motivated them to cultivate moringa. She did not stop at farming alone. By focusing on value addition, she helped these women enter the market with finished products rather than raw produce. Today, most of the workforce associated with her enterprise consists of women. From cultivation to processing and packaging, women manage every stage of production on their own. At the unit, women can be seen cleaning and drying moringa and tulsi. Tulsi seeds and leaves are prepared for herbal green tea, while moringa leaves are processed for powder and other products. ‘Working here has made us financially strong’ Women associated with Dr Kamini’s company, Dr Moringa, say the work has strengthened them economically. Vindheshwari, one of the workers, says the products are not only beneficial for health but the employment has improved their financial condition. “Working here has given us regular income and confidence,” she says. More than 18 products from moringa According to Dr Kamini, women currently produce over 18 moringa-based products. These include moringa powder, tablets, moringa tea, handmade soap, moringa seed oil, biscuits, laddus and moringa pain oil. The products are sold in local markets as well as on online platforms and are witnessing strong demand. Who is Dr Kamini Singh? Dr Kamini Singh spent her childhood in the lanes of Varanasi before moving to Lucknow. She earlier worked as a senior researcher at the Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture (CISH). She told Bhaskar that she spent nearly seven years in government service. In 2015, she resigned, and in 2017 began her independent work. That was when she started developing the moringa project along with farmers. Why moringa? Dr Kamini explains that moringa (sahjan) is easy to cultivate and grows in most regions. Despite this, awareness about its benefits remains limited. “Moringa does not require chemical inputs. It gives good yields at low cost,” she says. This made it ideal for organic farming. Convincing farmers initially was difficult, but as they understood its benefits, more people joined the initiative. Over time, both production and farmers’ incomes increased. Struggles before success Success did not come easily. In 2018, Dr Kamini leased seven acres of land in Sidhauli, near Lucknow, and began moringa cultivation. Initially, there were no buyers. She then took a loan of ₹9 lakh to set up a processing unit. By drying moringa leaves, she began making powder, followed by soaps, capsules and other products. Gradually, the market expanded. Today, her annual turnover has crossed ₹2.5 crore. PM Modi and moringa paratha In September 2020, during the first anniversary of the Fit India Movement, Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke about his fondness for moringa parathas, which he eats twice a week. Moringa leaves, roots and fruits are rich in nutrients and vitamins, and are studied for their role in antioxidants, reducing inflammation, diabetes control and cancer research. Dr Kamini translated this nutritional potential into a ground-level organic agricultural model by connecting farmers directly to production and markets. Products beyond moringa Apart from moringa, products are also made from lemongrass and tulsi. Herbal teas prepared from tulsi seeds and leaves have strong market demand, while lemongrass products are known to support immunity. Where are the products available? Dr Kamini says moringa products are available at various retail outlets and can also be purchased through Amazon, Flipkart and the company’s official website. Prices range from ₹75 to ₹1,000, making them accessible to a wide section of consumers. Awareness stalls are also set up to educate people about moringa’s benefits. Farmers’ income up by 40% According to Dr Kamini, farmers’ income has increased by around 40% through moringa cultivation. Currently, more than 500 women are associated with Dr Moringa. Over 30 women are employed on a salaried basis, while others work on commission or daily wages. A cooperative and commercial model Dr Kamini follows both cooperative and commercial models. Women farmers cultivate moringa through the FPO network, while products are sold in the market. A significant portion of the profits is routed back to increase farmers’ incomes. About 30% of sales come from online platforms and 70% from offline channels, including local shops, Ayurvedic stores, medical outlets, agricultural fairs, exhibitions and FPO networks. Women also sell products directly in their local areas, strengthening employment and income at the grassroots. By turning moringa into a sustainable livelihood model, Dr Kamini Singh has not only built her own identity but has also shown how agriculture, entrepreneurship and women’s empowerment can grow together.

stories.title: Teacher beats class-2 child 105 times with stick in Gonda:Thrashes him over incomplete homework; gave biscuit and said, 'If you tell anyone, I will hit you again'
stories.summary: In Gonda, a teacher brutally punished a Class 2 student for not completing his homework, beating him 105 times with a stick. When the terrified child began crying, the teacher gave him a biscuit and threatened to beat him even more if he told anyone at home. Other students were left frightened by the incident. After returning home in tears, the child narrated the entire ordeal to his family. The child’s father immediately took him to the hospital, where doctors provided first aid. When the father later went to the school to complain, the teacher scolded him and sent him away. Based on the father’s complaint, police have registered a case against the teacher, and the school management has expelled the accused. The incident falls under the Colonelganj police station area. Read the complete matter in detail Father complains, teacher booked for beating After school was over, the child reached home crying. He told his father, Raj Prasad, everything. Raj Prasad gave the child first aid. After this, at 4:30 PM, Raj Prasad reached the school with a complaint. The school principal Madhavra,j scolded him and drove him away. At 7 PM, Raj Prasad reached the police station with his son. An FIR was registered against teacher Prakhar Singh. Chachri Police Post In-charge SI Avnish Shukla has been entrusted with the investigation of the case. The child's medical examination was conducted on Friday. Father said - you won't be able to get him hanged Raj Prasad said - When I reached the school with a complaint, the principal, instead, told my son, 'Why didn't you come and tell me when the teacher hit you?' Now tell me, my son is a minor. If a 40-year-old man catches and beats him, how will he be able to escape? After this, when the police outpost in charge called the teacher's father, he said, 'You can't do anything to us. You won't get my son hanged.' Getting him hanged is not my right, but I can certainly get him punished. He should just be punished. He should be arrested. ‘We would have given the child medicine’ Meanwhile, Madhavraj, the principal of the school, said, The student was not completing his homework continuously for some days. Angered by this, the teacher hit him. We had said that we would arrange for treatment, but they went and filed an FIR.To prevent this from happening with any other child, we have removed the teacher from the school. Now I have no responsibility related to that teacher. I am fully cooperating with the police. We have instructed all our teachers that this should not happen again with any child.

stories.title: Hapur businessman kills cancer-stricken wife for ₹5 lakh:Hires employees as contract killers; 'saree ke paise' used as code word
stories.summary: In Hapur, a businessman allegedly murdered his 40-year-old wife for Rs 5 lakh. The woman was suffering from cancer, and frequent disputes erupted at home as the husband was not getting her treated. To eliminate her, the businessman roped in his two employees, both of whom owed him Rs 60,000 each. He waived off their loans and promised Rs 5 lakh for carrying out the murder. To avoid suspicion, he used the code word ‘saree ke paise’ while planning the crime. Finding the right moment, he called the employees home. Together, they attacked the woman, smothered her with a blanket, and slit her throat. To make it appear like a robbery, household items were scattered before the accused fled. The businessman later informed the police himself. The incident took place in Mohammadpur-Rustampur village under Bahadurgarh police station limits. Full incident details Alibi planned after murder After the incident, Rahul attended a wedding ceremony in Nanai village, about 20 km from his home, the same night and even had photographs taken there. He then rode his bike to his shop in Chandpur (Bijnor), where he spent the night. At around 4 am, he returned home and raised an alarm, claiming a robbery and reporting his wife Rita’s murder. Dog squad roamed in the lane of both accused murderers Upon receiving information about the murder, forces from several police stations reached the spot. Police deployed a dog squad, which roamed not only around the house but also near Shera and Firoz's houses. After this, the police interrogated the husband. The husband claimed he was attending his own wedding ceremony. Police retrieved the CDR of his calls, which provided clues to the murder and revealed the code word. According to the police, Rahul Sharma had lent 60-60 thousand rupees to Shera and Firoz. In the murder, it was also agreed that these debts would be waived in addition to the contract killing amount. Police picked up Rahul Sharma from his house last night. Initially, he tried to mislead the police with his words. After that, he was interrogated strictly. He was asked about the code word used in conversations with his two associates, at which Rahul broke down. After this, Firoz and Shera were also arrested by the police. Two knives used in the murder were recovered from both accused. ASP Vineet Bhatnagar stated- The murder case has been solved in 4 days. The husband turned out to be the main accused in his wife's murder. He had involved two employees by giving them a contract of 5 lakh. All three have been sent to jail.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:31 killed in massive blast in Pakistan's Islamabad; UP minister targets Rahul Gandhi with ‘fake Gandhi’ hoardings in Rae Bareli more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. AAP leader shot dead outside gurdwara in Jalandhar AAP leader Lucky Oberoi was shot dead by bike-borne attackers outside a gurdwara in Jalandhar’s Model Town area. Police are searching for the unidentified assailants. 2. UP minister targets Rahul Gandhi with ‘fake Gandhi’ hoardings in Rae Bareli Nine posters calling Rahul Gandhi a “fake Gandhi” were put up across Rae Bareli by BJP minister Dinesh Pratap Singh. Congress has termed it narrow and divisive politics. 3. Kashi Vishwanath temple to remain open 26 hours on Mahashivratri To manage heavy footfall, the Kashi Vishwanath temple will stay open continuously for 26 hours on Mahashivratri. Special arrangements are being made for devotees. 4. 31 killed in massive blast at Shia mosque in Pakistan's Islamabad A suicide attack took place at a Shia mosque (Imambara) in Islamabad, Pakistan’s capital, during Friday prayers. According to the Pakistani newspaper Times of Islamabad, 31 people have been killed and 169 injured in the attack. 5. Earthquake tremors felt in Lucknow, epicentre in Gonda Mild earthquake tremors were felt in Lucknow on Friday, causing brief panic. The quake measured 3.7 on the Richter scale with its epicentre in Gonda district. 6. Banarasi saree inspired by T20 World Cup crafted in Kashi Special Banarasi sarees featuring cricket motifs and World Cup trophies are being made in Kashi. These sarees will be gifted to Indian cricket team players. 7. RBI keeps repo rate unchanged at 5.25 percent The Reserve Bank of India has decided to maintain the repo rate at 5.25 percent. The decision was announced after the Monetary Policy Committee meeting. 8. ₹50,000 bounty gangster killed in UP encounter hours after robbery Delhi-based criminal Rihan was killed in a police encounter in Shamli, UP, within three hours of a robbery. A constable was injured, while one aide escaped. . 9. Minor climbs high-tension wire in Pratapgarh demanding marriage A 15-year-old boy climbed a high-tension power line and refused to come down for 40 minutes. He demanded police arrange his marriage before rescue. 10. Film ‘Ghooskhor Pandat’ faces backlash over title Members of the Brahmin community have objected to the film title ‘Ghooskhor Pandat’. The makers clarified that the story is fictional and not aimed at any community.

stories.title: How officers caught jewelry worth ₹33 crores in Sambhal?:20 GST officials posed as customers, guards; raided shop as stock rose
stories.summary: GST officers raided and seized unaccounted gold-silver and diamonds worth Rs 33 crores in Sambhal. The shocking story of how GST officers achieved such a big success has come to light. 15 to 20 officers from Moradabad had been coming to Sambhal in different teams for a month. They were keeping an eye on every movement of jewelry showrooms and traders. As soon as the trader dumped gold-silver jewelry, the team conducted the raid. Officers completed their raid at jeweler Himanshu Agarwal's place in Chandausi on Thursday. During the 21-hour raid, the team found 16 kg of gold, 8 quintals of silver, and about 34 carat diamonds. When the jeweler could not provide accounts for these items, the team seized them. How was it planned? A GST officer said that jewelers in Sambhal were being monitored for a month. For this, 15 to 20 officers would come from Moradabad to Sambhal in different teams. They would visit jewelry showrooms posing as customers. They would inquire about rates and gold stock. Some would pose as watchmen to monitor incoming and outgoing goods. Recently, when gold and silver rates suddenly decreased, traders started buying more jewelry. As soon as Himanshu Agarwal, owner of Montu Jewelers in Chandausi's Bada Bazar, increased his stock, the team conducted raids. Jeweler posts status amid protest After a raid lasting about 21 hours, the team collected a fine of 1 crore 20 lakh and seized goods worth 33 crores. The city's jewelers protested this action. On Thursday, shops were closed, and people took to the streets. They staged a sit-in demonstration. Education Minister Gulab Devi's daughter, Dr. Sugandha Singh, who is a block chief, reached among the traders. BJP city president Ankur Agarwal and former Minister of State for the Central Sanitation Commission Manju Diler also arrived. They talked with the traders. After assurance, the traders ended their protest. The market also opened on Friday. Discussions about this continued in the market on Friday as well. On this, businessman Himanshu Agarwal posted a message on social media - GST officials fully cooperated during the survey. We have not made any statement regarding any misconduct. Local people are deliberately spreading fear and rumors in the market, which is completely wrong. Montu Jewellers shop is located in Chandausi's Bada Bazar. It is owned by Himanshu Agarwal. Moradabad Zone's GST Additional Commissioner Grade-1 Ashok Kumar Singh said - For about a month, the team had been monitoring Montu Jeweller's activities and transactions. Based on accurate information from sources, a team of 10 officers raided Montu Jewelers around 1 PM on Wednesday. The team included 10 officials, including three female officers. The local police station was also called. This operation, which started at 1 PM on Wednesday, continued for 21 hours straight. The entire operation was conducted under camera surveillance. Could only account for half kg gold and one quintal silver: During the investigation, the jeweler could only account for 439 grams of gold and 120 kilograms of silver jewelry in stock. However, 16,638 grams of gold, 875 kilograms of silver jewelry, and 34.43 carat diamonds were found on the spot. This merchandise was not recorded in the stock register. The market value of recovered gold, silver, and diamond jewelry is estimated at around 33 crore rupees. The investigating officers have seized and taken possession of these goods during questioning. During the operation, the jewelers' employees were not allowed to go outside. Neither was any outsider allowed to enter, nor was anyone allowed to leave. 1.20 crore fine collected: After investigation, a fine of 1.20 crore rupees was imposed on the jeweler. The fine amount was deposited online. The investigation team also seized business-related loose papers and mobile phone data from the jeweler's showroom and residence, which will be investigated further. Traders closed market in protest During the raid, other traders in Bada Bazaar protested by wearing black bands. They closed the market and sat on a dharna. They raised slogans against GST officials. Thursday morning, traders also kept the market closed and continued their sit-in protest outside shops. Trader Rajesh Jindal said - Business in the jewelry market has stalled due to inflation. We are very troubled by this. This is the fifth or sixth raid by officers in Chandausi. We should not face such exploitation and should get facilities.

stories.title: 3 marriages in 6 years, was planning fourth:FIR against ‘looter groom’ in Jhansi; 3 wives allege he grabbed jewellery and cash, then threw them out
stories.summary: A shocking case of a 'robber groom' has come to light in Jhansi, where a man allegedly married three women over six years, took cash and jewellery as dowry, and then threw each of them out of the house. The matter surfaced when the three wives learned about his plans for a fourth marriage and approached the SSP office, accusing him of deceiving them one after another and grabbing their valuables. The accused also has a child with his third wife. On Thursday, the three wives complained to the police about the robber and demanded that his fourth marriage be stopped. The case is from the Babina police station area. The first wife said, I am a resident of Talbehat area of Lalitpur. She was married to Sunil, a resident of Lidhora village in Lalitpur district, in 2019. Her father is a gangman in the railways. Dowry of 8 lakh rupees cash, jewellery, etc. was given. A few months after the marriage, Sunil started demanding more dowry. Then he sent her to her parents' house for dowry.After a few days, he sent a divorce notice. Then his father came and said that she should divorce his son. The woman stated that after marrying her, her husband also married two other women. Now he is going to marry for the fourth time. I have filed a case in court. The matter is currently in court. Married second time by hiding first marriage Third wife also thrown out of the house The third wife of the accused youth, who reached the SSP office, said, I am a resident of Babina area of Jhansi. I got married to Sunil in 2023. My family gave approximately 8 lakh rupees and jewellery etc. in the wedding. After the marriage, it was revealed that Sunil had already married twice. This fact was hidden from me. A few months after the marriage, I became pregnant. He used to beat me for dowry.When I was 3 months pregnant, he assaulted me. He threw me out of the house for dowry. In this condition, my parents brought me home. I gave birth to a daughter. But my husband is not ready to keep me in his house.Now he is going to marry for the fourth time. So I called my husband's first and second wives. The three of us wives went to the SSP office on Thursday. We narrated Sunil's story of deceit. The police have assured investigation and action. Police said - Accused will be arrested soon Babina Police Station in-charge JP Pal said, The three wives had come to the police station. The third wife has filed a complaint. A case has been registered against the accused Sunil.

stories.title: UP engineer writes, 'Cheat, you changed...' and commits suicide:Hangs himself in Nainital before posting his fiancée's photo on WhatsApp status
stories.summary: A telecom engineer from Banda committed suicide in Nainital. The engineer's engagement had broken off just a few days ago. Before taking his life, he posted his fiancée's photo on WhatsApp status and wrote, "You changed, you deceiver." He was living in a rented room with his brother. On Thursday, when his brother went to work, as soon as he left, he hanged himself from the ceiling fan hook in the room. The suicide was discovered when his brother returned. The entire incident took place in Ward Number 1, Ambedkar Nagar area of Lalkuan Police Station. Bakshi ka Purwa Navy village is located in Naraini tehsil, about 60 km from the Banda district headquarters. Vinay Prajapati (28) from here lived with his cousin Raghvendra in Ambedkar Nagar of Lalkuan, Uttarakhand. Raghvendra also works in a private company there. Police broke down the door to recover the body According to Raghvendra, when he returned home from work around 6:30 PM on Thursday, the room was locked from inside. When the door didn't open even after calling out multiple times, he informed the police. Police arrived at the scene and broke down the door. Inside, they found Vinay's body hanging from the ceiling fan hook. Seeing this, Raghvendra became distraught. Police investigated. They found a mobile phone in his pocket. Upon checking the mobile, they found Vinay's WhatsApp status. In it, he had written about being betrayed by his fiancée. Fiance was refusing to talk According to brother Raghavendra, Vinay's marriage was fixed with a girl from Banda. Their engagement had taken place a few months ago. Everything was fine for some days after the engagement. But for about a month, the girl was refusing to talk to Vinay on the phone. She had also broken off the engagement. Vinay used to say that she talks to someone else. She has betrayed me. Had asked brother about food before dying According to Raghavendra, he was troubled by the broken engagement. But he had no idea that he would commit suicide. On Thursday morning, when I went to work, around 4:30 PM, while returning, Vinay called me to ask about food. At that time, there was no indication of any tragedy from Vinay's conversation. But, when I returned at 6:30 in the evening, the room was locked from inside. His body was hanging inside. Police arrived at the scene, broke open the room's lock, recovered the body, and sent it for a post-mortem after taking possession. The forensic team has also collected evidence from the spot. Police are investigating the case, keeping all aspects in mind.

stories.title: Sant Premanand Maharaj rides scooter in Vrindavan:Stops Fortuner, takes helper’s scooter rides it for 500 metres; devotees chant 'Radhe Radhe'
stories.summary: In Vrindavan, Mathura, Saint Premanand Maharaj surprised everyone when he rode a scooter himself. As usual, he had left Kelikunj Ashram in his Fortuner car for the Yamuna bank for spiritual practice. Midway, he suddenly stopped the car, got down, and pointed to the scooter-riding attendant accompanying the convoy. Asking for the scooter, he left the attendant, and the onlookers were stunned. Smiling, the attendant handed it over, and Premanand Maharaj rode off on the scooter. He rode the scooter for about 500 meters through the sandy stretch and reached the Yamuna bank. During this, his attendants ran ahead and behind him, while devotees followed, chanting 'Radhe-Radhe' and making videos. The attendants stopped people from recording. The incident took place on Thursday morning. See the pictures Going viral on social media Despite the servants' refusal, some devotees made a video of Premanandji and posted it on social media. Users are making interesting comments on it. One user wrote - ‘A saint riding a scooter, this is not a common sight.’ Another wrote - ‘It is a very interesting experience to see a saint riding a scooter.’ Know about Saint Premanand Maharaj Left home at the age of 13 Premanand Maharaj became a Radhavallabhi saint from an ascetic Upon reaching Vrindavan, Premanand Maharaj would visit Banke Bihari Ji every day. Then he became fond of Rasleela and started attending Radhavallabh's programs. He would stand there for hours. One day, a saint recited a shloka from Shri Radharas Sudhanidhi, but Maharaj could not understand it. Then one day, while circumambulating Vrindavan, he heard a sakhi singing a shloka. Hearing it, Maharaj paused. The shloka resonated so much with him that he broke his sannyasa dharma and went to that sakhi. He asked her for the meaning of the shloka. The sakhi said - To understand its meaning, it is necessary to be a Radhavallabhi. Thus, Maharaj became a Radhavallabhi.

stories.title: Notice issued to BJP MLA for holding Minister Swatantra hostage:UP BJP President seeks response in 7 days; convoy halted after heated exchange
stories.summary: A notice has been issued against the BJP MLA who held UP's Jal Shakti Cabinet Minister Swatantra Dev Singh hostage. UP BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary has sought a response from Brajbhushan alias Guddu Rajput within 7 days regarding the matter. However, the MLA says that he has not received the notice yet. On January 30, there was a confrontation between the BJP MLA and Minister Swatantra Dev Singh in Mahoba district. The MLA stopped the minister's convoy along with more than 100 village heads. He alleged that roads have been dug up and left unfinished. Work is not being done. After this, there was a heated argument between the minister and the MLA. The commotion calmed down after about 30 minutes. What was the conversation between the minister and MLA... Minister: Wherever there is a complaint, take me there. I will go to that village myself. I will leave my programs and go. Let's go... MLA: One minute-one minute...there are 40 to 50 villages. Minister: I will visit 40 villages. I will go to check all the places. Officers are with me. I will inspect everywhere. If officers are negligent, I will suspend them. MLA: Brother, roads are dug up. Paths are dug up. Brother... Minister: Even if roads remain dug up, I will still suspend the officers. I am ready to visit the villages, come along with me... After minister's departure, MLA held meeting and said - will stop CM too if needed After confronting the minister, MLA Brijbhushan Rajput called a meeting on February 3. In this, Rajput had said - if needed, we will stop the Chief Minister too. Taking someone hostage is not a big deal for me. I had gone to Jhansi and taken the Union Minister Pradeep Jain Aditya hostage in his own house, when I wasn't even an MLA. When there was a Congress government, we used to make officers who didn't work wear bangles and petticoats. This is not my personal issue, but rather one connected to the public and development. I am putting my point across on the street, so why should anyone have objections to this? With all your blessings, we stopped the minister. This is about the public and development. Why should I discuss this matter in a room? Why can't I do it on the street? If I expressed my views on the street, why are some people having problems with it? I'm not demanding any contracts, leases, or promotions. Rather, I'm only raising issues of the region. In such circumstances, it is not right to declare me wrong.

stories.title: SIR date extended by 1 month in UP:Names can now be added till March 6; final list to be released on April 10
stories.summary: The Election Commission has extended the deadline for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh, giving voters an additional month to file claims and objections. As per the revised schedule, applications can now be submitted till March 6, while the final voter list will be published on April 10. The information was shared by Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa during a press conference at Lok Bhavan in Lucknow. Rinwa said the SIR process in Uttar Pradesh began on October 27. Voter enumeration was carried out from November 4 to January 6. This was followed by the claims and objections period from January 6 to February 6, during which a large number of applications were received. According to official data, 82,684 applications were filed for deletion of names through Form 7, while around 37.8 lakh applications were received for addition of names using Form 6. Migrant voters can apply through Form 6A, and so far, 1,076 migrant voters have submitted applications. The Election Department said the number of Form 6 applications continues to rise. Around 1.40 crore voters had their names in the draft list but were not mapped, while 2.22 crore voters completed mapping, but discrepancies were found. Notices are being issued in all such cases. In total, notices are to be sent to 3.26 crore voters. So far, 2.37 crore notices have been issued, and 86.27 lakh have already been delivered. Hearings have been completed in nearly 30 lakh cases. In view of this, the deadline for filing claims and objections has been extended from February 6 to March 6. Voters can apply for inclusion, deletion, or correction of details till then. The final electoral roll under the SIR process will be released on April 10. To assist voters, Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will be available at polling booths on all working days from 10 am to 12 noon. Rinwa assured that no eligible voter’s name will be deleted without proper verification. Every objection will be examined before a decision is taken. He noted that many women and young voters are still missing from the voter list and urged citizens to come forward. He also advised voters to ensure that the spelling of their names in Hindi and English matches their Aadhaar card, so that any future online corrections can be made easily from home.

stories.title: 15-year-old boy climbs high-tension wire in Pratapgarh:Demands to arrange his marriage with his minor girlfriend; police rescue him after 40 minutes
stories.summary: A 15-year-old boy climbed a high-tension power line in Uttar Pradesh’s Pratapgarh district on Thursday, demanding that police arrange his marriage to his minor girlfriend before he would come down. The teenager remained suspended at a height of around 35 feet for nearly 40 minutes before being rescued by police. A video of the incident has surfaced. The incident takes place in the Devsara police station area. According to locals, the boy climbed an 11,000-volt power line and held on to the wire, triggering panic in the village. More than 50 people gathered at the spot after noticing him hanging from the line. When villagers asked him to come down, the boy refused. Police were informed, and on seeing the station house officer arrive, the minor reportedly said he would not come down unless his marriage to his girlfriend was arranged. Police persuaded the boy by assuring him that his demand would be addressed. A ladder was arranged, and he was brought down safely. As soon as he came down, the teenager broke down and started crying. The entire episode lasts around 40 minutes. Police later take the boy to the police station, counsel him and hand him over to his family. At the time of the incident, power supply to the 11,000-volt line is already switched off due to maintenance work, preventing a major accident. Only son of the family, affair was going on for 1 year The incident occurs in Bhaupur village, located about 60 kilometres from the district headquarters. Villagers say the boy is the only son of his parents and had dropped out of studies after completing high school. He has been in a relationship for about a year with a 13-year-old girl from the Patti area. Both belong to the Patel community. Became stressed after being beaten by girl's family Villagers say the boy had gone to meet the girl at her village two to three months ago, where her family members caught and allegedly assaulted him. The matter reached the police, but a compromise was later reached between the two families, and the complaint was withdrawn. Despite this, the two continued to talk on mobile phones. Angered by this, the boy’s family reportedly took away his phone, after which he remained under stress. When no one had courage to get minor down, police was called Around 2 pm on Thursday, villagers spot the boy hanging from the power line about 500 metres from his house. Fearing electrocution, no one dares to climb the pole. Some villagers inform the power sub-station, while police and electricity department officials reach the spot. When police ask him to come down, the boy insists that he will do so only after marrying his girlfriend. After prolonged persuasion, the station house officer assures him that the matter will be addressed, following which he agrees to come down. Police bring him down safely at around 2.40 pm using a ladder, after which villagers heave a sigh of relief. Police rescued minor using ladder Aspur Devsara Station In-charge Vijayendra Singh said- Both the boy and girl are minors. Considering the sensitive nature of the case, the family members were called, counseled and the boy was handed over to them.

stories.title: BJP minister targets Rahul with ‘fake Gandhi’ tag:9 hoardings put up across Rae Bareli; Congress alleges narrow political thinking
stories.summary: Posters targeting Congress leader Rahul Gandhi have been put up at nine locations in Rae Bareli, his parliamentary constituency, by Uttar Pradesh minister Dinesh Pratap Singh. The hoardings describe Rahul Gandhi as a “fake Gandhi” and pose the question: “Who is the traitor — real Sardar Ravneet Singh Bittu or fake Gandhi Rahul Gandhi?” The hoardings were installed early Friday morning at around 4.45 am. The move has triggered a sharp reaction from the Congress, which has termed it an example of a “petty mindset”. UP Congress Committee secretary Atul Singh told Dainik Bhaskar that the act reflects a narrow mentality. He said Rahul Gandhi is fighting both the Centre and the Uttar Pradesh government for public interest, from Parliament to the streets, and claimed the BJP would face defeat in the 2027 Assembly elections. What's in the hoarding... The hoardings carry a photograph of minister Dinesh Pratap Singh along with a large image of Bharat Mata. On the left side of the image, the text reads: “Real Sardar Ravneet Singh Bittu — betrayal with Congress; the god-like people of the entire country have abandoned Congress (does RG call him a traitor?).” On the right side, Rahul Gandhi is described as “fake Gandhi”, followed by a list accusing him of betrayal of India, Indians, Indian culture and values, Lord Ram, Sardar Patel, Subhas Chandra Bose, Dr APJ Abdul Kalam, Feroze Gandhi, Maneka Gandhi, and extending up to the Vadra family, described as businessmen from Moradabad district of Uttar Pradesh. The hoardings also mention Union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu and have been installed at nine locations across the city. Where the hoardings are installed The hoardings have been put up at Nirala Nagar, Gandhi Nagar, Ekta Vihar Colony, Saras Hotel, Degree College Chauraha, Ratapur Chauraha and Tripula on the national highway, with one hoarding at each location. Two hoardings have been installed at Didoli. Now know where the traitor statement originated from The controversy stems from an exchange between Rahul Gandhi and Ravneet Singh Bittu outside Parliament earlier this week. On Wednesday, February 4, Rahul Gandhi referred to Bittu as a “traitor” during a protest outside Parliament at Makar Dwar in Delhi. When Bittu approached during the protest, Rahul Gandhi said, “My traitor friend is coming,” and extended his hand for a handshake. Bittu refused to shake hands. Bittu told Rahul Gandhi that he was not working in the national interest and accused him of being an enemy of the country. This led to a heated exchange between the two leaders. Rahul Gandhi responded by saying, “Don’t worry, my traitor friend, you will return.” At the time, Ludhiana MP Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa and Amritsar MP Gurjeet Aujla were also present. Bittu later alleged that there was an attempt to assault him during the confrontation. BJP leader Manjinder Singh Sirsa said a Sardar cannot be a traitor and alleged that the real traitors are members of the Gandhi family, claiming they had deployed tanks and cannons at the Golden Temple. PM had said - Rahul stole Mahatma Gandhi's surname On February 5, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while replying to the Motion of Thanks on the President’s Address in the Rajya Sabha, made several allegations against the Congress. Without naming Rahul Gandhi, the Prime Minister accused him and his family of having “stolen” Mahatma Gandhi’s surname. He also claimed that Jawaharlal Nehru and Indira Gandhi viewed the people of the country as a problem. Dinesh had lost election to Rahul, targeting him since then Dinesh Pratap Singh currently holds independent charge as Minister of State for Horticulture, Agricultural Marketing, Agriculture, Foreign Trade and Agricultural Exports in the Uttar Pradesh government. He contested the 2024 Lok Sabha election from Rae Bareli against Rahul Gandhi. Rahul Gandhi won the seat by a margin of 3,90,030 votes. He secured 6,87,649 votes, while Dinesh Pratap Singh received 2,97,619 votes. After his defeat, Dinesh Pratap Singh said he would work for the nearly three lakh voters who supported him, and added that those who voted for Rahul Gandhi should now look to him to fulfil his responsibilities.

stories.title: T-20 World Cup Banarasi Saree being made in Kashi:Indian players to receive it as gift, design features all World Cup trophies, bats and stumps
stories.summary: 'From childhood until today, I have only watched cricket on TV. The joy I felt in my heart seeing India's victory. I always felt that. Never watched a match in the stadium but the love for cricket is perhaps now reflecting in my profession.' That's why I talked to Kashyam Foundation's trustee Sarvesh Srivastava about the T-20 Cricket World Cup and started working on a design. Which is now being woven on a Banarasi brocade saree. All 5 World Cups of India are being woven into it.' This is what Kashyam Foundation's designer Lakshmi Vishwakarma has to say. Under the supervision of Sarvesh Srivastava, Lakshmi prepared the design of this World Cup special saree in 3 months. Work is now being done on it. In Kashyam Foundation's factory in Lohta area, Bahadur and his associates are preparing it on brocade handloom. Work is done on this saree for 8 hours daily. World cup begins from tomorrow T-20 World Cup-2026 warm-up matches have begun. In this context, Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Sarvesh Srivastava of Kashyam Foundation and designer Lakshmi Vishwakarma, who designed this Banarasi saree for T-20 World Cup-2026 and was honored with Resham Ratna Award-2026. Information was gathered about the concept and creation of this saree. Read the report... See three pictures of T-20 World Cup 2026 special Banarasi saree... First, know about the specialty of cricket saree and the materials used in it... Banarasi saree dedicated to Indian cricket There are five handlooms installed in the workshop of Kashyam Foundation located in Lohta area, 8 KM from Varanasi district headquarters, where Bahadur and his associates are busy making brocade cotton sarees on one handloom. Nearby, foundation's Sarvesh Srivastava and zari master are sitting. Sarvesh had previously also made a World Cup saree during Cricket World Cup-2023. It features designs of World Cup wins Sarvesh said, “Keeping the T-20 World Cup in mind, our designer has prepared a design which is dedicated to Indian cricket. It features designs of cups from 1983 to the Women's World Cup winning Indian team. Along with this, the picture of World Cup-2026 is being made on its border. So that India hits a sixer in the World Cup this year.” Design of all World Cup trophies, bats and stumps Sarvesh said - On this special Banarasi saree, we have engraved the trophies of the 1983 World Cup, 2007 T-20 World Cup, 2011 World Cup, 2024 T-20 World Cup and Women's World Cup 2025 won by Team India. Additionally, bat-stumps, and T-20 World Cup images have been engraved on the border. This is being made by weaver Bahadur from Lohta and his associates. Saree being made with zari and silk Sarvesh Srivastava said - This saree is being made on a brocade handloom. Zari work is being done on silk. One saree will cost between ₹25,000 to ₹30,000. Two artisans working 8 hours daily will weave and complete it in 20 to 25 days. Right now we are making presentation type sarees. Going forward we will make 25 sarees. Which will be given to every India player and staff. Now know where designer Lakshmi Vishwakarma got the theme from... Cricket passion since childhood Lakshmi Vishwakarma is a designer at Kashyam Foundation and works here as a hobby. Recently Lakshmi was honored with the Reshma Ratna Award for her sarees. Lakshmi said- I have been passionate about watching cricket since childhood. While walking on the road, if cricket was on, I would stop and watch a few overs. Team India was seen lifting the World Cup in 2007, 2011, 2024, and 2025 Women's. Besides that, heard about the glorious 1983 World Cup through father's words. I always want to see the team winning in cricket and feel happy when seeing the team win matches. Carved happiness of heart into design Lakshmi said - I've been reading cricket news daily. Team India is also a strong contender for the T-20 World Cup. In this context, a design started floating in my mind. I began working on it and gradually prepared its draft and showed it to Sarvesh ji. When he saw it, he made some changes and then after that, the final draft was prepared in 3 months. Craftsmen are now working on it and the first piece is being prepared. Praying for Team India to win the World Cup Lakshmi explained - This is our prayer to Baba Vishwanath that Team India wins the World Cup this time too so that our saree also progresses and brings glory to the country. Team India is currently the strongest because they are the defending champions. So our saree is dedicated to those players. We want to gift this saree to them.

stories.title: Delhi criminal killed within 3 hours of robbery in UP:₹50,000 bounty holder, 90 cases; constable injured and aide escapes, 19th encounter in 4 months
stories.summary: A Delhi-based gangster, Rihan, with a ₹50,000 bounty on his head, was killed in an encounter in Shamli, Uttar Pradesh. Three hours before the shootout, Rihan and his accomplice robbed a young man of cash and a mobile phone. Following the incident, the police launched a widespread checking operation across the district. Around 12:30 a.m., both gangsters were surrounded. Police asked them to surrender, but they opened fire. Constable Sumit was hit in the shooting. The police then returned fire, during which Rihan was shot and fell to the ground. His accomplice managed to escape under the cover of darkness. After the encounter, Rihan was taken to a hospital, where he was declared dead during treatment. He was a resident of Zakir Nagar, New Okhla, Delhi, and had 90 cases registered against him. Police recovered a “Made in Italy” pistol, a local pistol, eight live cartridges, and a gold ring from him. The encounter took place near the Yamuna Canal in the Kotwali area. Criminal opened fire when stopped by police SP NP Singh said that at around 9 p.m. on Thursday in the Babri area, Rihan and his accomplice robbed Rahul, a resident of Fatehpur, of cash and a mobile phone while he was riding his bike. The gangsters then fled. Rahul managed to alert the police, which put the entire district on high alert and began checking operations. At 12:30 a.m., Kotwali and Adarsh Mandi police were searching near the eastern Yamuna Canal when they spotted the two on a bike. Police attempted to stop them, but they tried to flee by making a U-turn. During the pursuit, the gangsters opened fire, injuring Constable Sumit. Police returned fire immediately. Encounter lasted for 35 minutes Criminal Rihan was injured by gunshot, while his accomplice took advantage of the darkness and fled. Police admitted the constable and the criminal to the district hospital, where doctors declared the criminal dead. The encounter between police and criminals lasted for about 30 to 35 minutes. Rehan carried out chain snatching incidents targeting women in Delhi, UP and Haryana. Rehan had the most cases against him with 49 cases in Delhi and 28 cases registered in Ghaziabad. Cases of robbery, theft and deadly attacks were also registered in Shamli, Baghpat, Hapur and Bulandshahr. CM Yogi’s statement on police action Earlier, CM Yogi Adityanath, during the inauguration of the UP Pharma Conclave 1.0 on Tuesday, said that from 2012 to 2017, over 900 riots occurred in UP. “During such times, I was entrusted with responsibility. We decided on zero tolerance. People often ask why police shoot. If police do not fire, what should they face? If criminals are free to fire guns, we have given police guns too,” he said. High Court had said - UP Police conducting encounters for praise and promotion Last week, the Allahabad High Court expressed strong displeasure over UP Police’s ‘half encounters,’ stating that officers are firing unnecessarily for praise, early promotions, and social media acclaim. The court issued six-point guidelines, warning that if Supreme Court directives are not followed, the SP, SSP, and Police Commissioner could be held personally liable. 259 criminals killed in encounters in 8 years According to the state government, between March 2017 and October 2025, UP Police killed 259 criminals in encounters. During this period, over 15,000 police encounters were conducted, 31,000+ criminals were arrested, and more than 10,000 were shot at.

stories.title: Earthquake tremors felt in Lucknow:Epicentre traced to Gonda, quake measured 3.7 magnitude on Richter scale; residents report mild shaking
stories.summary: Light tremors of an earthquake were felt in Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh, on Friday. People were startled for a few moments as the earth suddenly shook, and in many areas, people came out of their homes and offices. The epicenter of the earthquake is reported to be in Gonda district, with its intensity measured at 3.7 on the Richter scale. Tremors felt around 7 AM Amidst their normal morning routine, people in many parts of Lucknow felt a slight tremor around 7 AM. The sensation of the earth shaking lasted for a few seconds, although the tremors were not strong. Those living in tall buildings felt it more clearly. Gonda was the epicenter of the earthquake According to the information received, the epicenter of the earthquake was located in Gonda district. The waves emanating from there affected surrounding districts, including Lucknow. Due to the low intensity of the earthquake, no major damage has been reported. No news of loss of life or property According to administrative sources, no loss of life or property or damage to any building has been reported from anywhere so far. The district administration and disaster management department are keeping an eye on the situation. Panic among people, but situation normal After the earthquake tremors, there was an atmosphere of panic among people for some time, but soon the situation returned to normal. According to experts, an earthquake of 3.7 magnitude falls into the normal category and usually does not pose a risk of major damage, yet caution has been advised. News is being continuously updated

stories.title: Efforts on to make Kashi Vishwanath's darshan smoother this year:Baba's door to remain open for 26 hours without a break, special arrangement for upcoming Mahashivratri
stories.summary: This time devotees will not be disappointed for darshan on Mahashivratri in Kashi as Vishwanath Temple administration has decided to keep the doors continuously open on Shivratri considering the expected crowd of devotees. The temple administration estimates that the number of devotees in Kashi Vishwanath Temple this time could be more than ten lakhs. In view of this, the temple administration has banned all types of convenient darshan and VIP protocol arrangements. Continuous darshan for 26 hours Maha Shivratri is the biggest day for Lord Shiv devotees in Kashi, the city of Baba Vishwanath, which devotees wait for throughout the year. This time Maha Shivratri falls on February 15. The temple administration has decided that the Kashi Vishwanath temple will remain open continuously for 26 hours on this Shivratri. Baba's doors will remain open until 6 AM the next day On February 15, after the Mangala Aarti at 4 AM, Baba's doors will be opened for general devotees. Baba's doors will remain open until 6 AM the next day, February 16. Devotees can offer water to Baba Vishwanath along with having a glimpse. Additionally, touch and easy darshan have been restricted from February 14 to February 17. Ban on easy darshan, special aarti in four phases Under another major change, considering the potential crowd of devotees, the temple administration has banned easy darshan with tickets and darshan under VVIP protocol on Mahashivratri. The purpose is to ensure that devotees coming from India and abroad do not face any difficulties in darshan and worship on Mahashivratri. 4-phase aarti of Kashi Vishwanath will also be special Additionally, this time the four-phase aarti of Kashi Vishwanath will also be special. After Mangla Aarti and Bhog Aarti, special aartis will be performed in four different phases instead of Saptarishi Aarti and Shayan Aarti. Moreover, the temple administration will also display tableaux related to Lord Shiva's life for common devotees. Answers to some important questions from devotees coming to Kashi on Mahashivratri What are the entry and exit arrangements at Kashi Vishwanath Temple? Kashi Vishwanath Temple Trust has arranged that people will exit from the same gate through which they enter for darshan. Gate 1. Ganga Gate - People who take a bath in the Ganges River will reach through this gate. Gate 2. Dhundiraj Ganesh Gate - People queuing from Dashashwamedh Ghat side will get darshan through this gate. Gate 3. Saraswati Gate - Devotees coming through Godaulia via Bans Phatak will reach the temple through this gate. Gate 4. Nandi Gate - Devotees coming from Maidagin and Godaulia will have darshan through this gate. When will Baba Vishwanath's wedding ceremony be held? The wedding rituals of Baba will be performed in the temple premises from 8 hours on the night of February 15. Baba's shringar puja will be performed. Can we offer prasad in the temple? No, prasad cannot be offered in the temple. There will be jhanki darshan. People can offer water, milk, flowers to the Shivling through a long tray from outside the sanctum sanctorum. Prasad is available inside the Kashi Vishwanath temple which devotees can take home. Otherwise, there are more than 500 shops outside the temple. What items are not allowed inside the temple? Answer: Before entering the temple, items like mobile phones, shoes, pens, paan-masala must be left outside. Checking happens at the gate itself. You can only take baskets containing prasad, milk, Ganga water, flowers etc. Cash can be kept for offerings. How do I reach Kashi Vishwanath Dham from Babatpur Airport and Station? After exiting the airport terminal and station, you will reach Beniyabag intersection by car or auto. There is a police barrier here, where you'll need to park your car. After this, walk 1.5 km to reach Godowlia intersection. From here, the lines for Kashi Vishwanath Dham begin. How can I take a bath in the Ganges? After reaching Godowlia, you can walk about 500 meters to Dashashwamedh Ghat for a holy dip in the Ganges. Additionally, you can also take a bath at Assi Ghat, Tulsi Ghat, Kedar Ghat, and Bhadaini Ghat.

stories.title: Rinku Singh's Facebook account hacked, FIR lodged in Aligarh:Hackers changed ID, monetisation money also stolen
stories.summary: Indian cricketer Rinku Singh has fallen victim to cyber fraud after his official Facebook account was hacked. The hackers not only took control of the account but also diverted its monetisation earnings to their own account. A case has now been registered at the cybercrime police station following a complaint filed by Rinku’s brother, Sonu Singh. According to the complaint, Rinku was busy with international cricket commitments and preparations for the T20 World Cup, due to which he could not closely monitor his social media accounts. The issue came to light on February 4, when Rinku tried to log into his Facebook account and found that the password was no longer working. After repeated failed login attempts, Rinku informed his brother, who immediately approached the authorities. Following directions from the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), a formal case was registered and an investigation has begun. As investigations continue into the cyber fraud case, fans hope that Rinku’s account will be restored soon and justice will be served. How was the Facebook account hacked? Rinku Singh’s brother Sonu Singh, a resident of Ozone City Gold State, revealed that Rinku is currently in Mumbai after returning from a T20 World Cup warm-up match against South Africa. When Rinku attempted to access his Facebook account on February 4, he realised that the registered email ID had been changed. Despite not using the account, photos and videos were being uploaded, which raised suspicion. Earlier, the account was linked to the email ID (rinkukumar344.8.7), but it is now being operated using another email ID, (commercial.rinkukumar). This confirmed that the account had been taken over by hackers. The Facebook page has around 1.6 million followers and is monetised, generating significant income. Sonu stated that this income is now being transferred directly to the hackers’ account. Police action and account recovery efforts Cyber Crime Station Inspector Ramendra Shukla confirmed that a case has been registered against unknown persons. SSP Neeraj Kumar Jadaun said the cyber team has been instructed to trace the hackers, stop further financial loss, and recover the account as soon as possible. Police officials have assured the family that strict action will be taken and digital evidence is being examined. Engagement With MP Priya Saroj Apart from the cyber fraud case, Rinku Singh has also been in the news for his personal life. He got engaged to Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj on June 8 last year at a grand ring ceremony in Lucknow. The event was attended by several high-profile leaders, including Akhilesh Yadav, Dimple Yadav, and Jaya Bachchan. The wedding was initially planned for November 18 in Kashi but was postponed due to Rinku’s packed cricket schedule, including IPL and the T20 World Cup. A new date has not yet been finalised. A Journey from struggle to national stardom Rinku Singh’s rise to fame is a story of hard work and struggle. Coming from a modest background, his father worked as a gas cylinder deliveryman. Rinku and his brothers also helped deliver cylinders to support the family. Despite financial hardships, Rinku continued playing cricket with borrowed equipment and limited resources. His life changed after his iconic five sixes in IPL 2023 for Kolkata Knight Riders, which made him a household name.

stories.title: FIR filed on Manoj Bajpayee’s film ‘Ghooskhor Pandat':UP police acts on Yogi’s orders; Falahari writes to Modi, Mayawati demands ban on film
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, protests have erupted over the title of Manoj Bajpayee’s film Ghooskhor Pandat. An FIR has been registered against the film’s director in Lucknow. The complaint was filed by Inspector Vikram Singh at Hazratganj Kotwali on the Chief Minister’s instructions. Police say the film’s title and storyline incorrectly portray a particular caste and community, especially the Brahmin society, which could stir discontent and disturb law and order. Meanwhile, in Mathura, Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Sangharsh Nyas president Dinesh Falahari Maharaj has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding an immediate ban on the film. He stated that the title unfairly portrays the community as ‘corrupt’, which is highly objectionable. Saints from Prayagraj have also voiced strong opposition. Shringerverpur Peethadheeshwar Jagadguru Ramanujacharya Swami Narayanacharya Shandilya Ji Maharaj said Bollywood exhibits a double standard, making films that repeatedly target specific groups, thereby creating societal divisions. Swami Brahmasram Maharaj, president of the Akhil Bharatiya Dandi Sanyasi Parishad, added that films like Ghooskhor Pandat harm Sanatan traditions and undermine mutual brotherhood. He too has demanded the film be banned immediately.

stories.title: Questions mount over deaths of three sisters:Father cites Korean influence, demands ban; investigation continues on multiple angles
stories.summary: On the night of 3 February, three sisters died after falling from a high-rise apartment in Ghaziabad. While an eight-page suicide note points to their deep immersion in Korean culture, several contradictions in the father’s statements and accounts from residents have raised serious questions. Initially, the father, Chetan Kumar, told police that his daughters died by suicide while completing the final task of a Korean online game. Later, he changed his version, saying the girls were addicted to Korean movies and social media reels. He claimed he had confiscated their mobile phones and warned them that if their behaviour did not improve, he would get them married. Chetan’s first wife, Sujata, told police that the girls had locked the room from inside and could not be saved. However, after this statement, both of Chetan’s wives locked themselves inside the flat and were unavailable for further questioning. Police are now examining Chetan’s statements, call detail records of both wives, bank transactions and forensic evidence from inside the flat. As the suicide narrative unfolds, multiple unanswered questions have emerged, which investigators are trying to resolve. To get closer to the truth behind the deaths of the three sisters, the Dainik Bhaskar team spoke to residents of Bharat City’s B-1 Tower, where the family lived in Flat No. 907. Several residents refused to speak on camera but raised significant doubts about the incident. Rajendra said - The girls were fighting, they might have been pushed Rajendra Sharma (75), a resident of the society, appeared disturbed by the deaths. He said that around 2 am on 3 February, his grandson was crying, so he stepped outside to calm him and walked around the ground floor. He said he heard shouting and sounds of children arguing. After some time, the noise stopped. About two to three minutes later, he heard the sound of someone falling. A few seconds later, he heard two more bodies hitting the ground in quick succession. He rushed to the spot and saw three girls lying on the ground, bleeding. By then, several neighbours had gathered. When asked about the sounds of argument, Rajendra said it felt like someone was trying to save someone else. He said it was possible that one girl slipped and the others fell while trying to save her. He also said it was possible they were pushed, as the distance between where the bodies landed was quite large. Why was the mother cursing her husband over the daughters' deaths? A woman from the society said that after news of the incident spread, residents rushed downstairs. She said she was going down in the lift when Chetan and his wife Sujata entered the lift as well. According to her, the couple were arguing, and Sujata was loudly abusing Chetan, repeatedly using foul language. Chetan remained silent. As soon as the lift doors opened, he rushed towards the spot where the bodies were lying. The woman said that even after seeing the bodies on the ground with blood scattered around, Sujata continued abusing her husband. She questioned how a mother could behave that way when the bodies of her three daughters were lying in front of her. People asked - The daughters died, then why is the father wearing a mask While talking to the residents of B-1 tower in the society, a person raised questions. He said - Chetan kept wearing a mask the whole time, someone whose 3 daughters have died is hiding his face. Think about it, when a child even gets a fever, parents become worried and don't even pay attention to what they're wearing. Even after such a big incident here, he remembered to wear a mask. The question is also why is he keeping himself separate from everyone? His face wasn't showing any signs of pain. Both mothers haven't appeared even 48 hours after death Neighbours said that after the girls fell from the balcony, both wives were seen briefly in the society, along with Chetan’s sister Tina. After that, the flat remained locked. The household includes Chetan, his two wives, his sister, a seven-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter. When the Additional Police Commissioner tried to speak to both wives, they locked the door from inside. Not only the father, but both mothers also avoided facing people. On the evening of 5 February, some female relatives arrived at the flat and stood outside for 35 minutes. Chetan eventually opened the door, still wearing a mask, let them inside and immediately shut the door again without speaking to anyone. Why did the daughters only put their father's photo on the floor? A woman from a 10th-floor flat said the girls had cut out small photographs and pasted them on the floor of their room. She questioned why only the father’s photos were used and none of the mothers’. She said the three girls had two mothers, yet not a single photo of either mother was found. She said this raised questions about the girls’ emotional state and family dynamics. Why was 'sorry' written only for Papa in the diary? A resident from the 11th floor said that the diary recovered as a suicide note contained an apology addressed only to the father. He questioned why there was no mention of the mother, especially since daughters usually share their feelings with their mothers. He said the girls were very young, and something significant must have been troubling them for them to exclude their mothers entirely. Woman said - The real cause of children's death should come to light Another woman resident, Isha Tyagi, said people should not jump to conclusions about Korean culture, mobile addiction or games. She said the real cause of death must come out. She said what was most shocking was that three children died together. She said it might be understandable if one child was disturbed, but three siblings dying together pointed to something far more serious. Father says - Korean videos should be banned in India The mystery surrounding the suicide of the three sisters continues to deepen. Attempts were made to speak to the girls’ father, but he refused to open the door and responded only from behind the mesh gate. The father said the children had created Korean-style identities and had even changed their names. He demanded that the government ban Korean dramas and videos, claiming such content is making children addicted. “My three children are gone. My life is gone,” he said, adding that such content should be stopped so that no other child loses their life. It may be noted that three minor sisters — Nishika (16), Prachi (14) and Pakhi (12) — died by suicide after jumping from the balcony around 2 am on 3 February. In their eight-page suicide note, the girls wrote, “Sorry Papa, I am really sorry.” Their last rites were performed in Delhi on 5 February. After the cremation, the father, Chetan, returned to his flat in Ghaziabad. Family has been living in rented flat for three years Chetan Kumar does online share trading. He has been living in a rented flat in Bharat Society for the past 3 years with his 2 wives Sujata and Hina and 5 children. Among the girls who committed suicide, Nishika was the daughter of Chetan's first wife Sujata, while Prachi and Pakhi were daughters of second wife Hina. When Chetan's first wife Sujata could not conceive for many years, he married Sujata's sister Hina (his sister-in-law). Just a few months after this, Sujata gave birth to Nishika. Second wife Hina gave birth to Prachi, Pakhi and another daughter. Later, the first wife had a son Lavish (7), who is mentally challenged and cannot speak. Police investigation continues DCP Says - Investigating All Angles DCP Trans Hindon Nimish Patil - All angles are being examined. The family’s silence, the mothers not coming forward and several links in the sequence of events are under investigation. Statements are being recorded, and new facts are likely to emerge soon ..
